  One fixed request body cannot serve a list this wide. `gpt-4o`, `gpt-4.1` and `gpt-3.5-turbo` reject `reasoning_effort` outright and OpenAI rejects an unknown parameter rather than ignoring it, while newer reasoning models reject it only alongside function tools and name the value to use instead — so `callOpenAIFormat` reads the remedy out of the rejection and remembers it per model for the session, rather than predicting support from a table that would go stale in the same way. `964cc540` added a fallback for servers whose wording matches no remedy pattern (Ollama's, for one): an unexplained 400 drops that one genuinely optional field and retries once. Pricing follows the same logic — `MODEL_PRICES` covers a handful of models against a dropdown now offering dozens, so `pricesFor` falls through to OpenRouter's public unauthenticated pricing endpoint for the same upstream models, with the built-in table still winning where it has an entry because it carries the promo logic; ids are reconciled by stripping snapshot dates and rewriting version separators, and an unpriced model reports tokens and no dollar figure rather than a fabricated zero. Usage attribution stopped being prefix-based — an OpenAI key also reaches `o3`, `o4-mini` and `chat-latest`, and an OpenRouter key reaches 300-odd models across every vendor — so `usageModelPrefixes` became `usageModelMatch` predicates that partition the id space, and `formatUsageReport` accepts either form.

- **Voice Model** — Sitrec → Settings → *Voice Model*, mirrored into the Assistant header (`964cc540`; `getVoiceModels()`, `DEFAULT_VOICE_MODEL`; i18n `custom.settings.voiceModel`). The realtime family is a second list, not more entries in the first: those models serve `/v1/realtime` over WebRTC and cannot be called through chat completions, so offering them for typed chat would produce an error the user could not act on. Chat and voice models come from the same `/v1/models` call and are told apart by a tag. The dropdown sits under *AI Model* and mirrors into the Assistant header, where the microphone that uses it is two icons away. The default stays `gpt-realtime-2` because it is the one with a verified price, and OpenRouter carries no realtime models to fall back on.

- **Add 3D Object** — right-click the ground → *Add 3D Object*, above *Create Track with Object* (`43fe3530`; `addFixedObject` in `src/CustomManagerMenus.js`; i18n `addFixedObject`). Places a grey 5 m sphere that does not move. A `CNode3DObject` has no position of its own and a `TrackPosition` controller asks a track every frame, but a thing standing on the ground has no journey to describe, and a synthetic spline track for it would mean an entry in Contents, a spline editor and keyframes that exist only to say "here, always". So it gets a `CNodePositionLLA` instead — one lat/lon/alt satisfying the same interface, placed at ground MSL to match the other ground-menu placements. Nothing is suppressed to hide it: it is simply never registered with `TrackManager` (which is what creates the Contents folder and what the track pickers enumerate) and is constructed with no `gui`, so it adds no controls anywhere. Dragging needed no new wiring — `resolveMoveTarget()` already classifies a movable root by behaviour (`setLLA` + `_LLA` + `ecef`) rather than by class. No `ObjectTilt` controller is added: that orients a model along its direction of travel, which a stationary object has none of. Creating one opens its edit menu, which is also what makes it draggable without holding Option, since `CObjectMoveWidget` attaches to whatever `getEditingObjectNode()` returns.

- **Focus While Editing** — the object edit menu, immediately after *Visible* (`43fe3530`; `focusWhileEditing` on `CNode3DObject`, applied by `updateEditFocus()` in `src/CObjectMoveWidget.js`). While the object's edit menu is open, every 3D view's camera looks at the object and orbits about it — what View → Focus Track does, for as long as you are editing. Implemented by assigning the view's `focusTrackName`, because a `CNode3DObject` answers `p()` like any track, so it inherits the orbit-about-target behaviour and the per-frame follow rather than steering cameras by hand. Suspended while dragging, since focus pins the orbit centre to the object and the camera would otherwise swing to chase the thing the pointer is moving; restored on drop, when you most want to see where it landed. The view's previous focus is remembered and put back rather than replaced with "default". Deliberately not serialised — it describes how you are working, not the object.

- **Switch an API key off without deleting it** — Sitrec → Settings → *API Keys…* (`5b0b1cb9`; `isProviderEnabled()` / `setProviderEnabled()` / `getKeyRaw()` in `src/BYOKKeyStore.js`). Gated in `BYOKKeyStore`, the one module every consumer already goes through, so terrain, live feeds, voice and the model dropdown honour it with no changes of their own: `getKey`/`getCachedKey` report nothing for a disabled provider and `getAllProviders` (hence `Globals.hasByokKeys`) excludes it. `getKeyRaw` ignores the flag and exists for the dialog alone, which must still show "Set" for a key that is switched off. Only the **disabled** ids are stored, so absence means enabled and a provider added later defaults on; they live under `sitrecByokDisabled`, a key that deliberately avoids the `byok_` credential prefix, and an unreadable store means "nothing disabled".

### Improvements

- **Small talk is answered locally, instantly and free** (`bedb4451`; `SMALL_TALK` / `SMALL_TALK_BY_PHRASE` / `normalizeSmallTalk` in `src/CClientNLU.js`). Greetings, thanks and filler carry no request, so answering them with a model call is pure waste — a turn's tokens on a hosted provider, and up to three minutes of prompt prefill on a local one. **296 phrases across eight categories** (`small_talk_greeting`, `_thanks`, `_farewell`, `_ack`, `_waiting`, `_nevermind`, `_ping`, `_please`) are now answered without a round trip, including the abbreviations people actually type (thx, thanx, ty, ta, cheers, tysm) and some two dozen non-English forms. Normalising folds case, surrounding whitespace, punctuation, emoji and apostrophes, so `"  Thanks!!! :) "` and `"what's up?"` both land. Matching is on the **whole utterance**, by `Map` lookup rather than by regex: "thanks" is small talk, "thanks, now show the tracks" is a request and must reach the model untouched — exact lookup makes that structural instead of a property of some regex being written carefully enough.

  The hard part is what must **not** be intercepted. "yes", "no", "sure" and their kin are excluded outright, because the assistant asks clarifying questions and a bare "yes" is the answer to one. But a question mark is not the only invitation — "Say the word and I'll move the camera." asks just as plainly with none — so the two categories that can express **consent** (acknowledgements, and a bare "please") are gated on `lastBotMessageInvitesAReply()`, which tests the assistant's last message for a trailing "?" (tolerating a closing bracket or quote) or any of 28 `OFFER_PHRASES`. The other six categories are ungated, because a greeting or a farewell can never be consent and gating them too would send most small talk to the model — the exact cost this exists to avoid. The offer list cannot be complete, since it matches model-generated prose, and is tuned for unequal failure directions: a false positive spends one wasted turn, a false negative loses what the user asked for and looks like being ignored, so it errs long and generic. `SMALL_TALK` is listed among the navigational intents, so answering "hello" does not mark the sitch dirty and prompt to save a file nothing changed.

- **"go bingley" now works without the "to"** (`bedb4451`; `GOTO_NAMED_LOCATION` and `GOTO_LLA` patterns in `src/CClientNLU.js`). A bare "go" reached the geocoder only as "go to"; it now behaves identically, as do "goto" and "fly to", and the coordinate form accepts "go 51.8, -1.8". The reason "to" was required in the first place is "go back": a bare go/move otherwise swallows every direction and command — go on, go north, go up, go home, go show the tracks — and turns them into a lookup for a place called "on". Those are refused by a stop-list whose refusal returns `null`, so `_tryMatch` falls through to the later patterns rather than consuming the message. The list is a saved round trip, not a correctness guarantee: anything slipping past is looked up, fails, and reaches the model through the existing fall-through.

- **A plumb line while moving an object** (`43fe3530`; `updateDropLine()` in `src/CObjectMoveWidget.js`). A 50% grey 1 px line runs from the object down to the ground whenever the move widget owns an object. Height above open terrain is the one thing a perspective view will not tell you — a sphere at 20 m and one at 2000 m look identical against distant ground, and while dragging that is exactly what you are judging. "Down" is the local up vector, not world −Y, because the render frame is ECEF; the geometry is object-relative, because ECEF coordinates are 6,378 km from the origin and holding them in float32 visibly jitters; and the ground comes from the elevation map (`getPointBelow(top, false)`) rather than a raycast, which under Google 3D returns the topmost LOD tile instead of the surface being looked at.

- **The assistant can create many objects in one call** (`43fe3530`; `addObjectsAtLLA` in `src/CSitrecAPI.js`, following `createSynthBuildings`). A ring of a hundred spheres was dozens of separate calls and exhausted the per-turn budget before the objects were placed; it is now one call, measured at 100 objects in 3.9 s. Partial success is reported as such — forty of fifty placed is a useful outcome the model can build on, and it needs to know which ten to retry — returning `count`, `created`, `failed`, the generated names and the first five errors. No `namePrefix` is offered, deliberately: `createObjectFromInput` ignores its name argument entirely, so documenting numbering that does not happen would only mislead the model into addressing objects by names they do not have.

- **A live microphone is now visible from anywhere** (`5b0b1cb9`; `installVoicePulseStyle()` in `src/nodes/CNodeVIewChat.js`, `addBarIcon()` / `removeBarIcon()` and `#menuBarIconStrip` in `src/lil-gui-extras.js`). The live indicator was `color:#ff5555` on an emoji, which the platform paints from colour bitmaps in the font — CSS `color` does nothing, so a live microphone was invisible. It is now a pulsing red pill behind the glyph (`sitrec-mic-pulse`, disabled under `prefers-reduced-motion`). A second microphone sits in a new generic right-hand menu-bar icon strip, left of the version panel, reading **REC** when live, so stopping a recording never requires finding a window whose header may have auto-hidden, scrolled away, closed or gone behind something else. Both buttons paint from one state so they can never disagree. The strip knows nothing about what an icon does; the chat view registers into it and removes on dispose, since the bar outlives the per-sitch view.

- **The Assistant header shows which model is answering** (`964cc540`; i18n `misc.chat.modelInUse`, `misc.voice.modelInUse`). It switches to the voice model while the microphone is live — the two can differ in cost by an order of magnitude, so it should not need a trip to Settings to find out — and follows a change made through the header, a restored session, or the assistant changing it itself.

- **A ticking "Thinking…" line, and a warning before a slow turn** (`964cc540`; `startThinkingIndicator()` / `stopThinkingIndicator()` in `src/nodes/CNodeVIewChat.js`). The indicator repaints once a second with elapsed time. On a local model a cold reply takes three minutes and a warm one three seconds, entirely because of prompt prefill, and nothing in the request distinguishes them — Ollama's `/api/ps` answers the question, so a custom endpoint is asked before sending and the user is told when a wait is coming. A server that cannot answer produces **no** warning: one we cannot stand behind would teach people to ignore the case where it is true. There is no progress bar because there is no honest one — prefill reports only to the server's own log, and streaming stays silent through all of it.

- **The API Keys dialog fits on screen** — Sitrec → Settings → *API Keys…* (`5b0b1cb9`). One header line per provider (tick, name, state, spend, buttons) plus a one-line summary, with description, rate and limits opening on click; spend stays on the collapsed line because it is the number a user opens the dialog to see. Every provider now fits in 745 px with no scrolling, down from roughly 140 px a row. Escape closes the dialog, caught at the document rather than the overlay (which only sees the key when something inside it has focus) and guarded so a nested `showPrompt` keeps its own Escape.

- **Escape no longer closes the Assistant while it is docked** (`43fe3530`; `escapeShouldHide()` on `CNodeViewText`, overridden in `CNodeViewChat`). A docked window is part of the layout, and closing it re-flows every view sharing its seams; Escape is a key people press to dismiss a dropdown, not to rearrange a workspace. Tab still toggles it, the header X still closes it, and floating behaviour is unchanged. The hook sits on `CNodeViewText`, which registers the global handler, so Notes can adopt the same rule with a one-line override.

- **One shared object edit menu** (`43fe3530`; `showNodeEditMenu` in `src/CustomManagerMirror.js`, replacing the inline copy in `src/nodes/CNodeView3DMouse.js`). The right-click path and the new create-and-edit path now call one method. The copy in the click path was already wrong — it was missing `placeMenuBesidePoint` and `pinMenuBelowBar`, so it opened on top of the object it was about to edit instead of clear of it. That path shrinks from 45 lines to 3, and both windows now land byte-identically.
- **Startup primes the AI key cache in one IndexedDB read again** (`5e2b08aa`; `primeKeyCache()` in `src/BYOKKeyStore.js`). It fetched the disabled-provider list and the custom endpoints with their own `getSetting` calls (`loadDisabled()`, `loadEndpoints()`) and then called `getAllSettings()`, which already returns both — three round trips where one does. The two extra reads ran *ahead* of the priming read, so keys reached `getCachedKey()` later than they needed to; that is the synchronous read `providerCredential()` in `src/nodes/CNodeTerrainUI.js` uses on a construction path that cannot await, to prefer a user's own tile-provider key over Sitrec's shared one. Both values now come out of the `getAllSettings` result with `disabledPromise` / `endpointsPromise` pre-resolved, and the catch path resolves them too, so nothing later re-reads the store one key at a time. This restores the "one await, one read" shape that the call site in `SettingsManager.js` documents and relies on. No behavior change in normal use. **It is a partial measure, and deliberately not a fix for what exposed it**: the delay it removes had been changing the *settled* 3D scene in the *Google 3D Tiles Shadow Test* fast-regression sitch — a moved camera frustum and an added LOS line, deterministic in both directions. A settle gate that waits on pending actions, parsing and the tile counters should converge no matter when a key arrives, so something is captured at initialization and never recomputed when its input lands later. That order-dependence is **not** fixed here, the same sitch still shows the split under harness concurrency, and it is tracked separately.

### Bug Fixes

- Fixed the Assistant printing an **Error** line for a tool call it went on to complete (`5b0b1cb9`; `endTurn()` in `src/nodes/CNodeVIewChat.js`). A failed tool call printed as it happened, but the assistant retries, so a printed error was usually the model's search rather than a failure — and `addSystemMessage` also pushed the line into `chatHistory`, which `historyToAnthropicMessages` replays as an assistant turn, wasting tokens and crowding real turns out of the 10-message window. Failures are now buffered per turn, and only a failed **action** never repaired in a **later** round is reported, as one deduplicated line capped at three entries that stays out of the history (`recordInHistory: false`). Rounds matter: a repair can only land after the model has seen the error, so a success in the same batch cannot be one. Failed *queries* are never buffered, and the full untrimmed text always goes to the debug channel. `CDirectLLMClient` and `CVoiceSession` gained `onRound`/`onTurnEnd` so all three transports — server, BYOK and voice — share the same turn boundaries.

- Fixed a failure on your own OpenAI key being reported as an **Anthropic** error (`830dd54b`; `src/nodes/CNodeVIewChat.js`). The BYOK failure line mapped only `openrouter`, labelling every other provider "Anthropic", so an OpenAI key problem was reported against the wrong account. It now names the service that actually failed, falling back to "AI provider".

- Fixed the assistant sending a truncated model id for any model whose name contains a colon (`964cc540`; `src/CustomSupport.js` and `src/SkyMaskAI.js`). `chatModelSetting.split(':')` sent `gpt-oss` for `gpt-oss:20b`, mangling Ollama-style tags; both sites now split on the **first** colon only. It went unnoticed against hosted providers because Ollama resolves a bare name to `:latest`, so the mangled id happened to work.

- Fixed `setMenuValue`'s `value` parameter declaring no JSON Schema type at all (`964cc540`; `sitrecServer/chatbot.php` and `buildToolSet()` in `src/CDirectLLMClient.js`). OpenAI and Anthropic tolerate the omission; Ollama's chat template indexes every property's type and died with "slice index out of range", failing the request before any model saw it. It now declares the `["number", "boolean", "string"]` union the schema actually specifies.

- Fixed `anthropic-dangerous-direct-browser-access` being sent to every Anthropic-format endpoint (`964cc540`). It is a non-standard header, so it forces a preflight the gateway must allow; sending it to a server that never heard of it killed the call before it was issued. It now goes to Anthropic's own API only.

- Fixed two latent faults in `CNodePositionLLA` reachable only by a position node built with no `gui` — which nothing had ever created before *Add 3D Object* (`43fe3530`). `recalculate()` read `this.guiAlt.getValue()` unconditionally and threw on construction, though the identical expression is guarded 150 lines earlier; and an assert fired every frame ("no guiAlt defined") guarding a commented-out return that was the only line in its branch ever to read `guiAlt`.

- Fixed a lil-gui defect in the vendored library (`964cc540`; `src/js/lil-gui.esm.js`, marked `SITREC PATCH` — re-apply on upgrade). `options()` repaints through `updateDisplay()`, which returns early when the **value** is unchanged, so replacing a placeholder list while the same value stayed selected left the placeholder on screen for ever. That is why the new *Voice Model* dropdown read "Loading…" indefinitely. The fix sets `_lastDisplayedValue = NaN` before repainting, since NaN is never equal to anything including itself.
- Fixed a `Missing Managed object Custom_NightVision` assert firing once per rendered frame in satellite scenes that have no NVG effect (`eb46253a`; `nvgSatBoost()` in `src/nodes/CNodeDisplayNightSky.js`). The lookup was written `NodeMan.get("Custom_NightVision", true)`, and that second argument is `assertIfMissing` (`CManager.get(id, assertIfMissing=true)`) — so the call requested the very assert it meant to suppress, when the next line, `if (!nvg || !nvg.enabled) return 1`, already handles a missing node. It now passes `false`. The node exists only where `CCustomManager.setup()` inserts it (`insertSensorEffect("NightVision", "Custom_NightVision", "Thermal", …)`, gated on `Sit.isCustom` plus a `lookView` carrying an `effectPasses` array), while `nvgSatBoost` is reached from `updateSatelliteScales()` on every look-view render for which `view.effectsEnabled` is set — and that flag defaults to true on anything that is not the custom sitch. Any look view drawing satellites without the effect node therefore asserted every frame. Both satellite sitches in the fast visual-regression suite, *Atremis Starlink* and *Qianfan Over UK and Europe*, failed to load on it, because both harnesses abort a run on any `ASSERT:` console line (`tests_regression/regression.test.js`, `tests_regression/fast-regression/run.mjs`). Present since `b713c56a` and shipped in 2.144.0, 2.145.0 and 2.146.0 — though the released blast radius is smaller than a failed load: every minified build strips `assert()` through Terser's `pure_funcs` (`webpack.common.js`), which covers `npm run deploy` for the public site, the Docker image and the production-mode serverless/desktop bundle, so those users got no halt, only the two `console.log` lines `CManager.get` emits before the assert, once per rendered frame. An unminified copy (`npm run build`, or the standalone build) additionally logs a `console.trace` and stops on `assert()`'s `debugger` statement whenever DevTools is open, which stalls the load.

### Security

- **The AI prompt log now keeps only the maintainer's own accounts** (`964cc540`; `$NLU_LOG_USER_IDS` in `sitrecServer/logNLU.php`, `isNLULoggingUser()` in `src/configUtils.js`, gate in `logUnhandledLLMCall()`). `logNLU.php` records what people typed to the assistant when a prompt falls through the local matcher to the model on Sitrec's own server route; it previously applied no per-user gate, so any signed-in user's fall-through prompts were retained. It is now restricted to two maintainer accounts **by user id and not by admin group** — other administrators hold that role for operational reasons and never agreed to have their prompts kept. Enforced in the endpoint, not only in the browser: the client also declines to send, but that saves a round trip rather than guaranteeing anything, since a stale cached build, a replayed request or a hand-made POST would all still arrive. The endpoint returns `200 {success: true, logged: false}` rather than an error, so a declined log can never surface as a broken chat turn. The client check uses `Globals.userID` rather than `getEffectiveUserID()`, so an admin using the "test as user" override cannot turn logging on for the account they are impersonating. The BYOK and custom-endpoint routes never reach this code at all.

### Documentation

- **The AI Assistant** — Help → *AI Assistant* (`964cc540`; new `docs/AIAssistant.md` with its `docsRegistry` entry and i18n `menus.help.documentation.aiAssistant`). The only AI documentation was about credentials. This covers what the assistant is, the range of actions it can take, the simple commands Sitrec matches locally without a model, that its actions are **real edits** which mark the sitch unsaved and are only partly covered by undo, the confirmation prompt when the sitch came from a link, phrasing advice, choosing a model and what changes between the routes, the header model readout, the spoken assistant and its two microphone buttons, and a plain list of what it is bad at.
- **Your API Keys** — `docs/APIKeys.md` gains the dynamic model list, custom endpoints and the voice model (`830dd54b`, `964cc540`, `5b0b1cb9`).

## Version 2.146.0 (2026-08-30)

### New Features

- **Ground Track: points placed on the ground as a line-of-sight source** — **Traverse → Ground Track**, selected as **Traverse → LOS Source → Camera + Ground Track** (`c4c99fd6`; new `src/nodes/CNodeGroundTrack.js`, `src/nodes/CNodeGroundTrackLOS.js`, `src/GroundTrackHandles3D.js` and `src/TerrainHandles3D.js`; `src/FitPointHandles3D.js` refactored onto the shared handle machinery, 317 → 206 lines; wiring in `src/CustomManagerSetup.js`; `isEditorWindow` flag in `src/nodes/CNode.js` and `src/nodes/CNodeCurveEdit2.js`; new `docs/GroundTrack.md` with its `docsRegistry` entry and i18n `menus.help.documentation.groundTrack` — *Ground Track (Points on the Ground)*). A third video-derived line-of-sight source alongside *Camera + Object Track* and *Camera + Point Track*. Those two store a video **pixel** and rotate the camera centreline by the angle it sits off centre, so both are only as good as the field of view and the camera aim they are given. A ground track stores a **place**: the line of sight is camera position to ground point, and it reads nothing else from the camera at all. It also bounds the range from above, because an object silhouetted against terrain is nearer than that terrain. `CNodeGroundTrack` and `CNodeGroundTrackLOS` are created for any custom sitch that has `JetLOSCameraCenter` and `JetLOS`, whether or not there is a video, and are inert until a point is placed — `CNodeGroundTrackLOS` falls back to the plain camera LOS while the track is empty, and they are created unconditionally so a sitch saved before this existed still gets them on reload (keyframes ride in the node's own mod, which never reaches a node that does not exist when mods are applied). Editing works in both the look and main views: **Ctrl+click** places or moves the point for the current frame, **click an unselected point** selects it by travelling to its frame and moving nothing, **click the selected point** grabs and drags it over the ground, **Alt+click** deletes it, and **dragging empty space** orbits exactly as if the editor were off. Selecting and moving are deliberately two presses — a point describes one frame, so reaching for it usually means "show me that moment", and a single press that both travelled and grabbed meant every look at a keyframe risked nudging it. "Selected" is not new state: it is the playhead being on that point's frame, which is what makes the red frame-labelled handle an affordance rather than a decoration. Ctrl is required because in a 3D view a plain press has already begun an orbit by the time the editor hears about it. **Between Points** chooses what happens in the gaps, and the placed points never move either way: *3D Position* (default, `BETWEEN_3D`) runs a smooth curve through the placed positions and reads no terrain at all; *Ground Intersection* (`BETWEEN_GROUND`) sweeps the **direction** smoothly instead and raycasts each ray to the world, so every frame is a real place with a real range — roughly 37x dearer, and it stands down while a handle is being dragged. Interpolated points deliberately do **not** re-snap to terrain: because the sightline is camera-to-point, snapping feeds the terrain profile straight into it, and a measured clifftop track dived to the shoreline and climbed back, swinging the LOS by several degrees, which a traversal then turns into speed and acceleration that were never in the data. Ground Intersection rays graze (measured: at 6 km and 6° of depression, about 1 km of range per degree), so a hit disagreeing with the curve by more than `RANGE_AGREEMENT` is treated as a skimmed ray and rejected. The rest of the folder: *Enable Ground Track*, *Show Track*, *Interpolation* (Spline / Linear), *Place on 3D Tiles* (roofs, walls, trees), *Place on Objects*, *Delete Point at Frame*, *Clear All Points*, *Limit A/B to Track*, and disabled *Points* and *Ground Range* readouts. `TerrainHandles3D.js` is new shared machinery — projection, hit-testing, casting the cursor onto the world, borrowing and **restoring** both views' camera controls, and the overlay lifecycle — and `FitPointHandles3D` was moved onto it with behaviour unchanged, gaining the control-restore fix described under Bug Fixes.

- **Voice assistant: speak to Sitrec on your own OpenAI key** — the microphone button in the Assistant window's header (`315c2e9e`, corrected by `c9052369`; new `src/voice/CVoiceSession.js`; `toggleVoice()` / `startVoice()` / `stopVoice()` / `_setVoiceButtonState()` and the `uiBar.addIcon` button in `src/nodes/CNodeVIewChat.js`; audio counters in `src/BYOKUsage.js`; `src/BYOKProviders.js`; i18n `misc.voice.*`; `docs/APIKeys.md`; `tests/CVoiceSession.test.js`). Pressing the microphone opens a WebRTC connection from the browser straight to OpenAI's Realtime API (`gpt-realtime-2`) on the user's own key, added under **Settings → API Keys…**. Sitrec's server is not in the path and never sees the credential, the audio, or the conversation. It is a second **transport**, not a second assistant: the same system prompt, the same tool set, and the same `sitrecAPI.handleAPICall(call, "chat")` execution path, so every injection and confirmation guard the typed path has applies unchanged — a separate dispatch would have been a second door into the API with none of those locks on it. WebRTC rather than the WebSocket transport was chosen for echo cancellation: without it the microphone picks up the assistant's own voice through the speakers, server-side turn detection reads that as the user speaking, and the assistant interrupts itself on every reply. `src/voice/` sits outside the `require.context('./nodes')` sweep in `RegisterNodes.js`, which eagerly bundles everything in that directory regardless of how it is imported, so the 65 KB chunk is fetched on the first press and never before. Audio tokens get their own counters and their own rates in `BYOKUsage` — audio is billed at $32/$64 per 1M against text's $4/$24, so folding it into the text counters would have understated a voice session's cost roughly eightfold; `cachedInput` is an absolute rate because OpenAI charges a flat $0.40/1M whether the cached token is text or audio, which no single multiplier can express. Records stored before the new fields read them as zero. Every teardown path is covered so the microphone can never outlive its reason to be open: `setVisible()` (the choke point for the header X, the Show/Views checkbox, Escape and Tab), `dispose()` for a sitch load, New Chat, and a connection lost after connect. A `voiceGeneration` counter cancels a startup still in flight across its four awaits. **`c9052369` is the fix for that counter and is intra-release** — `voiceGeneration` was never initialised, so `++this.voiceGeneration` produced `NaN`, and because `NaN !== NaN` the `this.voiceGeneration !== generation` cancellation check read as "cancelled" on its very first test. Every startup returned silently right after the dynamic import and pressing the microphone did nothing at all: no error, no chat line, no permission prompt. It was silent because that early return is the "a hide cancelled you" path, which is deliberately quiet, and a diagnostic dump showed `generation: null` because `JSON.stringify(NaN)` is `null`, reading as "never set" rather than "set to a value that poisons every comparison". `voiceGeneration`, `voiceSession` and `voiceStarting` are now initialised in the `CNodeViewChat` constructor: a counter only ever compared for inequality has to start as a number, and lazy initialisation is not enough because `++undefined` does not throw.

- **Live ADS-B Traffic: every aircraft in the area as one lightweight layer** — **Contents → Live Feeds → Live ADS-B Traffic** (`d2d10842`, `6f978ce0`, `13ae3591`, `5b8877f3`, `844813dd`, `ed921a6f`; new `src/traffic/CNodeADSBLiveTraffic.js`, `src/ADSBLiveFetch.js`, `sitrecServer/proxyADSBLive.php`; picking, hover and promotion in `src/nodes/CNodeView3DMouse.js`; menu in `src/CustomManagerSetup.js`; i18n `custom.showHide.liveTraffic*`; `docs/Tracks.md`; `tests/ADSBLiveFetch.test.js`). Draws every aircraft adsb.lol currently sees around the camera as flat aircraft silhouettes pointing along their course, coloured by altitude, each with a short trail. Beside the switch sit a *Traffic Radius (nm)* slider (5–250, step 5, taking effect on the next poll) and a *Traffic* count readout. **One node for the whole sky, not one per aircraft**: a busy area returns 130+ aircraft and the set changes every poll, so per-aircraft tracks and objects would have meant hundreds of nodes churning several times a minute with a per-frame `getValue` cost and a saved sitch carrying the lot. The layer is two draw calls — an `InstancedMesh` of silhouettes and one `LineSegments` of merged trails. Turning it on sets the clock to now and pauses playback, because the feed is the live present and with the clock left in the past the sun, sky and shadows would all disagree with the traffic drawn under them. It is centred on the **camera** rather than `Sit.lat/lon`, which in a fresh custom sitch stays at its default in the Pacific off Baja until Reset Origin — an origin-centred query would show an empty sky to anyone who had simply flown somewhere, which reads as a broken feature. Markers scale with distance to hold a constant apparent size (one view has to serve an approach at four miles and a terminal area at ninety), motion is dead-reckoned between the five-second polls, and course and orientation are derived once per poll rather than per frame since `getLocalNorthVector` allocates five vectors a call and that was the layer's whole per-frame cost. The silhouette needs **two** rotations, not one — lay the shape's `+Z` onto local up, then spin about that axis onto the course — or half the traffic sits edge-on and invisible from above; it is `DoubleSide` because an observer on the ground looks at these from underneath, and trails fade from 15% at the tail to full at the head so they read as a direction of travel. **Click an aircraft to promote it to a real track**: a single click fetches that aircraft's full ~24-hour trace and adds it as an ordinary Sitrec track, the same thing *Import ADS-B Track…* does without needing the hex address. Picking is screen-space proximity, not a raycast against the `InstancedMesh` — a marker is about 0.6° across, so an exact `instanceId` hit would demand pixel-accurate aim at a moving target, and proximity is what `findClosestTrack` already does, so tracks and aircraft behave alike under the cursor. The drag test compares release against press in `onMouseUp`, **not** in `onMouseMove`: `onDocumentMouseMove` routes to `onMouseDrag` when a view defines one, pointer capture can deliver moves somewhere other than the document, and a fast drag can produce a release with no intervening move at all. The view reaches the layer through `NodeMan` rather than an import, because a static import in `CNodeView3DMouse` would drag the lazy chunk back into the main bundle for every user. A second click on an already-imported aircraft does nothing and says so, checked against `FileManager` rather than a local set so it survives a reload and also catches a track imported through the manual dialog. Hovering shows an info box with type, registration, altitude, speed and heading plus a hint saying what a click does; one shared hit-test (`_liveFeedHitAt`) serves hover and click so a tooltip can never describe a different aircraft from the one a click would promote, and it is skipped while a button is held because during a camera drag the cursor sweeps the whole scene. Labels are a DOM overlay on the main view (`src/livefeeds/LiveFeedOverlay.js`, shared with the other feeds) — see the Live Feeds entry for the declutter design. The status readout is written to never overstate what it knows: `loading…` before the first answer, `none within 50nm of 33.9°N 118.4°W` when a completed search found nothing (position and radius captured *before* the await and stored only on success, so a failed poll, a camera move or a radius drag can never relabel still-displayed results as a search at the new place), `⚠ adsb.lol is not responding — retrying in 26s` for a 502 from our own proxy, and a distinct wording for stale data. **The layer is not serialized** — `CustomManagerSerialize` writes anything with a `modSerialize` function, so defining none keeps a view of the live present out of every save, and also lets the file sit outside `src/nodes/` and load as its own 73 KB chunk on first enable. `api.adsb.lol` sends no CORS headers, so unlike the trace importer the PHP proxy is mandatory and the layer reports itself unavailable in serverless builds; it also answers 403 to a request with no `User-Agent`, which is what PHP's cURL sends by default, so `curlGetRequest` gained an optional extra-headers parameter (defaulting to none) and the new proxy identifies itself.

- **Seven more live feeds: military aircraft, ships, webcams, road traffic, weather balloons, rocket launches and earthquakes** — **Contents → Live Feeds** (`7ffce47a`, `86455eed`, `cd8d13be`, `5b8877f3`, `844813dd`, `ed921a6f`; new `src/livefeeds/LiveFeedRegistry.js`, `src/livefeeds/CNodeLiveFeedLayer.js`, `src/livefeeds/LiveFeedFetch.js`, `src/livefeeds/LiveFeedOverlay.js`, `sitrecServer/proxyLiveFeed.php`; new `windy`, `aisstream` and `tomtom` entries in `src/BYOKProviders.js`; `GUI.prototype.moveToFirst` in `src/lil-gui-extras.js`; menu loop in `src/CustomManagerSetup.js`; i18n `custom.showHide.liveFeeds`; `docs/Tracks.md`, `docs/APIKeys.md`; `tests/LiveFeedRegistry.test.js`). **A table, not seven subsystems**: one proxy row plus one `LIVE_FEEDS` registry entry defines a feed, and the menu, the marker layer, the status readout and the attribution are all driven from it. The client names a feed **id** and never a URL — every keyless upstream host is hardcoded server-side, and the only client values reaching a URL are range-checked numbers. `LIVE_FEEDS` is imported statically while the layer is lazy: the registry is a few hundred lines of table and parsers, but the layer pulls in three.js geometry and instancing, and splitting the table out too would risk the menu and the registry drifting apart, which is the failure the table exists to prevent. The seven are *Military Aircraft* (adsb.lol ODbL, 10 s), *Marine Traffic (AIS)* (aisstream.io, websocket), *Webcams* (Windy.com, 5 min), *Road Traffic Incidents* (TomTom, 2 min), *Weather Balloons* (SondeHub, 60 s), *Rocket Launches* (Launch Library 2 / The Space Devs, 30 min, drawn at the **pad** because drawing a trajectory would be inventing one) and *Earthquakes* (USGS, M2.5+ in the last 24 h, 5 min). Civil ADS-B stays a separate node inside the same folder — aircraft need dead reckoning between polls, trails and click-to-promote, and an earthquake needs none of it — but `844813dd` moved its switch, radius and count **into** the Live Feeds folder, since it is the same kind of thing and having it outside while military aircraft sat inside made the grouping look arbitrary; Contents is left with only the track tools again. `cd8d13be` also added `GUI.prototype.moveToFirst` (`Controller.moveToFirst` existed, but a folder is a `GUI`, not a `Controller`) so the folder sits at the top of Contents rather than beneath the per-track folders, each of which expands to a dozen controls — several screens of scrolling before a new feature is even visible is indistinguishable from it not being there. **Keyed feeds do not go through the proxy.** `86455eed` replaced the first cut's Digitraffic Baltic-AIS and Finnish-webcam feeds — a regional substitute for a worldwide feature looks broken to everyone outside the region — with three worldwide feeds on the user's own free key. `docs/APIKeys.md` promises a user's keys are never sent to Sitrec's server, so proxying one would quietly break that; each provider was checked to serve CORS to a browser **before** being chosen (Windy's preflight explicitly allows `x-windy-api-key`, TomTom echoes the Origin). A useful side effect is that these three also work in serverless and desktop builds, so the `isServerless` guard in `setFeed()` is now **keyless-only**. A feed with no key shows `needs a key — Settings, API Keys` rather than an empty world, so a missing key names its own fix. AISStream is a websocket rather than a poll, so `CNodeLiveFeedLayer` gained a second transport: it subscribes from the open handler (the connection is dropped if nothing subscribes within three seconds), keys markers by MMSI in a `Map` so a vessel reporting every few seconds replaces its position instead of accumulating one marker per report, rebuilds geometry on a timer rather than per message, reads authentication failures out of the **message** stream since a bad key arrives as a message on an otherwise healthy socket, and reconnects with backoff on close, clearing the socket reference first so turning the layer off does not immediately reconnect it. Two coordinate-order traps are covered by tests because either one silently queries the wrong part of the world rather than failing: AISStream takes `[lat, lon]` bounding boxes, TomTom takes `minLon,minLat,maxLon,maxLat`. **Marker shape carries meaning alongside colour** — ships are boxes, balloons spheres, launches and road incidents cones, webcams and earthquakes octahedra — because with several layers on at once colour alone stops being enough, and is no help at all to a colour-blind viewer; markers are a third the size of the aircraft silhouettes, which number about a hundred and need a readable heading, while these run past a thousand in one view. Clicking a marker does the most useful thing available (`_openFeedMarker`): a military aircraft imports its full trace like a civil one, a webcam opens its current image (a webcam you cannot look through is not worth marking), anything with a source URL opens it with `noopener,noreferrer`, and a ship or radiosonde with no link reports its details into that feed's own readout rather than a modal — a dialog per click would make browsing a busy layer unbearable. **Labels** (`LiveFeedOverlay`) are a DOM overlay on the main view rather than sprites in the scene: text as 3D objects fights the depth buffer, re-renders on every camera move, and is blurry at a readable size, while DOM gets crisp glyphs and real font metrics for collision boxes, with `pointerEvents: none` throughout. The hard part is declutter, not drawing — labels are budgeted at `MAX_LABELS = 36`, sorted nearest-first, re-laid-out every 100 ms, and placed greedily; one that would overlap a label already down is **dropped** rather than nudged, because nudging moves a label off the thing it names, which is the worse failure. (35 aircraft over Los Angeles produced 7 labels, the rest correctly suppressed.) A distance gate was tried first and removed: an absolute cutoff in metres is the wrong instrument — what makes labels unreadable is on-screen crowding, which the collision test already handles exactly — and at 400 km it simply made labels vanish at ordinary viewing distances, since a camera framing Los Angeles sits about 2,300 km out. Three parsing bugs were found and fixed while building it: USGS's third coordinate is **depth in kilometres, positive down**, not an altitude, and honouring it literally buried an M5.1 marker 136 km inside the Earth, so quakes are drawn at the epicentre with depth in the detail line; `proxyLiveFeed.php`'s cache key omitted the upstream URL, so repointing a feed served the old body for its whole TTL; and a status of `none` before the first poll claims a result that has not been fetched, so both layers now say `loading…` until the first answer. Every error is prefixed with a warning sign and followed by the seconds until the next retry, because the old wording said nothing about whose fault it was or whether waiting helps — and an AISStream error arriving as a message on a healthy socket is now marked **fatal** (socket closed, close handler declines to resurrect it, status says to check the key) rather than promising "retrying" forever while nothing retried. Upstream quirks worth recording: SondeHub's duration is a token rather than seconds and returns a map of maps needing the latest frame per sonde, and Launch Library's plain endpoint sorts far-future placeholders to the top so `/launch/previous/` is what answers "was there a launch near this time?". OpenSky is excluded (non-commercial, and REST use in production needs their agreement) and TeleGeography cables are excluded (CC BY-NC-SA is copyleft data).

- **Move a 3D object by dragging it** (`a0f5cfb9`, `022b3bb8`; new `src/CObjectMoveWidget.js`; driven per view from `CNodeView3D`'s render path; `findRootTrack` from `src/FindRootTrack.js`; opacity uniform in `src/nodes/CNode3DObjectGeometry.js`; `src/PointEditorWidget.js`, `src/PointEditor.js`, `src/SplineEditor.js`, `src/CustomManagerMenus.js`, `src/lil-gui-extras.js`, `src/nodes/CNodeView3DMouse.js`; `tests/lil-gui-extras.test.js`). An object never owns its position — a `CNodeControllerTrackPosition` copies one out of a track every frame — so until now the only ways to move one were the track's own editor or its numeric boxes, even though the object is right there on screen to point at. `CObjectMoveWidget` puts the same `PointEditorWidget` the spline editor uses on its control points onto the object itself, resolves what actually holds that object's position with `findRootTrack`, and writes the drag there: a synthetic spline (`CNodeSplineEditor`) moves the control point at the current frame, inserting one first when the frame falls between two existing points; a fixed position (`CNodePositionLLA` — the camera and the target) takes `setLLA`, which also refreshes its Lat/Lon/Alt boxes; anything else (ADS-B, KML, MISB, satellites) is read-only data, so no widget appears at all. The drag applies a **delta**, never an absolute position: the object sits where the track says *after* smoothing and ground clamping, so its rendered position is not the track's. That is also what makes the windblown target work — the delta goes onto the undrifted `node.ecef` rather than onto `p(f)`. In AGL mode only the along-local-up component may change the stored height, since that is a clearance rather than a datum altitude. **Two ways in**: the object whose edit menu is open (right-click an object), or **any** movable object near the cursor while Option/Alt is held, which opens no menu and suppresses camera navigation for as long as it is active, so a drag that misses the handles does nothing instead of spinning the scene. Alt is read from the DOM events' own `altKey` rather than through `isKeyHeld`, because `keyup` does not request a render (`keydown` does) and an event's `altKey` cannot latch; a `blur` listener clears it for Alt+Tab, which takes the key away with no `keyup`. Either way the widget stays hidden until the cursor comes near, then crossfades in over 150 ms while the object fades to 25% — restoring every material's `opacity`, `transparent` and `depthWrite` afterwards — and the object drops out of the right-click picker while faded, so a click reaches the ground behind the thing being edited. Gradient materials had to learn about opacity for that: `gradientFragmentShader` ended `gl_FragColor = vec4(..., 1.0)` and a `ShaderMaterial` gets no built-in opacity uniform, so `material.opacity` was inert and a gradient object stayed solid through the fade. It now declares one, defaulting to 1.0, which reproduces the old alpha exactly — the whole regression suite renders byte-identically across the change. The arrow handles are picked as a padded invisible `CylinderGeometry` at the head's full base radius, running the arrow's whole length plus 3 screen pixels in every direction, rather than as the cone itself: a cone tapers to nothing, so at the tip — the part people aim at — the target was a pixel or two wide, and the shaft under it three. `Raycaster` does not test `.visible`, so it picks without drawing; the tip goes from ~0 px to 10.2 px of grab radius, at the cost of the arrows shadowing a ~10 px core of the 40 px disc, which is its pivot and was already crossed by the shaft.

- **Full export set for every spline track** — **File → Export** (`ff3a290b`; `addTrackExportButtons()`, `smoothedTrackNode()` and delegating `exportTrackCSV` / `exportMISBCompliantCSV` / `exportTrackKML` in `src/nodes/CNodeSplineEdit.js`; `CNodeArray.exportFileStem()` and the `exportFolderName` hook in `src/nodes/CNodeManager.addExportButton`; `src/TrackManager.js`; `docs/Tracks.md`). A spline track previously offered only *Export Spline* (its control points) and only from the Contents or Physics menus — it appeared nowhere under **File → Export**, and the per-frame track it generates could not be exported at all. Both routes that build one were responsible: `TrackManager.addSyntheticTrack()` creates the smoothed wrapper with `exportable: false`, so no buttons were registered, and `CNodeSplineEditor` registered none of its own despite inheriting working exporters from `CNodeTrack` and `CNodeArray`. Each spline now gets a **File → Export** sub-folder holding all four — control points as a droppable `.spline.json`, plus per-frame CSV, MISB CSV and KML. Registration happens in the `CNodeSplineEditor` constructor for sitch-built splines (the three in `SitAguadilla`) and from `TrackManager` for synthetic ones, which cannot use the constructor because it needs both the display name and the wrapper node, and must run after `recalculate()` or the CSV probe returns null on an empty array and silently adds no button. The three per-frame exports delegate to `trackOb.trackNode`, the `CNodeSmoothedPositionTrack` wrapper, **not** the raw spline — that is what the displayed line draws and what the Smoothing window acts on, so exporting the spline directly would silently drop any smoothing the user had dialled in. A sitch-built spline has no wrapper and exports itself. Filenames and the sub-folder title come from the spline's name rather than the node id, which for a synthetic track is a generated timestamp such as `syntheticTrack_1785271794788`; `exportFileStem()` and `exportFolderName` both default to the id, so no existing export changes name. Verified on both routes: all four formats emit 7028 data rows, with each format's datum carried correctly (plain CSV HAE, MISB and KML MSL, a −47.75 m geoid separation over Puerto Rico).

- **"Edit Head Only" for Point Track** — **Video → Point Track** (`7f61d30e`; `src/CObjectTracking.js`; i18n `tracking.editHeadOnly`; `docs/PointTrack.md`). `mouse.handlers.down` hit-tests `findClickedKeyframe()` first and returns on the first match, so any keyframe within 5 screen pixels of the click wins it. On a slow-moving object the track doubles back and a dozen earlier keyframes end up inside the yellow cursor, and the head — the point at the current frame — then loses its own click. Measured on the Agua Tracking sitch at frame 133, pressing dead centre on the cursor grabbed keyframe 44: the head was not merely awkward to grab, it was unreachable, and the mistake is invisible until you scrub back. *Edit Head Only* (off by default, serialized alongside the other Point Track settings) skips the keyframe hit-test entirely, leaving `isWithinTrackPoint()` — the existing head-drag path — as the only thing that can arm a drag. There is no new movement code, so dragging the head behaves exactly as before. The whole track still draws, since the context is the point of looking at it, but the parts a drag can no longer reach fade back: the cyan path from 50% to 25%, the other keyframes from full to 10%. The keyframe at the current frame sits under the cursor and **is** the head, so it keeps full opacity — what stays bright is exactly what can still be moved. The yellow cursor and search ring are untouched. Delete/Backspace is deliberately unchanged: it still removes the keyframe under the mouse whatever frame it belongs to, because the restriction asked for was on movement, and deletion is an explicit keypress rather than the accident this mode exists to prevent.

### Improvements

- **Right-click a control point to delete it, and tracks may now go down to a single point** (`a0f5cfb9`, `022b3bb8`; `deleteControlPointAtEvent()` and the `onContextMenuInner` dispatch in `src/nodes/CNodeView3DMouse.js`; `removePointByIndex`, `load()` and `dispose()` in `src/PointEditor.js`; `isLinear()`, `minimumPoints` and `updateSplineMesh` in `src/SplineEditor.js`; `src/PointEditorWidget.js`). Right-clicking a control point of a track being edited deletes it and opens nothing. It is dispatched from `onContextMenuInner` ahead of every menu, so "delete this point" and "open the track menu" are settled in one place rather than racing over the same button press, and it iterates `NodeMan` rather than reading `Globals.editingTrack` because sitch-defined splines (Aguadilla's lantern editor) are enabled directly and never pass through `TrackManager`'s `editingTrack`. It is refused for the last remaining point, since a track with none has no position at all and `getPointFrame` asserts on it. To make one-point tracks safe, `SplineEditor.isLinear()` is now `curveType === 'linear' || numPoints < 4`, read by `getPoint`, `getControlPointDirection` and `updateSplineMesh` alike — Catmull-Rom needs four control points, and below that three.js synthesises the end tangents by reflection and at one point divides by a zero-length span — and `minimumPoints` drops to 1 for every curve type. `PointEditorWidget.onPointerDown` now returns early for any button but 0: `onPointerMove` already refused to drag for non-left buttons, but `pointerdown` dispatched `dragging-changed` first and unconditionally, and listeners treat that as a real drag — `PointEditor` snapshots the track state for undo, and every view turns its camera controls off. That was harmless while nothing used the right button; with right-click delete it meant right-clicking a point dispatched "drag started" with N points, deleted the point, then dispatched "drag ended" with N−1, recording a spurious *Move track control point* undo entry on top of the delete, and undoing **that** wrote the N saved positions back into an N−1 array, shifting every point past the deletion. The early return sits after `setupRaycasterForEvent`, so `activeView` still tracks the press, and before the intersect test, so a right-click over a handle leaves the widget entirely alone and reaches the context-menu path with the state it expects. *Remove Closest Point* now calls `removePointByIndex` instead of repeating the array and scene surgery inline behind a native `alert()`.

- **An object's edit menu no longer opens on top of the object it edits** (`a0f5cfb9`; `placeMenuBesidePoint()` and `pinMenuBelowBar()` in `src/lil-gui-extras.js`, called from `CNodeView3DMouse` after `standaloneMenu.open()`; nine tests in `tests/lil-gui-extras.test.js`). With the move widget the object is now something you want to *see* while its menu is up. The menu shifts right by half its width, or left by one and a half widths when that would run off the viewport, and when neither fits — a narrow window — falls back to whichever side can still hold it clear of the click. Vertically it is pinned to a fixed row one menu line under the top bar, so every object menu appears in the same place. Both keep `originalLeft` / `originalTop` in step, or undocking would snap the menu back over the object. Placement runs after `open()` so the width and title height read are the populated menu's.

- **Native `prompt()` replaced with Sitrec's own modal at six input sites** (`06713aa2`; `showPrompt()` in `src/showError.js`; call sites in `src/index.js` (Add Object), `src/CustomManagerSubSitch.js` (Rename Sub Sitch), `src/CustomManagerMenus.js` (Add Label), `src/CTextExtraction.js` (Learn Character), `src/nodes/CNodeAnnotateOverlay.js` (annotation text) and `src/scriptedVideo/ScriptEditorWindow.js` (Rename Script); `tests/noNativePrompt.test.js`, `tests/showPromptSerialization.test.js`). Native `prompt()` freezes the main thread, cannot be styled or translated, and stalls the render loop. Callers silently depended on both properties of that freeze, so `showPrompt` re-establishes them explicitly: a `promptIsOpen` flag makes it refuse to open while one is already up (an impatient double-click on *Add Object* used to be swallowed by the blocked thread; without the guard it stacked a second modal and made two objects — the extra request resolves as cancelled, which every caller already handles), and it holds playback for the modal's lifetime by setting `par.paused` and restoring it through a single `cleanup()` exit path that also covers backdrop click and Escape. Callers read frame-dependent state around the prompt — `CNodeAnnotateOverlay` stamps a stroke with the frame clicked, `CTextExtraction` pulls the video image at `par.frame`, `createObjectFromInput` starts a track at `par.frame` — and a running video that advanced past them produced results wrong in ways that look like nothing happened: a faded-out annotation (`getStrokeOpacity` is 0 once age ≥ `fadeFrames`), a character template learned from the wrong frame. `pausedLock` is respected by the setter, so an analysis holding the frame counter keeps it. A regression test now fails the build if any file under `src/` calls the native prompt.

- **The never-used Reflection Analysis folder is hidden from the object menu** (`a0f5cfb9`; `src/CustomManagerMenus.js`). The analysis methods stay callable and `dispose()` still needs `reflectionArrowIds` to exist, so only the GUI goes.

### Bug Fixes

- **Fixed "Add Object" failing with `NodeMan.getAllNodes is not a function`** — **Objects → Add Object** (`06713aa2`; `getNextObjectName()` in `src/CustomManagerMenus.js`; `src/utils/parseObjectInput.js`; `tests/addObjectFromMenu.test.js`). That method has never existed on any manager. It was invented in `fe829520` (2025-12-20) alongside a test file that only covered the pure string parser, leaving the one function that touched the node graph untested, and `65f821a2` later moved it verbatim into `CustomManagerMenus.js`. It only ran when the user typed bare coordinates (`parsed.name || getNextObjectName()`), so naming an object skipped it entirely — which is why it survived several releases. `getNextObjectName` had a second bug that would have kept it broken: it scanned `node.menuName`, a sitch-level property, while the name actually lands on `menuText` (set by `TrackManager` on the spline editor node), and since node ids are timestamped it would have returned "Object 1" forever.

- **Fixed undo leaving 16 of the 28 nodes a created object registers behind, and undo history surviving a sitch load** (`06713aa2`; `UndoManager.clear()` called from `disposeEverything()`; `src/undoCreateObject.js`; `PointEditor.dispose()`; `disposeSyntheticTrack()` in `src/TrackManager.js`; `tests/createObjectUndo.test.js`, `tests/trackTeardownNodeLeaks.test.js`, `tests/undoManagerClear.test.js`). `unlinkDisposeRemove()` severs a node's edges but disposes only that node, and recursing through inputs does not reach `_color_colorInput` or `_modelLength`, which are not inputs at all. Three causes were fixed at their sources: `createObjectFromInput` now records its auto-created sub-node ids at construction and undo sweeps them, object last; `PointEditor.dispose()` called `node.dispose()`, which frees resources but never unregisters, leaking 7 nodes per teardown; and `disposeSyntheticTrack()` never ran `pruneUnusedFlagged()`, so the auto-wrapped scalar input constant `syntheticTrackDisplay_<ts>_width` survived every removal (`CMetaTrack.dispose()` always did). Separately, `UndoManager.clear()` existed but nothing ever called it, so actions closing over a torn-down sitch's nodes carried into the next sitch; it is now called from `disposeEverything()`, the single teardown chokepoint. Verified live: three create/undo cycles hold at 432 nodes with no stragglers.

- **Fixed two objects created in the same millisecond colliding on their generated id** (`06713aa2`; `CManager.UniqueName(prefix)` in `src/CManager.js`; applied at the 8 generated-id sites; `tests/uniqueName.test.js`). `${prefix}_${Date.now()}` is not unique, and the second object threw out of `CManager.add`. `UniqueName` returns the name unchanged when free and only appends `_1`, `_2` on collision, so no existing id changes shape, and deserialized ids stay verbatim.

- **Fixed exported KML being unparseable when the track or sitch name contains an XML-reserved character** (`ff3a290b`; `escapeXML` moved from `src/ExportCameraKML.js` to `src/utils.js`; `exportTrackKML` in `src/nodes/CNodeArray.js`; `tests/KMLExportEscaping.test.js`). The KML `<name>` is built from `Sit.name + "-" + <stem>`, and was written raw. That was survivable while the stem was a node id, which is inherently XML-safe, but a name as ordinary as "Search & Rescue" makes the whole document unparseable rather than just that element — and this release feeds human-readable spline names through the same string. Both `<name>` elements are now escaped, while the download filename stays raw. Re-import is unaffected: the XML parser unescapes on the way back in, so the name round-trips exactly. `escapeXML` was moved to `utils.js` so both KML writers share one copy instead of a fifth near-identical inline version appearing.

- **Fixed a stalled adsb.lol trace host being able to take down the whole PHP backend** (`ed921a6f`; `sitrecServer/proxyADSBTrace.php`; `AbortSignal.timeout` in `src/ADSBTraceFetch.js`). `curlGetRequest` sets no `CURLOPT_TIMEOUT`, so it waits forever; `proxyADSBTrace.php` — which has shipped since `17a588ef` — called it with no timeout, so a stalled upstream held a PHP-FPM worker for the whole request, and enough of those exhaust the pool and stop **every** server feature answering, not just ADS-B. adsb.lol's trace host was observed stalling twice on 2026-08-30. The proxy now passes a 15 s timeout (longer than the live feed's 10 s, because a full 24-hour trace is a much larger body) and identifies itself with a `User-Agent`. The client gained a 20 s deadline too, since without one a hung fetch leaves the *importing …* status line unresolved forever, and a timeout is now reported as "adsb.lol did not respond in time. It may be down — try again shortly." rather than a raw abort. This mattered less when reaching the proxy took a deliberate dialog entry; it is now one click on an aircraft.

- **Fixed a track's old curve staying on screen after its points were deleted, and a load that could spin forever** (`a0f5cfb9`; `updateSplineMesh` in `src/SplineEditor.js`; `load()` in `src/PointEditor.js`). `updateSplineMesh` returned early below two points, which left the last shape it drew on screen — whittle a track down to one point and the old curve stayed hanging there; it now hides the curve line instead. And `PointEditor.load()` shrinks with a `while` loop that tests only the length while `removePoint()` declines below `minimumPoints`, so a load asking for fewer points than the editor would give up spun forever. That could not happen while the floor was 4 and every saved track had at least four points, but it can now that the floor is 1, so the loop breaks when the count stops falling.

- **Fixed picking a traverse method re-opening the FOV curve editor over a sitch saved with it closed** (`c4c99fd6`; `showActiveSources` now skips nodes flagged `isEditorWindow`; `src/nodes/CNode.js`, `src/nodes/CNodeCurveEdit2.js`). `CNodeSwitch.choiceChanged` calls `showActiveSources`, which walks up the input tree showing every source, and that walk reached `fovEditor` through the camera. An editor window is a tool the user opens and closes, not a display of the thing being selected. Selecting *FOV Editor* as the FOV source still opens it — that is a different code path.

- **Fixed releasing a terrain-handle drag switching camera controls on rather than restoring them** (`c4c99fd6`; `src/TerrainHandles3D.js`, with `src/FitPointHandles3D.js` refactored onto it). The camera-fit landmark handles used to re-enable both views' controls on pointer-up regardless of how they were found, which overruled Free Look. The shared handle machinery now saves and restores the state it borrowed.

- **Bounded `CNodeArray.exportArray`'s inspect probe to one row** (`ff3a290b`; `tests/MISBExportInspect.test.js`). `makeExportButton` calls every exporter with `inspect = true` at node **creation** just to build a tooltip from the header and first row, and this built the entire CSV — 7028 rows for the measured track — then discarded all but two lines, delaying every node that owns an array export. `exportMISBCompliantCSV` already bounded its probe; `exportArray` now does the same.

- **Fixed `npm test` silently skipping the entire Jest suite whenever the SitrecBridge phase failed** (working tree; new `scripts/runTests.mjs`, `test` and `test-nofits` in `package.json`). The root test command was `npm --prefix tools/SitrecBridge test && npx jest tests/`. Running the bridge suites first, under their own `node --test` runner, is deliberate — see the 2.110.3 entry below — but the `&&` joining them was not. The bridge suite spawns a real broker that binds a loopback TCP port, which a sandboxed shell refuses outright: measured on clean code, 35 tests, 25 pass, 10 fail, and every one of those ten reads `listen EPERM: operation not permitted`. The short-circuit then meant the ~4400 Jest tests never ran at all, while the run still ended in what looks like a finished test report (`1..35`, `# fail 10`) — so the only tell that the far larger suite had been skipped entirely was the test count. The command was never falsely green (it exited non-zero), but a red run naming only the component already known to be sandbox-flaky invites exactly the wrong conclusion. `test` and `test-nofits` now call `node scripts/runTests.mjs --fits` and `--nofits`, which runs the bridge phase and the Jest phase — **always both**, in the same order as before — then prints a `=== Test summary ===` block naming each phase PASS or FAIL, and exits non-zero if either failed. `--fits` runs `npx jest tests/` (exactly what `npm test` did) and `--nofits` runs `node scripts/jestFits.mjs --skip`; trailing arguments pass through to the Jest phase, and an unrecognised mode exits 2. When the bridge phase fails the runner also prints a hint that an all-`listen EPERM` failure is a sandboxed shell refusing a loopback port rather than a code regression, and that the Jest result above it stands either way. The pass/fail condition of the command is unchanged — it still succeeds only when both phases succeed, so nothing that used to fail now passes — what is new is that a bridge failure can no longer conceal the Jest result. This reaches CI too, since `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs root `npm test`. `test-fits` is untouched. Verified sandboxed: bridge FAIL, Jest still ran and enumerated its suites, the summary reported both phases, exit 1.

## Version 2.145.0 (2026-08-29)

### New Features

- **Wind Tracer: a global fit for passive drifters observed through a hand-slewed camera boresight** — **Traverse → LOS Traverse Method → Global Fit: Wind Tracer** (`c73133ff`; new `src/WindTracerFit.js` and `src/nodes/CNodeLOSFitWindTracer.js`; integration in `src/MakeTraverseNodesMenu.js` and `src/JetStuff.js`; `buildLOSDataset()` additions in `src/LOSFitting.js`; `docs/TraverseMethods.md`; `tests/WindTracerRecovery.test.js`). The trajectory is written as an unknown anchor plus a displacement shape, `P(t) = P0 + D(t; theta)`. For every candidate set of wind and vertical-motion parameters, `solveWindTracerAnchor()` eliminates `P0` with a 3×3 normal-equation solve over the complete fitted window, so there is no initial-range search and range is triangulated from the whole clip. The outer search is deterministic: a wind rose supplies the global seed and Nelder-Mead refines bounded wind, shear, buoyancy, terminal-speed, flame-out, cooling and time-varying-wind parameters. `buildLOSDataset()` now supplies `camRight`, `camUp` and per-frame `vFOV`; the fit uses the image-plane axes for a high-pass Fourier nuisance basis whose lower cutoff is derived above the measured azimuth-sweep frequency, allowing faster operator wobble to be modelled without deliberately giving the nuisance model the slow trajectory’s own frequency. The Traverse menu adds *Tracer Pointing σ (°)* and *Tracer Loose Shear*, while *Wind Tracer Result* reports solved wind, ground and vertical motion, range, corrected and raw residuals, modelled pointing and pinned-bound or observability caveats. The limitation is explicit: slow pointing drift cannot be recovered from a boresight alone, a smaller corrected residual is not necessarily a better trajectory on operator-coloured noise, and a good fit establishes compatibility with a passive tracer rather than identifying the object as a lantern or balloon.

### Bug Fixes

- **Fixed Wind Tracer missing strong rises and descents** — **Traverse → LOS Traverse Method → Global Fit: Wind Tracer** (`5933cca6`; `WIND_TRACER_PARAMS`, `VERTICAL_SEEDS` and `fitWindTracer()` in `src/WindTracerFit.js`; `tests/WindTracerRecovery.test.js`; `docs/TraverseMethods.md`). The vertical law is sign-symmetric, but the original `beta0` bounds of 0.90–1.60 were not: a still-lit descent was capped near 1 m/s, while faster sinking was reachable only through the flame-out branch. Once `tOut` lies past the clip, that parameter has no effect at all, leaving a flat cost plateau that the original wind-rose seed could not cross. `beta0` now spans 0–2, making net buoyancy symmetric about neutral and continuously exposing rates up to `vTerm` in either direction. Seeding is now staged: three cheap vertical probes rank the wind rose, the best eight winds are crossed with nine explicit vertical regimes—seven lit and two cold—and the best lit and cold candidates are briefly refined on a common frozen context before the winning branch enters the full fit. The recovery test covers strong and gentle ascent, neutral motion, and gentle and strong descent.

- **Fixed synthetic buildings floating above or sinking below Google Photorealistic 3D tile ground** (`f816ae66`; new `getVisiblePointBelow()` in `src/threeExt.js`; five snap sites in `CNodeSynthBuilding` and `CNodeSynthBuildingEvents`; `visibleGroundChanged` dispatches in `CNodeBuildings3DTiles.update()` and `CNodeTerrainUI.updateTerrainVisibility()`; `docs/Terrain.md`). Buildings previously used `getPointBelow()`, which returns the elevation-map surface even while the photorealistic tiles are the rendered ground; at the measured Arizona site those surfaces differ by 1.7–2.3 m. `getVisiblePointBelow()` first resolves the elevation-map point on the requested latitude/longitude column, raycasts the tile surface from there when the tiles are the visible ground, and falls back to the elevation map when no tile hit is available. Synthetic buildings use it during construction and editing, then re-snap when a tileset settles or when the tiles are toggled on or off. `CNodeSynthBuildingEvents.resnapToGround()` rebuilds the vertices, mesh, GUI values and editing handles, defers a ground change that arrives during a drag until pointer-up, and lets stale event listeners unregister when their building has been disposed.

- **Fixed tile-geometry edits leaving synthetic buildings on the old surface** — **Terrain → Remove Geometry** (`1eec194f`; `announceSurfaceEdited()` in `src/nodes/CNodeBuildings3DTiles.js`). *Flatten Trees* and the *Remove Geometry* brush mutate already-loaded tile geometry synchronously and idempotently, so the streaming-settled edge added by `f816ae66` cannot detect them; buildings therefore remained floating or buried after an edit. `visibleGroundChanged` is now dispatched after *Apply Edits*, *Restore Geometry*, undo/redo state restoration, and a completed manual brush stroke. Brush notification happens once at the end of the stroke rather than for every pointer-move dab, avoiding repeated building mesh rebuilds while painting.

### Documentation

- **Expanded the `LOSFitting.js` engineering contract and derivations** (`0fad9855`; comments only, with no executable changes). The module header now distinguishes the pure mathematical fitters from the Three.js/Sitrec adapters, documents `Float32Array` and `Float64Array` inputs, `minRange`, dataset-relative `excluded` indices, and the family-specific residual units that must not be compared without conversion. A glossary and per-fitter derivations explain the LOS projection matrix `M_i = I - d_i d_i^T`, the CV/CA design blocks, in-place normal-equation accumulation, time normalization, conditioning, Monte Carlo variants, Kalman/RTS smoothing and physics-fit conventions.

## Version 2.144.0 (2026-08-27)

### New Features

- **Lunar eclipses: the Earth's shadow on the Moon, with a computed blood moon** — **Lighting → Lunar Eclipse** (`6de3d486`; new `src/CLunarEclipseCalc.js` — `shadowRadiiKm`, `directSunlightAt`, `getShadowGeometry`, `getLunarEclipseState`, `getUmbralProfile`, `sampleUmbralProfile`, `lunarDiskIllumination`, `danjonFromIllumination`, `lunarEclipseDimming`, the frozen `NO_LUNAR_ECLIPSE`, and the shared `lunarEclipseRender` publish object; new `src/atmosphere/umbralLight.js` — `airNumberDensity`, `tangentRayBending`, `tangentRayAirColumn`, `buildUmbralProfile`, `atmosphereFromClarity`, `UMBRA_ATMOSPHERE_DEFAULTS`, `ATMOSPHERE_TOP_KM = 88`; new singleton node `theLunarEclipse` in `src/nodes/CNodeLunarEclipse.js`, created by `addNightSky()` in `src/nodes/CNodeDisplayNightSky.js`; `MOON_ECLIPSE_GLSL`, the `uEclipse…` uniform block and `_applyLunarEclipse()` in `src/nodes/CPlanets.js`; the `lunarEclipseDimming()` factor in `CNodeSunlight.update()`'s moonlight branch; pre-sprite `syncToObserver` calls in both render paths of `src/nodes/CNodeView3D.js` and in `CNodeDisplayNightSky.update()`; new `docs/LunarEclipse.md` with its `helpDocs` entry (`menuId: "lighting"`) and i18n `menus.help.documentation.lunarEclipse` (*Lunar Eclipses*); `tests/CLunarEclipseCalc.test.js`, 35 tests). Set the time to a lunar eclipse and the Moon is eclipsed — the long soft penumbral gradient, the feathered umbral edge, and the deep red of totality. There is nothing to switch on: the node is created with the night sky, and a new folder of controls appears under Lighting. **Geometry** is astronomy-engine's own `CalcShadow()` reproduced rather than approximated: the same umbral and penumbral cone radii (`shadowRadiiKm`), the same geocentric Moon and aberration-corrected Sun, and the same 88 km atmospheric enlargement of the Earth's opaque radius. Contact times therefore agree with that library's published semi-durations to about a second (the tests bracket them and pin the difference under two, which is as closely as they can be checked — astronomy-engine's own search runs to a one-second tolerance), and the eclipse kind and peak obscuration match to six decimal places. **The soft edges are geometry, not a blur.** For each point on the Moon, `directSunlightAt()` computes what fraction of the Sun's disc the Earth hides using the two-circle lens area already unit-tested as `sunDiskObscuration()`, and puts it through the limb-darkened `eclipseLightFraction()` — both reused from `CEclipseCalc`. The locus where those two discs are internally tangent works out algebraically to the umbral cone radius k, so this is not an approximation to the cone model, it *is* the cone model, with the whole penumbral gradient and the feathered umbral edge falling out of the same expression that produces the contact times. There is no blur parameter anywhere. `MOON_ECLIPSE_GLSL` in `CPlanets` is the per-fragment twin (`eclipseDiscOverlap`, `eclipseLimbFlux`), working from each fragment's true 3-D surface position in the Moon's body-fixed frame, so the shadow's curvature across the disc and the foreshortening of the terminator near the limb are exact rather than a screen-space circle; both use an `atan2` separation and scale by the Sun's angular radius, because in raw radians the lens-area formula cancels catastrophically in 32-bit floats exactly at tangency. **The colour is computed, not tinted.** `umbralLight.js` traces rays grazing the Earth from the ground to 88 km through a US Standard Atmosphere — Rayleigh scattering with the King factor, ozone in the Chappuis band (300 DU nominal), stratospheric and tropospheric aerosol with an Ångström exponent, and a statistical cloud term (`clearFraction`, roughly two thirds of the limb cloudy at any moment) — works out how far each ray is refracted, follows it to where it lands in the shadow, convolves the deposit with the limb-darkened solar disc, and integrates 36 wavelengths from 380 nm in 10 nm steps through the CIE 1931 observer into linear sRGB. The red of the umbra, its darker centre and the turquoise ozone fringe at the umbral edge are consequences of that integration, not settings. The result is a 1-D radial radiance profile uploaded as a 256-sample half-float `DataTexture`, sqrt-encoded so three decades of dynamic range survive and squared on read. **88 km is a seam, not a fudge**: at that altitude a grazing ray's bend displaces it well under a kilometre at the Moon's distance (the tests pin `384400 · tangentRayBending(88) < 1` km) and its transmission is essentially unity, so the same number that reproduces astronomy-engine's contact times also cleanly divides the refracted light below it from the plain geometric shadow above, with no double count and no gap. It is the one genuinely disputed number in lunar-eclipse prediction — the classical alternatives are Chauvenet's 1/50 of the Earth's radius (127 km) and Danjon's 1/85 (75 km) — and `docs/LunarEclipse.md` covers the dispute. **The controls** (all six serialized via `addSimpleSerials`): *Eclipse Shading* (master, default on, a complete no-op outside an eclipse); *Blood Moon Color* (default on; off mixes the refracted term to its own luminance, rendering the same brightness in grey); *Atmospheric Clarity* (0–1, default 0.5) — the single knob `atmosphereFromClarity()` maps onto stratospheric AOD (`0.003 · 80^(1−c)`, log-interpolated because aerosol loading spans two decades), tropospheric AOD (`0.05 · 6^(1−c)`) and cloudiness (`0.82 − 0.34c`), which walks the whole Danjon L0–L4 range from a post-Pinatubo near-invisible Moon to an exceptionally clear coppery one; *Auto Exposure* (default on); *Exposure (stops)* (−4…20, changing it turns Auto Exposure off); *Shadow Outlines* (default off); and a disabled *Eclipse* readout reporting `none`, `Penumbral, pen. mag …`, or `<Kind>, umbral mag …, mV …` plus `, Danjon L…` during totality. **Exposure**: a total umbra is ~10 magnitudes (a factor of 10⁴) below a full Moon, so at true brightness it renders black. `_exposureFor()` puts the *mean* radiance of the shadowed part at the eclipse's deepest phase at `AUTO_EXPOSURE_TARGET = 0.30` — the mean rather than the peak, because the umbral rim is a hundred times brighter than the middle and exposing for the rim leaves the interior black. The gain is cached on the peak time and clarity, so it is keyed to the eclipse EVENT and held for the whole of it: the Moon still visibly darkens as it enters the shadow instead of the picture self-levelling, exactly as a fixed-exposure photo sequence through totality behaves. The sunlit part costs nothing: a branch-free soft shoulder in the shader (`min(illum, 0.8) + 0.2·(1 − exp(−over/0.2))`) rolls illumination off above 0.8 instead of clipping it flat, and is a strict no-op at exposure 1, so the surface texture survives. **Shadow Outlines** rings the umbra in gold (1, 0.843, 0) and the penumbra in orange (1, 0.647, 0) out at the Moon's distance — the same colour convention `CNodeDisplayMoonShadow`'s *Show Moon's Shadow* uses for the Moon's own shadow cone on the Earth, so the two read as a set. Architecturally it mirrors `CNodeEclipse`: a 48×48 tessellated quad in `GlobalSunSkyScene` whose vertices are refracted on the CPU with the same model the Sun and Moon disc shaders use, so it stays registered with the Moon near the horizon, and an analytic fragment shader whose two hairlines are antialiased by `fwidth` so they stay one pixel wide from a whole-sky view down to a close-up.
