A bench row has ONE link, so `handoffCandidateCSVs` sends the consistent band, or the WEAK band when nothing passed the consistency screen — a fallback, not an addition, because a bound-pinned solve standing beside an endorsed one reads as its peer. "Unresolved" was the row most worth opening and the one that arrived carrying only the scenario track. (The live gallery offers the same choice as its two buttons instead.) Track names now come from a readable slug table rather than the hypothesis key — `w_minimum_acceleration`, not `w_plausible`. Keys stay untouched, because they are persisted identity in the exported records and the result cache and code branches on them; display names could not be used either, since a key is a FAMILY and a name is a MEMBER, so per-member naming would split the polynomial sweep into five near-identical tracks. Slug widths were measured against the 132 px dropdown budget so none is clipped.

- **Fixed the derived Truth sub-track of a MISB / FMV file being imported, listed in the menus, and drawn as nothing at all** (`07d97dc8`; `CTrackFileMISB.trackIsTruth` in `src/TrackFiles/CTrackFileMISB.js`, consumed by the existing `isTruthTrack` in `src/TrackManager.js`). `isTruthTrack` tests for a whole name of "truth" or a trailing "(Truth)" — the shapes the BOT importer and the traverse handoff produce — but this file names its derived tracks with a PREFIX, `Truth_<base>`, which matches neither. The answer key therefore fell through to the supplementary branch and was given the small INVISIBLE reference sphere meant for a FrameCenter track. `trackIsTruth()` now says so structurally, since the name cannot, and the track gets the lime icosahedron like a BOT scenario's truth. This is distinct from `isSupplementaryTrack`, which stays true: the truth track genuinely shares a flight with track 0 and must keep out of closest-point-of-approach timing.

- **Fixed BOTBench grading candidates against a ground plane at SEA LEVEL** — **File → File Analysis → *BOTBench...*** (`3c4898a1`; `MIN_GROUND_SAMPLES`, the unconditional `misbFrameCenter` read and the `groundZ` block in `src/analysis/BotBenchIngest.js`). A bulk run has no terrain, so the underground screen (`flatTerrainProbes` in `BotBenchRunner`) grades every FMV candidate against one flat level plane. Sea level is the only answer available with no other information and inland it is badly wrong — over Cheyenne it sits 1,867 m below the real surface, which let every buried candidate through the screen and put the Ground Vehicle and Fixed Point fits on a plane more than a kilometre under the road they were meant to ride. `FrameCenterElevation` (ST 0601 tag 25) / `FrameCenterHeightAboveEllipsoid` (tag 78) is the producer's own terrain height where the optical axis meets the earth, sampled once per record, so `groundZ` is now the MEDIAN of those converted to the dataset's own ENU Z (not geodetic altitude — converting each one properly removes the Earth-curvature drop between the origin and the aim point). The frame center is read UNCONDITIONALLY rather than only on the frame-center pointing path, which is what had thrown the measurement away for gimbal-pointed clips like truck.ts. Guards: fewer than `MIN_GROUND_SAMPLES` (5) falls back to sea level; a median at or above the lowest sensor height is refused outright, since a ground above the aircraft is a broken column; median not mean, because a mean would be dragged by the odd wild center a producer emits when the axis swings off its terrain model. Heights go through the same `haeOf` datum resolver as everything else, so a tag-25 (MSL) center gets the geoid and a tag-78 (ellipsoidal) one does not — mixing them would put the plane out by the geoid height, the very error the block exists to stop. WHAT THIS IS NOT is terrain: it remains one level plane, right for flat ground and wrong by the local relief in a valley or on a slope, and the row records which source it got. Measured on truck.misb.csv: groundZ sea level → 1,904 m, from 711 of 711 rows.

- **Fixed a traverse analysis being pulled off course by HELD frames at the end of its window** — **Traverse → *Analyze Traverse Methods...*** (`f53954f4`, narrowed in `a5cf08a4`; `trimHeldFrames` in `src/TraverseAnalysisData.js`, applied by `analysisFrameRange` in `src/AnalyzeTraverse.js`). A track node holds its last sample for every frame past the end of its data, so a 20 s clip imported into a 30 s sitch ends in 10 s of a sensor parked at its final position. Nothing rejected those frames and they are not neutral: a third of the residual budget then describes an aircraft that stopped dead in mid-air, and every fit is pulled between the real motion and that fiction. Measured on a synthetic balloon clip (20 s at 10 Hz in the default 900-frame / 30 fps custom sitch), the held tail moved the balloon fit from 150 m off truth to 888 m, its angular residual from 0.003° to 0.43°, and the verdict from "consistent with several conventional interpretations" to "Unresolved" — with no warning anywhere. BOTBench never had the problem because it derives its timebase from the file, so this was also most of the apparent BOTBench-vs-live disagreement. The trim is applied in `analysisFrameRange` rather than inside the dataset builder so that the fits, the charts and an applied gallery tile all read ONE window and cannot disagree about which frames were used, and the console states how many frames were dropped and the range actually analysed. The rule keys on POSITION ONLY — the obvious "neither position nor sightline moves" never fires, because the camera-centre LOS keeps rotating through the tail (measured 0.015°/frame against a position frozen to the millimetre) — and a fixed camera is not a held tail, so the rule is "motionless at the END of a window that moves somewhere". Values are copied out of `losNode.v()` before comparing, because several LOS nodes return one mutated object and diffing two of them compares an object with itself (that bug trimmed a 900-frame window to frames 890–899). It never trims more than half a window; that case is reported as `refusedTrim` with a warning that it is a scene problem the analysis cannot cut its way out of. NARROWED BEFORE RELEASE (`a5cf08a4`): the first draft trimmed BOTH ends, and a frozen run means one of two things that position alone cannot tell apart — frames past the end of the track's data, or a sensor that genuinely stood still. A vehicle camera parked for the first half of a clip and then driving would have lost every bearing from the parked half. What separates them is WHERE they can occur: a track holds its last sample past the END of its data by construction, so the artefact is always a tail. Only the trailing end is trimmed now; a parked FINISH is the one case still lost, and it costs bearings taken from a fixed point, which is the geometry that contributes least to a range solution. An interior hold is never touched — cutting one out would splice two moments together and put a false jump in every velocity.

- **Fixed *File → Import* going somewhere different from dropping the same file, while the sitch browser was showing** (`f32ee091`; `importFile` and the new `onAllSelected` parameter of `selectAndLoadLocalFile` in `src/CFileManager.js`, `acceptImportedFiles` in `src/CSitchBrowser.js`). Both routes already went through `uploadDroppedFile`, except with the browser up: a DROP queues the files and loads the custom sitch first, while Import went straight into whatever sat behind the overlay. On a cold start that is "empty", which has no lat/lon, so every track node built against it asserted on the next rendered frame. `acceptImportedFiles` now takes the selection and treats it exactly as a drop on the browser — queue on `pendingDropFiles`, then `_loadCustomSitchForQueuedDrops`. The browser is read ONCE before the picker opens, because it closes itself as soon as the first file is handed over and re-reading it per file would send file 1 down the queued route and the rest down the direct one; and if the browser has closed while the OS dialog was up, the selection is imported the ordinary way rather than being left on the floor.

- **Fixed BOTBench reading and writing the WRONG folder's cache when a second folder was chosen in the same dialog session** — **File → File Analysis → *BOTBench...*, *Folder (Read)* / *Folder (Caching)* / *Flush Cache*** (`a5cf08a4`; `loadDirCache` and `flushCaches` in `src/analysis/BotBenchUI.js`). The per-folder cache records shipped in 2.135.0 were keyed by `dirPath`, which a walk numbers RELATIVE to the folder that was chosen — so the chosen root is always `""`. Picking a second folder in the same dialog handed it the FIRST folder's cache record, handle and writable flag: its results were read from, and written into, the first folder's directory. Both the lookup and the flush are now keyed by handle identity. A list rather than a `WeakMap`, because `flushCaches` has to walk every folder the dialog has touched, which a `WeakMap` cannot be asked to enumerate.

- **Fixed a shipped third-party package losing its license attribution** — **Help → Documentation → *Third-Party Notices*** (`c04d9696`; `COPIED_NOT_IMPORTED` in `scripts/generateThirdPartyNotices.js`). `collectNpmDeps` reads the webpack stats file, so it only sees packages webpack resolved as MODULES. A package that `copy-webpack-plugin` drops into the output verbatim is shipped without ever being imported, is absent from the stats, and so silently lost its attribution in every `--from-stats` run while still being distributed. `@cornerstonejs/codec-openjpeg` — the JPEG 2000 WASM decoder under `libs/openjpeg` — is the case in hand. The list must be kept in step with `webpackCopyPatterns.js`; naming a package that is also imported is harmless, since `bundled` is a Set.

### Documentation

- **Local-only working notes under `docs/` can no longer ship with the app** (`32fbcba9`; `skipDirs` in the markdown walk in `webpack.common.js`, `**/temp/**` in the `docs/` copy in `webpack.standalone.js`). `docs/` is walked by the `MarkdownToHtmlPlugin`, which recurses into subdirectories and emits THREE things per file: the rendered `.html`, the raw `.md` (deliberately, for chatbot access), and any non-markdown file verbatim. Gitignoring a directory under `docs/` therefore does NOT stop it shipping — it only stops it being committed. Both walks now skip `temp`. The UI-redesign working documents (`ARCHITECTURE.md`, `DESIGN-LANGUAGE.md`, `LAYOUT-MODEL.md`, `README.md`, `TODO.md`, `UI-TEST-CHECKLIST.md`) move from `docs/ui-redesign/` to `docs/temp/ui-redesign/`, so they are no longer published as pages in the app's documentation list; the files are unchanged and git history keeps them at the old path. The design-token comment at the head of `src/extra.css.js` is repointed and says where history has them.

### Internal

- **BOTBench M2-BALLOONS generated scenario set (dev-side; no app UI)** (`f96d8375`; `benchmarks/botbench/lib/m2Set.js`, `m2Batch.js`, `m2.bench.test.js`, `npm run bench-bot-m2`; new observation kind in `lib/observation.js`, "light" wind config in `lib/wind.js`, manifest fields in `lib/exportInterchange.js`). A second generated set beside M1 in the same folder tree — `results/m2-balloons/batch_<straight|curve|orbit>/<0.0|0.1|0.5>deg/{Input,Truth,All}/` — 5 behaviours × 4 ranges = 20 variants per folder, 3 platforms × 3 drift levels = 9 folders, 180 scenarios, 1260 files, about a second to generate. THE AXES DIFFER FROM M1 ON PURPOSE: M1 sweeps clip DURATION on its outer axis because a maneuver's detectability is a question about time, but a balloon barely moves, so its detectability is a question about how the SENSOR moves — the outer axis here is the platform path (straight / gentle constant bank / full orbit) with duration pinned at the 20 s a real tracking clip tends to be, flown by a tracking aircraft at 21,000 ft and 130 m/s rather than M1's low orbiter. Two orthogonal behaviour axes cross at one centre scenario: rising/level/sinking vary vertical rate at one wind (+3 / 0 / −2 m/s measured), slow/level/fast vary drift speed at zero vertical rate (2.24 / 6.32 / 21.54 m/s measured), with `level` being both zeroes; `sinking` rides party-rising with a negative ascent rate, because party-neutral pins its rate at zero and cannot express descent. OPERATOR DRIFT IS A NEW OBSERVATION KIND: M1's error ladder is the Aguadilla wobble, a seeded random walk that recentres (zero-mean, the kind of error a fit absorbs), whereas drift is a deterministic one-way ramp reaching the stated angle on sky at the last frame — the kind a fit cannot absorb, because over a short clip it is indistinguishable from the target genuinely drifting. It is DECLARED as what it is: `exportInterchange` emits model `"systematic"`, `correlated: true`, `sigmaDeg = D/sqrt(3)` (the RMS of the ramp) and a note stating the error is not zero-mean, since a solver reading only `sigmaDeg` would apply a weight right for noise and wrong for a bias. `rangeM` is HORIZONTAL range and each manifest row now carries `slantRangeM` and `depressionDeg` beside it, because the platform flies 5.5 km above the balloon and reading "2 miles" as the distance to the target would be wrong by a factor of two and wrong about the geometry entirely (2 miles horizontal is a 6.4 km sightline at 59.6° of depression; 50 miles is 3.9°). Verified against the generated files rather than the labels, including drift reaching 0.0000 / 0.1000 / 0.5000° on sky at the last frame and 201 frames retained in every scenario.

- **Benchmark result trees are deleted with a retry instead of failing half-done** (`718bfc57`; `benchmarks/botbench/lib/resetOutDir.js`, used by `m1.bench.test.js`). `fs.rmSync(recursive)` on a Dropbox-synced working copy throws `ENOTEMPTY` when Finder recreates `.DS_Store` inside a directory while the delete is still walking it — and it throws AFTER deleting most of the tree, so the bench aborts with the set half gone. A half-deleted results tree is indistinguishable from a complete run to anything that reads it: the manifests are valid, the CSVs are valid, there are simply fewer of them. Hit for real on the M1 tree, which came back with two of its four duration folders. `resetOutDir` retries on `ENOTEMPTY`/`EBUSY` and rethrows anything else, since a permissions failure would not improve with another attempt.

## Version 2.136.0 (2026-08-17)

### New Features

- **BOTBench analyses MISB sources that state their pointing as a FRAME CENTER** — **File → File Analysis → *BOTBench...*** (`misbFrameCenter`, `misbHasFrameCenterLL`, and the ECEF pass in `ingestMISBRecords`, `src/analysis/BotBenchIngest.js`). A large family of MISB exports carries no platform attitude and no gimbal angles at all: pointing is stated as the geodetic point the optical axis lands on (ST 0601 tags 23/24 plus 25 or 78). The app already treats that as pointing — `CTrackFileMISB` derives a "Center" track and the camera looks along it — but `misbHasSightline` accepted only SensorRelativeAzimuth/Elevation plus the full PlatformHeading/Pitch/Roll triple, so every row of such a file was dropped and BOTBench refused a file the app opens without complaint. `misbFrameCenter` now extracts and validates the center as `{lat, lon, altHAE, altMSL}`, and the ECEF pass builds the direction as `centerECEF.sub(sensorECEF).normalize()` — sensor to frame center, which is the boresight by definition of what a frame center is. ANGLES WIN WHEN A ROW CARRIES BOTH: the gimbal angles are the measurement and the center is derived FROM them through the producer's terrain model, so the angles are the shorter path with one less model in it. AN ALTITUDE IS REQUIRED, NOT DEFAULTED — tag 78 (already ellipsoidal) preferred over tag 25 (MSL), for the same reason `SensorEllipsoidHeight` beats `SensorTrueAltitude`; a row with a center lat/lon but no height is counted in the new `centerNoAlt` tally and dropped, because choosing a height would invent the elevation angle, which is the one component the caller most wants measured. A center coincident with the sensor position (same lat/lon AND same height) states no direction and is counted as `noSightline` — deliberately not the nadir case, which shares lat/lon but differs in height and survives. Warnings state that a frame-center direction inherits the producer's terrain-model error and that the error is CORRELATED with their geolocation solution rather than independent of it (at 5 km slant range, 100 m of terrain error is about a degree of tilt). Frame-center rows are excluded from the missing-`SensorRelativeRollAngle` count, since a direction built from two positions never uses roll; `centerNoAlt` joins `droppedRows` in `assessSourceQuality`; and a new `record.meta.pointing` records which convention the run used (`"gimbal angles"`, `"boresight (platform frame)"`, `"frame center"`, or `"mixed (N of M by frame center)"`) so a reader comparing residuals across two runs knows what each was built from — it is recorded on the record's meta only, not surfaced as a table column. Because `ingestMISBRecords` is shared, this covers KLV/transport-stream FMV clips as well as MISB-column CSVs. A new `haeOf({lat, lon, altHAE, altMSL})` helper resolves the datum for the sensor, the frame center and truth through one path, so two of them can never end up on different datums and manufacture a fake vertical error.

- **BOTBench analyses STANAG 4676, in both its CSV and its XML container** — **File → File Analysis → *BOTBench...*** (new `toSightlineMISB()` in `src/TrackFiles/CTrackFileSTANAGBase.js`; `sightlineMISB` / `ingestTrackFile` / `ingestSTANAGXML` in `src/analysis/BotBenchIngest.js`; `CSV_TRACK_TYPES` in `src/TrackFiles/TrackCSV.js`). STANAG was refused with "carries multiple track roles (platform/target/ground) and BOTBench cannot choose one", while the app loaded it happily. The roles are not competing candidates for "the sensor": they are the two ENDS of one ray plus the producer's estimate on it, and which is which is stated by the format. `toSightlineMISB()` pairs the platform and ground endpoints of the SAME track point into the frame-center convention (sensor position + FrameCenter position), so the new pointing path above consumes it without inventing a fourth shape — pairing inside the track file rather than asking a caller to re-pair two split tracks by index, which invites exactly the off-by-one that silently rotates every bearing. `CSV_TRACK_TYPES.STANAG_CSV` moves from `pointing: "gimbal"` (which it never was; the multiRole gate refused it before the mis-declaration could bite) to a new `pointing: "endpoints"`, and the `conv.multiRole` refusal is removed altogether — dispatch is now by pointing convention via `sightlineMISB`. STANAG_CSV is the only `multiRole: true` type in the table, so no other format's behavior changes. THE THIRD POSITION IS NOT SCORED AS TRUTH: the producer's own target estimate lies ON this same ray, so it is a solution rather than an independent observation; `toSightlineMISB()` omits it, `record.truth` stays null, and a warning says so explicitly. WHICH ALTITUDE TAGS THE HEIGHTS GO IN IS ASKED OF THE FILE, not hard-coded: STANAG heights are ellipsoidal by the 4676 default, but the XML subclass reads `&lt;dynamics cs="..."&gt;` and reports an EGM/MSL/NAVD file as orthometric, so `isAltitudeHAE()` chooses between `SensorEllipsoidHeight`/`SensorTrueAltitude` and `FrameCenterHeightAboveEllipsoid`/`FrameCenterElevation`. Hard-coding the HAE tags would make such a file skip the geoid conversion and put both endpoints out by N (~19 m in Colorado, up to ~100 m globally) — both ends move together so the DIRECTION barely changes, which makes the wrong sensor position invisible. STANAG CSVs are picked up by a folder sweep like any `.csv`; `.xml` is accepted only through **Choose Files** (`botBenchExplicitFileRole` / `isExplicitlyCollectable`), because XML is a container a folder may hold for a hundred unrelated reasons and sweeping it would put a guaranteed error row in every run — the same failure the mp4/mov exclusion already exists to prevent. New `tests/botbench/stanagXmlIngest.test.js` (jsdom, for `DOMParser`) pins the XML and CSV flavours to identical datasets and pins the orthometric-cs tag choice.

- **BOTBench analyses DJI-style `.srt` telemetry sidecars that carry gimbal angles** — **File → File Analysis → *BOTBench...*** (`ingestSRT`, `srtHasPointing` in `src/analysis/BotBenchIngest.js`; `keepOnlyPointingSRT` in `src/analysis/BotBenchUI.js`). A DJI sidecar can carry per-frame position, platform attitude and gimbal angles, which is a complete gimbal-pointing sightline; it goes through the same `CTrackFileSRT` the live import uses, so the two cannot drift. A sidecar carrying position only refuses about POINTING, the same honest refusal a position-only CSV gets (the repository's own `data/test/DJI_20231217152755_0007_D.SRT` is exactly that case, and a test pins it). A folder walk queues by FILENAME, which is right for every other format here — but `.srt` names both drone telemetry and ordinary subtitles, so this one extension is judged on CONTENT: `srtHasPointing` parses with the same parser the ingest uses (so the walk's answer and the ingest's answer cannot disagree) and the walk drops files with no sightline rather than filling a bulk run with guaranteed error rows. A file the user picks BY HAND skips the check on purpose (`pairSidecars(..., {explicit: true})`) — there, the refusal is the answer they asked for. An unreadable `.srt` during the walk is queued anyway, so the ingest can report the real reason instead of the file vanishing silently.

### Improvements

- **Auto Masking sub-folder** — **Video → Masking → *Auto Masking*** (`18832056`; `createMaskingFolder` in `src/CMotionAnalysisUI.js`). Every automatic control moves into one closed-by-default sub-folder: both *Mask Ground* buttons, the admin AI pair (*[ADMIN] Mask Ground with AI* + *[ADMIN] AI Margin*), *Auto Mask OSD* with its five tuning controls (*Auto Window*, *Auto Threshold*, *Auto Spread*, *Target Color*, *Color Tolerance*), and *Auto Mask Redactions* with its eight parameters. *Enable Mask*, *Edit Mask*, *Brush Size* and *Clear Mask* stay at the top level, so the everyday controls are no longer buried under twenty tuning sliders.

- **Menu search finds MENUS, not just controls, and ranks and reads better** — **Help menu, *Search menus...* box** (`18832056`; `setupHelpSearch` in `src/lil-gui-slider-settings.js`). `collectFromGUI` used to recurse through folders collecting only their controls, so a menu like "Masking" — the very word a user types to find it — was the one item the search could never return. A new `folderItem()` makes the folder itself a result (its `$title` is the element, the folder itself is the `gui`, so opening the chain lands on the menu the user searched for rather than its parent), and top-level menu-bar slots are collected too. Results are ranked in this order: sub-menus before individual controls, then shallowest path first, then an exact name before a prefix match before a mid-string match, then alphabetically — replacing an unordered `filter().slice(0, 20)`. Each row is now two clipped lines (breadcrumb above, name below, folders in blue and bold) with an explicit line-height, and the results box is a flex sibling of the input with an explicit gap, so results no longer overlap the input or each other; the box is `display: none` while empty so the gap leaves no stray band. Tooltips that merely repeat the row's own label are suppressed — most menu entries carry a `title` equal to their name, and a native tooltip repeating the visible text was pure noise floating over the list. Highlighting moves from `highlightController` (a yellow background fill) to `highlightElement` (an absolutely positioned overlay box): the fill only ever worked on control rows by accident, surviving as slivers around their widgets, and flooded a bare folder title until the label was unreadable; an `outline` failed differently, since a row's `.widget` paints above it except in the 4 px of padding at each end. The query and its result list now survive navigating away and closing/reopening Help — only the transient state (the hover highlight, and any menu the search opened behind it) is cleared — so trying successive results no longer means retyping.

- **A BOTBench refusal now names POINTING or POSITION, with per-cause counts, instead of blaming the clock** (`ingestMISBRecords` in `src/analysis/BotBenchIngest.js`). Every refusal below the record loop is about TIMING, and with fewer than two surviving records they all fire: the clock trials need two records to measure an interval, so an empty array reported "Neither UnixTimeStamp nor KLV PES PTS gives a usable, advancing timeline ... this clip carries no timing" no matter how good the timestamps were. A file whose only fault was an unrecognised pointing convention therefore sent the reader after the one column that was fine. A new gate at `complete.length &lt; 2` throws first, stating "this is a POINTING or POSITION problem, not a timing one" and listing how many records had no usable sensor position, how many had no camera pointing (neither the gimbal az/el plus attitude triple nor a frame-center position), and how many stated a frame center with no height for it. The incomplete-pointing warning is likewise rewritten to say a sightline needs EITHER the angles OR a frame-center position.

- **`parseMISB1CSV` stops warning about columns it has already accounted for** (`MISB_CSV_IGNORED_HEADERS` and `MISB_CSV_HEADER_ALIASES` in `src/MISBUtils.js`). "UNHANDLED MISB DATA" exists to surface a tag nobody has mapped yet; a pandas-exported client file fired it four times on columns that are all decided about, which trains the reader to ignore the one warning that matters. The blank header `df.to_csv()` writes for the row index is now known (with `"unnamed:0"` for the same column after a round trip) and says nothing; `"UAS LS Version"` / `"UAS Datalink LS Version"` alias to `UASDatalinkLSVersionNumber` (ST 0601 tag 65), whose full name no exporter writes out — the value is stored verbatim, since `misbTagInfo` does not declare tag 65 numeric; and TIME and PTS are registered as looked-at-and-not-used with a one-line note each. They are NOT mapped to a clock on purpose: a column named TIME duplicates the epoch stamp in some exports and holds a relative clock in others, and mapping it would let a relative clock overwrite a good epoch column whenever it sat to the right of one; PTS carries no declared unit (90 kHz ticks, ms, µs) and is relative, so the era test that classifies an epoch stamp has nothing to bite on — read at the wrong scale it would multiply every speed, acceleration and g-load by a constant nobody would notice. A test asserts a pandas-exported frame-center CSV now produces zero UNHANDLED warnings.

### Bug Fixes

- **Fixed the DJI SRT parser storing every MISB value as a STRING** (`srtNumber` in `src/TrackFiles/CTrackFileSRT.js`). Every field `SRTMapMISB` maps is a numeric MISB tag — position, altitude, platform attitude, gimbal angles — but the SRT text was written straight into the MISB row as a string. Arithmetic coerced them, so tracks drew correctly and the anomaly stayed invisible for as long as nobody type-checked; a consumer doing the check every other parser has earned (`Number.isFinite`, as `BotBenchIngest` does) saw a whole file of unusable rows. Values are now parsed to numbers, with non-numeric text becoming null, matching every other parser in the codebase. A test pins the types on the parser's own output as well as on the ingest.

- **Fixed BOTBench's generic track-CSV path running before the geoid grid was loaded** (`ingestBotBenchEntry` in `src/analysis/BotBenchIngest.js`). The FMV branch awaits `ensureGeoidLoaded()`; the plain track-CSV branch did not, so it ran on whatever happened to be loaded already — right inside the app, where the sitch loads the grid, and wrong anywhere it had not been fetched yet. An MSL altitude with no offset available is taken as an ellipsoid height, putting the sensor out by the local geoid separation (tens of metres, up to ~100 m globally). Both the CSV branch and the new track-file branch now await it, best-effort, with the failure already reported by the existing geoid warning in `ingestMISBRecords`.

## Version 2.135.0 (2026-08-17)

### New Features

- **Column scatter plots in the BOTBench results table** — **File → File Analysis → *BOTBench...*** (`src/analysis/BotBenchUI.js`, scatter mode in `src/nodes/CNodeCustomGraphView.js`). Every numeric column now has a raw-value extractor in `SCATTER_COLUMNS` (Samples, Duration, Baseline, Sweep, CV rcond, Noise ratio, Top |err|, Top range, Top max speed, Top mean alt, Truth/Best rel. sep) — raw from the result row, not parsed from the formatted cell, because `fmtMetres` mixes m/km within one column. Left-clicking a header assigns it to the X axis, right-click Y, middle-click dot size; clicking the same header again clears it, and headers show live `[X]`/`[Y]`/`[size]` markers. The selection plots as a sized scatter in a floating `CNodeCustomGraphView` (id `botBenchScatter`), light-themed so a pasted copy prints, draggable and resizable; the bench dialog is a modal at z-index 10000 and the view manager keeps re-stacking view z-indices, so the view re-asserts `scatterElevateZ = 10001` each render rather than once. Hovering a dot fires `onScatterHover`, which outlines and scrolls to the matching table row; declared-anomalous scenarios plot red, the rest blue — the same meaning as the Target-column flag. The graph side is a new scatter mode on `CNodeCustomGraphView`: `setScatterData({points, xLabel, yLabel, sizeLabel})`, an independent min/max `scatterAutoScale` (the value-X branch of `autoScale()` forces equal aspect — right for spatial pairs, wrong for arbitrary column pairs), sqrt-area dot radii of 3–14 px so dot AREA tracks the size column, largest-drawn-first so small dots never get buried, a hover tooltip with the point's label and coordinates, and a `mouseleave` handler so the last dot's highlight cannot stick.

- **BOTBench per-folder result cache, and a read/caching split of the folder picker** — **File → File Analysis → *BOTBench...*** (`src/analysis/BotBenchUI.js`). Each leaf folder gets a `.botbench-cache.json` (schema 1) holding, per scenario filename, the sha256 of every input that shaped its row — the CSV bytes, the `.scenario.json` sidecar, the `.truth.json` answer key — plus the analysis options as-run and the finished row. On a re-run, a file whose hashes AND options all match is filled from the cache; its Status cell says "cached" with the save date and app version on the tooltip, so a reused row is never silent. The hashes also ride on every row (`row.fileSha256`), so an Export JSON records exactly which bytes produced each result. The cache stores rows, not the in-memory analysis, so a cached row's Gallery/Report buttons are disabled with the reason on the tooltip rather than failing on click. Cache lookup is best-effort: any hashing or read failure falls through to a normal run. "Choose Folder" is now two buttons: **Folder (Read)** picks with `showDirectoryPicker({mode: "read"})` — existing caches are still reused (reading needs no write grant) but none are written — and **Folder (Caching)** picks with `mode: "readwrite"` and writes the cache back after each file. A new **Flush Cache** button deletes the cache file from every folder the dialog has touched, reporting folders whose read-only grant blocked the delete. Drag-and-drop stays cache-inert: its `FileSystemEntry` API is read-only.

- **Open Consistent+Weak — the traverse gallery can hand off the solutions the analysis declined to endorse** — **Traverse → *Analyze Traverse Methods...*** (`showResultGallery` in `src/AnalyzeTraverse.js`; `consistentTrackCSVs` / `candidateNotes` in `src/TraverseHandoff.js`). The gallery's "Open tracks in new window" button is renamed **Open Consistent**, and a second button, **Open Consistent+Weak**, also sends the weak band: candidates that passed the broad screen (`rank &gt;= 1`) but failed the consistency screen — `boundaryLimited` ("pinned at a search bound"), optimizer warnings ("optimizer incomplete"), or a fit tier below the screen. These load as tracks named `w_&lt;key&gt;` beside the `c_` band, because on an "unresolved" file the weak band is often the only thing there is to look at; kinematically-extreme and invalid candidates (`rank &lt; 1`) stay out even here. The one-track-per-family rule spans both bands: ranking is best-first, so a family with a consistent member gets its `c_` track and its weak members are counted in that entry's `alsoRan`, never doubled as a `w_` twin. The sitch Notes gain a "WEAK CANDIDATES IN THIS SCENE" section with each candidate's declining reason in brackets, and set-aside tiles remain excluded from both buttons.

### Bug Fixes

- **Fixed narrow-FOV ground gaps under terrestrial refraction — Google 3D tile selection now accounts for the refraction lift** — **View → Atmospheric Refraction → *Terrain and Buildings*** (`e954e8c7`, flat-mode follow-up `9f894d03`; `FlatAwareTilesRenderer._terrestrialRefractionRetest` in `src/nodes/CNodeBuildings3DTiles.js`). The terrestrial-refraction vertex shader lifts rendered terrain by ~k·d²/2R, but tile selection culled against the UNBENT bounding volumes. At very narrow FOV the lift dwarfs the frame — measured at fov 0.025° on a 36 km sightline (k 0.176): lift ~18 m against a ~16 m frame height — so every tile the bent render needed on screen was, by unbent math correctly, out of frustum, never loaded, and the look view showed a sky-colored band where the ground should be. Stock-rejected tiles are now retested against their OBB translated to the drawn (lifted) position via `liftWorldPoint` — the CPU twin of the shader chunk, so the two cannot drift — expanded by the lift's worst deviation across the tile (evaluated at the near edge, center, and far edge in horizontal range, clamped to the context's `maxLiftM`). It must be the exact OBB: a padded-sphere retest admitted every coarse tile along the sightline's underground chord through the planet and queued 10k+ downloads. The effective k (`resolveTerrestrialK`) is folded into the per-view settle fingerprint so toggling refraction or editing k re-traverses the LOD instead of staying stale until the camera moves; with refraction off the lift context is null and the retest is a strict no-op. Flat-Earth mode keeps refraction (the flat scene hook warps the camera pose first so the chained refraction hook derives its uniforms from the warped pose), so the flat far field lifts the warped sphere with a context built from `flatEarthWarpPoint(camera)` — the warped observer — while the near field keeps the unwarped camera + volumes + lift pair, which a locally rigid warp maps consistently onto what renders.

- **Fixed traverse handoff tracks landing at the start of the clip when the analysis ran on an In/Out (A–B) segment** (`consistentTrackCSVs` and `contextTrackCSVs` in `src/TraverseHandoff.js`, using `clipFrameDate` from `src/TraverseHypotheses.js`). Handoff CSV timestamps were built as `startMs + f/fps`, ignoring `dataset.frame0` — the offset of the analyzed A–B window into the clip — so tracks from a segment analysis opened in the new window timestamped from the start of the clip, out of register with the sitch time. Both the candidate tracks and the context tracks (sensor path, truth) now build their timestamps through `clipFrameDate`, which applies the `frame0` offset, so a handoff from a segment analysis lands in the analyzed window.

### Internal

- **BOTBench benchmark suite (dev-side; no app UI)**: the maneuver-class taxonomy is completed from 10 to 13 kinds — new `straight-cv`, `slow-turn`, and `accel-instant` generators, a `leadIn` option on `highg-turn`, a dive/pull-up `sense` on `hypersonic-glide`, and sustained event windows now emitted by `sine-wave`, `vertical-loop` (clamped to clip end), and `figure-eight` (`benchmarks/botbench/lib/maneuverTargets.js`, `maneuverSet.js`). A new M1 batch (`lib/m1Set.js`, `m1.bench.test.js`, `npm run bench-bot-m1`) sweeps 23 variants × 4 durations (20/60/120/300 s) × 3 operator-error levels (0/0.15/0.3°) = 276 scenarios into `results/m1/` trees with manifests and timing. A `worker_threads` parallel driver (`run-m1-parallel.mjs`, `lib/m1WorkerEntry.js`, `npm run bench-bot-m1-par`) runs the 12 independent batch folders concurrently with byte-identical output to the sequential bench. A new visualization pipeline (`vizBotBench.mjs`, `npm run bench-bot-viz`) renders a results set into a self-contained HTML page — shape gallery, animated scene player, envelope scatter, pointing-error strip, timing — and keeps a `registry.json` run history behind an index page. Scenario filenames now lead with the target part and carry variant suffixes (`lib/exportInterchange.js`; matching field-index fix in `realtracks.bench.test.js`).

## Version 2.134.0 (2026-08-16)

### New Features

- **Global Radius Resize — one control resizes every radius-only marker in the scene** (`f64993b3`; `src/TrackManager.js`, `src/nodes/CNode3DObjectGeometry.js`). Replaces "Target Sphere size ft" in the Objects menu, which was wired to nothing — it fed a `sizeTargetScaled` node whose only consumer had been commented out, so moving it changed nothing on screen. The new `globalSphereResize` `CNodeGUIValue` (0.01–100 m, radius in metres, matching each object's own Radius field) drives `resizeAllObjectSpheres`, which resizes in place via `geometryParams.radius` + `rebuild()` so controllers stay attached. It applies to any geometry whose ONLY dimension is a radius — sphere, ellipsoid, circle, the platonic solids — decided by the new `radiusIsOnlyDimension` in `CNode3DObjectGeometry.js`, which reads the geometry table against the new `NON_DIMENSIONAL_GEOMETRY_PARAMS` set (segment counts, detail, ratios, angles, winding numbers, flags). Listing the non-dimensional side makes the failure safe: a later geometry with an unrecognised length lands on the dimensional side and is left alone, while a capsule (radius AND `totalLength`) or torus (radius AND `tube`) is never deformed. `syncGlobalSphereResize` makes the control FOLLOW the scene — on every `tracksChanged` it takes the largest radius present, written through `setValue`'s `ignoreOnChange` so importing one small object never silently resizes a scene the user already sized by hand; only a drag or click acts. The default marker radius is now the named `DEFAULT_TRACK_SPHERE_RADIUS_M` (40 m).

- **BOTBench rows open in a fresh Sitrec window** (`1105ea7e`; new `src/FileHandoff.js`, `openInNewSitrec` in `src/analysis/BotBenchUI.js`, `buildScenarioNotes` in `src/analysis/BotBenchIngest.js`, receiver in `src/index.js`). The File cell in the BOTBench table (File → File Analysis → *BOTBench...*) is now a link that opens that scenario in a new Sitrec window. It cannot be an ordinary href — a folder-picked or dragged file is an in-memory Blob with no path — so `FileHandoff.js` puts the bytes into the existing `IndexedDBManager` cache (`putFileHandoff`, `HANDOFF_TTL_MS` = 1 hour) and the new window collects them via `?handoff=<key>`, routed through the same importer as a drag-and-drop so a link and a drag stay one code path. One key carries an array of files plus meta in a single transaction, so nothing arrives half-transferred; the record is not deleted on read, so a reload of the receiving window still finds it — only the TTL removes it. The window is claimed synchronously before the store write (popup blockers honour `window.open` only during the click), and the bench opens `action=new` — the neutral custom sitch, since a BOT file carries its own geography. The interchange sidecars travel as PROSE into the sitch Notes panel (`buildScenarioNotes`), because the app's importer has no route for a `.scenario.json` and would report it as an unsupported file; the answer key is a separate labelled Notes section that appears only when a truth sidecar exists.

- **The consistent candidates travel too — from the bench AND the results gallery** (`659bf6e7`; new `src/TraverseHandoff.js`; `src/AnalyzeTraverse.js`, `src/analysis/BotBenchRunner.js`, `src/analysis/BotBenchUI.js`, `src/index.js`). A bulk row or gallery tile says a fit landed 97% of range from truth; it cannot say whether two candidates are 5 metres apart or 5 kilometres, which is usually the question. The handoff now carries the candidates themselves as ordinary CUSTOM1 CSV tracks, and the results gallery (Traverse → Analyze Traverse Methods...) gains an *Open tracks in new window* toolbar button. CONSISTENT means the ranker's `eligible` flag — the same quantity the executive verdict counts; one track per type, named `c_<key>` (`c_quadcopter`, `c_lantern`), with the best-ranked member standing for a multi-member family (the polynomial sweep's five differ only in curvature) and the rest counted in the notes. The gallery additionally excludes set-aside tiles. `TraverseHandoff.js` holds the shared selection/naming/CSV assembly (it cannot live in either caller — `BotBenchRunner` already imports from `AnalyzeTraverse`, so importing back would be a cycle); the three parameters are the frame conversion, the destination, and what else travels. The frame conversion is deliberately NOT shared: the live gallery converts through `unpackTrackToECEF` + `ECEFToLLA_radii` (altitudes HAE), while a BOT scenario uses the importer's own `botENUToLLA` (flat plane, altitudes MSL) — the generic conversion put candidates 40.0 m from a truth track the analysis scored at 2.8 m (geoid separation plus curvature); `botENUToLLA` puts them at 1.8 m, in the scenario's frame by construction. The gallery also sends the sensor path and truth (`contextTrackCSVs`) since a fresh window only gets what the URL names; the bench does not, because its scenario CSV already carries both. Handoff markers are 1 m, and the meta asks for a FRAMING — closest marker spans 3% of the look view's width — computed by the receiver (`applyHandoffLookFraming` in `index.js`), because the angle depends on the receiving window's aspect. Truth is included in the framing (8 of 10 real-arm scenarios are `unresolved` with no passing candidate) and range-blind candidates get no vote. Both the marker resize (`applyHandoffTrackObjectSize`, scoped to the handoff's own objects) and the framing hang off `tracksChanged`, not off the import returning, because `uploadDroppedFile` resolves on file ACCEPTANCE, not track existence — a framing applied at that moment lost the race to sitch setup every time on a two-file handoff.

### Improvements

- **The BOTBench table says what the answer was, what the ranking cost, and when a number cannot be trusted** (`1105ea7e`; `src/analysis/BotBenchUI.js`, `src/analysis/BotBenchIngest.js`, `src/analysis/BotBenchRunner.js`). A run reported a median relative separation of 0.680 with no way to tell whether the fits missed the objects or the ranking discarded answers it already had (it was the second: the closest candidate's median was 0.015). New *Target* and *Platform* columns come from the answer-key sidecar via a named-field allowlist — the generating spec holds `initialHorizontalRangeM`, so range and every give-away field stay off the list; a declared-anomalous scenario is flagged (there, "unresolved" is the correct outcome), sham splices are labelled as sham, and where no sidecar declares the platform it is MEASURED from the sensor path (`describeMeasuredPlatform`) and shown in italics. *|err|* now shows the residual beside its NOISE FLOOR — sigma × sqrt(π/2) (`RAYLEIGH_MEAN`), the residual a perfect track scores against the declared pointing error; the predicted 0.0376° matched all nine measured truth residuals (0.0365–0.0401°), and a residual at the floor cannot carry range. A new *Best* column reports the closest candidate ANY method produced (an oracle ceiling — truth picks that winner), so "found then out-ranked" is visible at a glance. Curve-fit family winners are flagged range-blind on the row and counted in the summary (their distance comes from the search anchor, not the data). *Rate* and *Decl* merge into one *Noise* ratio; the *Probe* column is gone (its useful statement moved to the *Src* tooltip); table cells are now indexed by NAME with a guard asserting the name list matches `TABLE_COLUMNS`, so inserting a column can no longer silently write into the wrong one. The File column no longer front-clips filenames — which left nine of ten generated-scenario rows showing an identical trailing suffix — and the CSV export gains the new fields (`targetDescription`, `platformDescription`, `anomalousDeclared`, `topRangeBlind`, `noiseFloorDeg`, `candidatesBelowFloor`, ...). The summary report drops boilerplate in favour of ranking-cost and noise-floor blocks. One stated limit: generated filenames encode the target and range, and imported tracks are titled by filename — a blind challenge set must be blind in its filenames; a test pins this rather than pretending it is fixed.

- **Track markers are shaded as solid bodies, and 3-D labels match the menu** (`f64993b3`; `src/TrackManager.js`, `src/nodes/CNode3DObject.js`). Imported-track markers now use `material: "phong"` instead of the lambert default — an untextured lambert sphere reads as a flat disc because nothing catches a highlight, which matters most with several markers at different depths. The 3-D label now uses the same middle-truncated short name as the Objects menu, via the new exported `shortObjectName` in `CNode3DObject.js`: the rule existed but was inlined and computed only `menuName`, so an imported track drew its full 90-character filename across the scene while its menu entry showed the tidy version. It is applied to the LABEL text rather than substituting `menuName`, so a caller that deliberately labels an object something other than its name keeps that choice. Also corrected in passing: markers passed `object: "sphere"` to `CNode3DObject`, but `addParams` reads props by parameter name and the parameter is `geometry` — the prop was always inert (unnoticed because "sphere" is the default); fixed at all three call sites.

- **Tgt Start Dist: a usable range, and re-ranging that reaches the ceiling** (`1248e00a`; `src/CSituation.js`, `src/JetStuff.js`). The default `startDistanceMin`/`startDistanceMax` go from 0–80 to 0.01–50 (in the sitch's big units): a floor of exactly zero puts the object AT the sensor — a degenerate case every fit had to defend against — and the old ceiling left most of the slider's travel in ranges nothing is ever solved at. The control's fixed `maxMax: 30` is dropped; it sat BELOW the default ceiling and quietly capped how far the slider could be re-ranged. Omitted, it defaults to `end`, so re-ranging always reaches whatever the sitch declared — including the tighter ranges SitAguadilla and SitGoFast set for themselves.

- **BOT scenarios land on real terrain** (`70705400`; `src/TrackFiles/CTrackFileBOT.js`, `benchmarks/botbench/lib/*`). Every benchmark scenario was generated at 35°N 125°W — hundreds of kilometres out to sea, geometrically fine and useless to look at now that a row can be opened in a window. The generator's new `DEFAULT_SITE` is 37.244358, -120.738187 at 27.6 m MSL (Central Valley farmland), named once so the two literal copies — `readInterchange`'s sidecar fallback and the app's `BOT_DEFAULT_ORIGIN` — derive from it; a mismatch would import the shipped set at the wrong place on the globe. The site comment records the standing datum trap: the same point is -4.9 m HAE (geoid separation -32.5 m), and a conversion that skips it lands tens of metres out. This commit also adds `CTrackFileBOT.trackIsTruth(trackIndex)` — "is this sub-track the answer key", distinct from `trackRoleHint`'s "what should the camera point at" — which the truth-marker work below relies on.

### Bug Fixes

- **Fixed a BOT scenario's ground-truth track being drawn with no visible marker — truth is now a lime icosahedron** (`f64993b3`; `src/TrackManager.js`). A BOT scenario's truth IS a supplementary sub-track (sensor is primary), so it took the supplementary branch's small `visible: false` reference sphere and the answer key was drawn as nothing at all. A new `isTruthTrack` test — checking the name first (`truth` / trailing `(Truth)`), then the structural `CTrackFileBOT.trackIsTruth`, because the marker is built before the file is registered with `FileManager`, so the structural test returns nothing at the only moment it is asked — now runs AHEAD of the supplementary branch, and truth gets a lime (`#32CD32`) icosahedron: unmistakable beside the candidate spheres, still a single-radius solid so it resizes with *Global Radius Resize*. The narrow name test deliberately does not fire on names that are merely ABOUT truth (e.g. "ground_truth_study.csv").

- **Fixed the dropped-file import promise never settling on success** (`89eb0a89`; `importDroppedFile` in `src/DragDropHandler.js`). The promise around the `FileReader` called `reject` on error and nothing at all on success, so for every file that read correctly it stayed pending forever. Every caller was fire-and-forget, so nothing noticed — but `await uploadDroppedFile(...)` never returned, and because the await never came back its `finally` never ran, so `reservedImportNames` kept every name it ever claimed instead of releasing it once the import registered. Now `resolve()` fires in `onloadend`, with a comment pinning what resolution means: the bytes are read and the parse is QUEUED for the main loop, not complete — which is exactly why the new handoff code hangs its follow-up work off `tracksChanged` rather than this promise.

- **Balloon integration states "no geoid here" explicitly instead of inheriting it from a failed fetch** (`c535e6f4`; `src/BalloonPhysics.js`; no production behavior change). `integrateBalloonPositions` converts MSL↔HAE through the EGM96 geoid, whose grid is fetched over the network; under Jest the accessor silently returned 0 with a warning, and the benchmark's flat-plane reproducibility was resting on that fetch quietly failing — anything that made it succeed would have moved every balloon truth track. The function now takes an optional `geoidOffset` (defaulting to the real `meanSeaLevelOffset`, the same injection pattern as `windAt`); flat-plane callers (the benchmark generator's single choke point and the balloon unit tests) pass `FLAT_GEOID` to state the assumption where it is made. `CNodeBalloonTrack` passes nothing and is unchanged, so a genuinely missing await on a production path still warns exactly as before; the MISB test paths mock the real geoid instead of silently getting 0. The generated benchmark set is byte-for-byte identical (manifest hash unchanged).

## Version 2.133.0 (2026-08-16)

### New Features

- **Big slider — rest the pointer on any slider for three seconds and get a full-width one** (`8b831598`; new `src/BigSlider.js` and `src/CValueBox.js`; `_setValueFromX`, `_dragStart`, `_dragMove`, `displayText()` and `_fillPercent()` added to `NumberController` in `src/js/lil-gui.esm.js`; styles in `src/extra.css.js`; `src/nodes/CNodeFrameSlider.js` refactored onto `CValueBox`). Hovering any lil-gui slider for `HOVER_DELAY_MS = 3000` ms pops up a full-width bar near the bottom of the window (`Z_INDEX = 9500` — above the menu bar at 9000/9001 and the frame slider, below the modal dialogs at 10000), for when a hundred pixels of travel is not enough precision. Dragging it drives the very same controller: the pointer-X-to-value mapping, previously a closure locked inside `_initSlider`, now lives on `NumberController` as `_setValueFromX`/`_dragStart`/`_dragMove` and takes the track element as an argument — the small slider passes its own `$slider`, the big one passes its bar, so elastic ranges, wrapping sliders and `wrapReceiver` carries behave identically on both. The read-out box that follows the knob is the frame slider's box, extracted into `CValueBox` and shared; the big slider asks the controller for the same string its input box shows via the new `displayText()`, which also made the log-slider's `updateDisplay` override redundant (removed). Clicking off the bar dismisses it and does nothing else — not automatic, because several document-level capture listeners (the menu bar's close-on-outside-click, the UI logger, the feature manager) would otherwise see the dismissing click. While the popup is up, the pointer events in `SWALLOWED_EVENTS` are intercepted in the capture phase at the **window** (upstream of document) and only re-emitted as a drag on the bar itself; dismissal happens on the click rather than the press, so the whole press–release–click sequence lands on the backdrop. Escape ends a drag cleanly.

- **New Sitch Startup — per-user preferences for how a fresh sitch begins** — **Sitrec → Settings → *New Sitch Startup*** (`bc2ad408`; new `src/StartupDefaults.js` with `applyStartupDefaults()` and `setSitchStartLocation()`; `setupStartupSettings()` in `src/CustomSupport.js`; sanitizer clauses in `src/SettingsManager.js` and `sitrecServer/settings.php` with clamp tests in `tests/SettingsManager.test.js`; `SELECTABLE_UNITS` exported from `src/CUnits.js`; `buildingSourceAvailability()` exported from `src/nodes/CNodeTerrainUI.js`; `custom.settings.startup*` keys in `src/i18n/en.js`). Six settings, saved per user like the rest of the Settings menu: *Units* (Nautical / Imperial/US / Metric / Feet only, via the shared `SELECTABLE_UNITS` so the list cannot drift from the live Units picker), *Use Start Location* (opt-in, off by default), *Start Latitude* / *Start Longitude* (wired through `attachLatLonInputs`, so they accept decimal degrees, D M S, hemisphere letters, MGRS, or a whole "lat, lon" pair pasted into the latitude box; `noSlider()`, snap off so the step never rounds a pasted coordinate), *Start Altitude (m)* (metres **above ground**, 0 = standing on the ground, clamped 0–100000), and *3D Buildings* (the row only appears when `buildingSourceAvailability()` reports a usable Cesium or Google source — the same gate the Terrain menu's buildings toggle uses, now shared by construction). All six go through both sanitizers so they survive the server round trip. They apply **only** to a freshly started `custom` sitch while `!Globals.sitchEstablished`, so named recreations and anything loaded from a save or share link keep their own camera, terrain and units; a `?latlon=` URL parameter is applied afterwards and still wins, and now routes through the same `setSitchStartLocation()` instead of repeating the logic. `setSitchStartLocation()` **replaces** `Sit.TerrainModel` / `Sit.mainCamera` / `Sit.fixedCameraPosition` rather than mutating them, because those objects are shared by reference with the registered sitch definition — mutating one would edit the sitch itself for the rest of the session. Units sit under the same custom-only gate deliberately: a sitch's numbers carry no unit of their own (`CNodeGUIValue.getValueFrame()` returns `Units[unitType].toM * value`, so Gimbal's `startDistance: 32` means 32 NM only because Units is Nautical), and while changing units **live** is safe (`changeUnits()` rescales every node), changing them at **startup** is not — there are no nodes yet to rescale, and 32 NM would quietly become 32 km. Hence `applyStartupDefaults()` runs after the sitch sets its own units and before any node exists.

### Bug Fixes

- **Fixed every sky label in the look view drifting out of place when Match Video Aspect is on — and celestial click-picking missing with it** — **Camera → *Match Video Aspect*** (`a59afa7a`; `src/nodes/CNodeDisplaySkyOverlay.js`, `src/nodes/CNodeView3DMouse.js`). Turning the box on displaced every star, planet, satellite and 3D-object label: a pure radial stretch about the pane centre, worst at the edges, some labels spilling into the black letterbox bars where no 3D is drawn — measured ×1.1626, 19–56 px of error, on a 549×851 pane with a 1536×2048 video. `CNodeDisplaySkyOverlay` re-derived the projection by hand instead of asking for the one the view was rendered with, and got it wrong twice in a way that compounds: it built its camera with `aspect = widthPx/heightPx` while the render uses the video aspect, and it mapped NDC across the whole div while the render only fills the CSS-letterboxed canvas inside it. It survived this long because in the pillarbox case the two errors cancel exactly — only letterbox breaks, and the main view never letterboxes. All three label passes (3D labels, star names, satellite names) now run inside one `withDisplayedCamera()` window and map through `renderedRect()`, the two helpers picking and fit handles already use. That made three hand-rolled camera clones, a hand-mirrored copy of the render's video-pan patch and a `* this.zoom` NDC multiply redundant, and removed an `applyCameraOffset()` that double-applied the tweak `prepareCameraForLOD` already applies; labels now also track y-compress and the display lookAt, which they never did. `displayedCamera()` copies `projectionMatrix` rather than rebuilding it (the pan and y-compress shifts are written straight into the matrix), and `camera` is now a live getter onto `overlayView.camera` so it can never go stale against the occlusion tests. `label.offset` is applied in 2D after projection instead of nudging the 3D position and re-projecting, kept at the historical 0.5× (`offsetScreenPixels` steps NDC by pixels/widthPx and NDC spans 2) so labels in saved sitches do not move. `CNodeView3DMouse` had the same bug inverted — celestial picking projects each candidate forward and compares screen pixels, so it hunted ~45 px from the visible dot and found nothing; `findClosestCelestialObject` is now a `withDisplayedCamera` wrapper around an Inner, with its four mappings routed through `renderedRect`. Verified by intercepting the actual `fillText` calls against an independent projection: max error 0.000 px with the toggle on, off, on + video pan, and on + 1.8× zoom; a click at the dot now picks the satellite it lands on. Still wrong in the same family (pre-existing, deliberately left): `offsetScreenPixels`, `pixelsToMeters` and `metersToPixels`.

- **Fixed stars and satellites changing brightness the moment Match Video Aspect is toggled** — **Camera → *Match Video Aspect*** (`e933a007`; `adjustPointScale()` in `src/nodes/CNodeView.js`, `letterboxScaleY` published by `src/nodes/CNodeView3D.js`, FOV term in `src/nodes/CNodeWaterReflection.js`). `adjustPointScale()` sizes point sprites from two terms and only one tracked the letterbox: `camera.fov` is the rendered (narrowed) field of view, but the pixel height was still the full pane's when the 3D was drawn into a shorter letterboxed target — measured, star and satellite `baseScale` both jumped ×1.1454 on tick. Most stars sit below the point shader's 2 px floor, where scale surfaces as alpha, so the size error was reported as a brightness change. Match Video Aspect narrows the FOV and shrinks the render target together, so the correct answer is exact invariance: `CNodeView3D` now publishes `letterboxScaleY`, the vertical fraction of the render target the match keeps, computed as a ratio of the height before and after the adjustment — deliberately **not** derived from the canvas CSS box, which would cost a forced reflow per view per frame and silently mis-describe scripted-video output (where `ScriptRenderer.renderViewAt` overrides `widthPx`/`heightPx` to the output size while leaving the div at the live pane, so a CSS-derived fraction would shrink every star ~12% in an export). It is exactly 1 when the box is off, and is skipped while XR is presenting. The FOV term becomes the true pixels-per-angle ratio `tan(22.5°)/tan(fov/2)` instead of the small-angle stand-in `45/fov` — required for a sprite to hold its size across a FOV change, and a deliberate global change at every FOV except the 45° reference: narrow views get marginally larger sprites, wide views noticeably smaller (~2.5% at 30°, ~21% at 90°). `CNodeWaterReflection` hard-coded `45/90` for its 90° cube face — exactly where the approximation is worst — so the reflected stars had been ~17% brighter than the sky they reflect; updated to the same tangent ratio. Verified: star and satellite `baseScale` bit-identical across the toggle (ratio 1.00000, was 1.1454). Still open in the same family (pre-existing): `adjustPointScale` ignores `camera.zoom` and yCompress; XR reads `view.camera` rather than the xrCamera; export runs `CPointLightCloud.preRender()` before `fovOverride` is applied.

- **Fixed the equatorial grid drawing over the look view of a new sitch while its own control said off** — **Show → Celestial → *Equatorial Grid in Look*** (part of `bc2ad408`; `showEquatorialGridLook` default in `src/nodes/CNodeDisplayNightSky.js`). The custom sitch set the legacy master flag `showEquatorialGrid: false` but never the per-view look flag, whose default was `true` — so the grid drew over the look view with the *Equatorial Grid in Look* checkbox unticked. The per-view default is now **off** unless the sitch asks for it; sitches that request it explicitly, like Starlink, are unaffected. (The look view is the one matched against a photo or video frame, where a coordinate grid is in the way far more often than it is wanted; the main view keeps its own default.)
