## Version 2.130.0 (2026-08-14)

### New Features

- **Bring Your Own Key (BYOK): one dialog for every credential you supply** — **Sitrec → Settings → *API Keys…*** (`8a7b3e12`, `5b4cb61f`, `6a4fae7f`, `0d457a65`, plus the `adminOnly`/`visibleProviders()` gating in `df6cdd6c`; new `src/BYOKProviders.js`, `src/BYOKKeyDialog.js`, `src/BYOKUsage.js`, +149 in `src/BYOKKeyStore.js`, new `docs/APIKeys.md`, `custom.settings.apiKeys.{label,tooltip}` and `menus.help.documentation.apiKeys` in `src/i18n/en.js`, new `tests/BYOKKeyStore.test.js` and `tests/BYOKUsage.test.js`). `src/BYOKProviders.js` is a registry — `BYOK_PROVIDERS`, grouped by `PROVIDER_CATEGORIES` into *AI assistant*, *Maps &amp; terrain* and *Data feeds* — where each row declares its auth shape (`key`, `userpass`, `none`), what the key unlocks, how usage is metered, and which `LIMIT_DEFS` apply, so adding the next provider is a table entry rather than new UI, new storage and new usage plumbing. `showKeyDialog()` renders straight from that registry with `textContent` throughout and **never displays a stored secret, not even partially** — each row shows only a *Set* / *Not set* badge, and the entry field is `inputType: 'password'` and is never prefilled with the stored value (an earlier iteration showed the last four characters and was removed, because `CSitrecAPI.getMenuSummary()` enumerates lil-gui labels into the system prompt that is POSTed to `chatbot.php`, which is exactly where key material must not travel). Storage is `IndexedDB` under `byok_&lt;id&gt;` via `src/BYOKKeyStore.js`, and values are wrapped by an AES-GCM envelope tagged `sitrec-obf-v1:` so the store holds an opaque blob rather than a recognisable `sk-ant-…` string. That is **obfuscation, not encryption** — the passphrase ships in the public bundle — and it is stated as such in the docs and in the code: it covers the accident cases (a screenshot of the storage inspector, a profile backup, a pasted support dump), not anything running on the page. WebCrypto was chosen over a hand-rolled XOR because it is the same amount of code and gives a self-checking envelope, so a corrupted value fails loudly instead of yielding garbage that would then be sent to a provider as a key; values written before the envelope existed still read and re-wrap on the next save. `primeKeyCache()` populates a synchronous cache at startup because terrain and tile code reads a provider key on a synchronous construction path and cannot await IndexedDB; `0d457a65` then derived `Globals.hasByokKeys` from that one call's count rather than a second `hasAnyKey()` read, keeping this historically timing-sensitive path to one await and one read. Four registry rows — `mapbox`, `maptiler`, `spacetrack`, `adsbx` — are registered and fully functional as far as storage, usage and limits go, but nothing reads their key yet, so they carry `adminOnly: true` and `visibleProviders()` hides them from non-admins; offering them would invite a user to paste a credential that then does nothing.

- **Run the AI assistant on your own Anthropic key** (`8a7b3e12`, refined by `6a4fae7f`; `BYOK_PROVIDER = 'byok-anthropic'` and `BYOK_MODELS` in `src/CDirectLLMClient.js`, `sendToLLMDirect()` in `src/nodes/CNodeVIewChat.js`, `updateChatModelSelector()` and `showApiKeyDialog()` in `src/CustomSupport.js`). With an Anthropic key stored, three new entries appear in **Sitrec → Settings → *AI Model*** (and in the Assistant view's header menu, which mirrors the same controller): *Claude Opus 5 (your key)*, *Claude Sonnet 5 (your key)* and *Claude Haiku 4.5 (your key)*. Choosing one routes the conversation browser-direct to Anthropic through `CDirectLLMClient.chat`, bypassing `chatbot.php` entirely; the distinct `byok-anthropic` provider token means that is always an explicit user choice and never silently moves an existing server user onto their own card. Token counts and cost are recorded per model by `src/BYOKUsage.js`, **banked at the rate in force when the tokens were spent**, so a promotional rate lapsing cannot retroactively reprice past turns. The BYOK path deliberately does not POST to `logNLU.php` — a user who supplies their own key is asking to talk to the provider, not to us. Removing the key resyncs everything: `showApiKeyDialog()` passes a per-change callback into the dialog **and** runs it again on close (`6a4fae7f`), so clearing a key no longer leaves `Globals.hasByokKeys` true with the dropdown still offering "(your key)" entries backed by nothing, and a `chatModel` still pointing at `byok-anthropic` after its key is gone is reset to a server model rather than leaving the assistant aimed at a provider we have no credential for. This half needs the assistant to be enabled: `scripts/serverlessClientEnv.js` forces `CHATBOT_ENABLED=false`, so in serverless and desktop builds the chat view hides itself (`src/nodes/CNodeVIewChat.js:32`) and an Anthropic key stored there currently has nothing to drive — the *API Keys…* dialog itself is deliberately **not** gated on `CHATBOT_ENABLED`, because terrain and data keys matter just as much in a build with no assistant.

- **Run Google Photorealistic 3D Tiles and Cesium Ion on your own key, with your own limits** (`5b4cb61f`, `6a4fae7f`; `providerCredential()` in `src/nodes/CNodeTerrainUI.js`, `trackGoogle3DRootSession()`/`trackCesiumOSM3DBytes()` in `src/TileUsageTracker.js`, `isProviderBlocked()` enforcement in `src/GooglePhotorealisticTilesAuth.js`, `recordProviderUsage()`/`estimateProviderSpendUSD()` in `src/BYOKUsage.js`). `providerCredential(byokId, sharedValue)` prefers the user's own key over Sitrec's shared one and reports `isOwn`, which matters beyond bookkeeping: the `canUse3DBuildings` permission exists to protect Sitrec's **shared** key, so a user spending their own money is no longer gated by it. The billing model is taken from what the server already models rather than guessed — Google bills Photorealistic 3D Tiles **per session**, one request to `/v1/3dtiles/root.json` with every tile afterwards riding on it for free (which is why `tile_usage.php` caps `google_3d_root` daily at 30/60/120 by tier while leaving `google_3d_tiles` audit-only), and Cesium OSM is metered in **bytes**. The two `LIMIT_DEFS` follow suit: `dailyRootSessions` ("Max Google 3D sessions per day") and `dailyBytes` ("Max Cesium data per day", entered in MB and scaled at the enforcement point). A per-tile cap — which this first had — would have throttled rendering without touching the bill. Enforcement sits at the root-tileset **cache miss** in `SharedGoogleCloudAuthPlugin`, the exact point where a new billable session would be minted, so an already-loaded view keeps working on cache hits and only new sessions are refused, with an error naming where to raise the cap. With a key set, sessions and bytes are counted **locally and not reported to `tile_usage.php`**: they consume none of Sitrec's shared quota, should not count against it, and the user's own usage is not Sitrec's business. That local counting deliberately ignores `isServerless`, since a user on their own key in a serverless build is exactly who needs the figure. No default tile prices are shipped — pricing varies by plan, region and free allowance — so each provider declares its own rate denomination (`rate.label`: per 1000 sessions for Google, per GB for Cesium, per 1000 requests elsewhere, replacing a generic "per 1000 &lt;unit&gt;" that produced the meaningless "per 1000 bytes"), and with no rate entered the dialog shows counts and no dollar figure rather than inventing one. `6a4fae7f` also fixed `estimateProviderSpendUSD` reading `usage.requests` where `recordProviderUsage` writes `usage.total`, which made every estimate come out as exactly `0` however the rate was set.

- **The look view's clock is now optional, and it and the compass are mirrored into the Look menu** (`0c2b58ea`; `Globals.showTimeDisplay` and `addTimeDisplayMenu()` in `src/UIHelpers.js`, `visible` on `CUIText` and the skip in `CNodeViewUI.renderCanvas` (`src/nodes/CNodeView.js`, `src/nodes/CNodeViewUI.js`), `this.showHideController` on `CNodeView` published by `CNodeCompassUI`, `compass` and `timeDisplay` slots in `src/ViewUIBarMenus.js`, `timeDisplay.{thing,tooltip}` and `viewMenus.{compass,timeDisplay}` in `src/i18n/en.js`, `showTimeDisplay` added to `globalsNeeded` in `src/CustomManagerSerialize.js`). The two-line UTC + local date/time readout `AddTimeDisplayToUI` puts over the look view was unconditional — a sitch either had it forever or (like FLIR1) never. It is now **Show → *Time Display in Look*** (label composed at runtime by `viewControlLabel(viewId, t("timeDisplay.thing"))`, because the overlay follows whichever view the sitch attached it to), mirrored via `.shareAs(viewMenuKey(viewId, "timeDisplay"))` into that view's own header menu as **Look → *Time Display*** — the same controller, not a second copy of the flag. Defaults ON, so every existing sitch renders exactly as before, and the row is created inside `AddTimeDisplayToUI` so a sitch with no clock gets no toggle. Visibility lands on the **text element**, not the node: `labelVideo` is one overlay canvas that different sitches load with different content — the clock, plus the alt/az/pitch lines from `arrayDataPTZ` in Folsom Lake — so `setVisible(false)` on the node would take the PTZ readouts down with it. `CNodeViewUI` therefore runs each element's update callback **first** and only then skips drawing a hidden one, because the clock lines decide their own visibility in that callback and testing first would latch them off with nothing left to turn them back on. Both lines read `Globals.showTimeDisplay` every frame rather than being switched by the menu's `onChange`, so the menu, a restored save and the API all take effect with no refresh hook to remember; `showTimeDisplay` joins `globalsNeeded`, and because `finishDeserialization` runs after the sitch is set up, a saved `false` wins over the per-sitch default of `true`. The compass needed no new state at all — it is a `relativeTo` child of its host view, so it already had a **Show → Views** row; `CNodeView` now keeps that as `this.showHideController` and `CNodeCompassUI` publishes it under its host view's key, giving **Look → *Compass***. Only `lookView` requests the slot, so `compassMain` is unaffected.

### Bug Fixes

- **Fixed zooming and ground picking converging on empty air over Google Photorealistic 3D tiles** (`df6cdd6c`; new `intersectDisplayed()`/`gatherDisplayed()` in `src/raycastGround.js`, replacing `raycaster.intersectObject(group, true)` in `raycastLocalGround()`). Three.js's raycaster ignores `.visible`, and `3DTilesRenderer` keeps every loaded tile in the scene graph, hiding the LOD levels it is not currently showing by clearing `visible` on their tile group. A coarse ancestor tile spans a whole region on a few hundred vertices, so it interpolates a basin floor from the high ground around it — over Los Angeles one sat **1.66 km above** Torrance airport. As the nearest hit, that invisible tile won every pick, and because zoom dollies *toward* the picked point, cutting the remaining distance by a fixed fraction per notch, the camera converged on a point in mid-air and the airport never got any closer; from the outside it looked like something was in the way. `intersectDisplayed()` is Three.js's own `intersectObject` walk plus a `.visible === false` prune, so only geometry the renderer is actually drawing can be picked. This is a **correctness change, not a speed one** — measured over the Torrance tiles (339 displayed meshes, 206 hidden) a ray costs ~0.044 ms through `intersectObject` and ~0.055 ms through the pruning walk, because the BVH rejects a hidden tile about as fast as the traversal skips it. An earlier revision of this entry claimed the prune was also cheaper; it is not. This fixes every consumer of `raycastLocalGround()`: `CameraControls` zoom and drag, `CNodeView3DMouse` picking, `GroundPaintBrush` mask painting, `C3DSynthManager` placement, `CNodeCamera`'s orthographic ground fit and ground-track switch, and `CSitrecAPI`'s world-point picks.

- **Fixed the *Show Filename* setting never being saved to your account** (`6a4fae7f`; `sanitizeSettings()` in `sitrecServer/settings.php`, new `tests/settingsAllowlistParity.test.js`). The settings allowlist exists twice — `sanitizeSettings()` in `src/SettingsManager.js` and again in `settings.php` — and `showFilename` was only ever added to the browser one when the feature shipped in **2.65.0**, so it was silently discarded on the way to the server and fired the `key in serverSettings` assert on every settings save. The failure mode was quiet: the setting worked locally, saved without error, and simply never followed the user to another browser or device. Both files carry a comment saying "you must update BOTH" and nothing enforced it, so `tests/settingsAllowlistParity.test.js` now compares the two lists in both directions and additionally asserts each parsed list is non-empty, so a reformat that breaks the parsing fails loudly instead of trivially passing against two empty sets (verified to report `showFilename` with the fix reverted).

- **Fixed every tool result reaching the assistant as `{}` on the server chat path** (`8a7b3e12`; `handleAPICalls` in `src/nodes/CNodeVIewChat.js`). `CSitrecAPI.handleAPICall` is `async`, but the chat view called it without `await` and pushed `result.result ?? result` — with `result` a pending Promise, `result.result` is `undefined`, so the Promise itself was pushed and `JSON.stringify` rendered it as `"{}"`. The model therefore saw an empty result for every function it called, on both the initial pass and the recursive follow-up. `handleAPICalls` is now `async` and awaited at all three call sites.

### Security

- **The assistant now asks before making changes in a sitch you opened from someone else's link** (`df6cdd6c`; new `src/SitchProvenance.js` and `tests/sitchProvenance.test.js`, `_confirmWriteInExternalSitch()` and the extracted `TRANSIENT_CALLS` / `CHAT_READ_ONLY_CALLS` in `src/CSitrecAPI.js`, provenance classification at the `?custom=` load site in `src/index.js`). `?custom=` accepts **any** URL with no allowlist — that is how recreations get shared — which means a sitch's Notes, track names, object titles and graph labels can be written by whoever sent the link rather than by the person who clicked it, and those strings reach the assistant's context. The trust decision therefore belongs to the **sitch**, not to any one field: `classifyProvenance({resolvable, ownerId, viewerId})` marks a load `EXTERNAL` when the `?custom=` value is an arbitrary URL, or is a Sitrec-hosted object owned by a different user (being on our own storage says who paid for the bytes, not who wrote the words). Two rules are load-bearing and documented in the module: provenance is derived **only from the delivery channel, never from the sitch payload** (a serialized `trusted: true` would be written by the attacker), and it is runtime-only state that is never persisted or serialized. Under an external sitch, reads run completely untouched — `CHAT_READ_ONLY_CALLS` covers every getter plus recoverable view changes (camera, time, layout, playback), so the workflow this exists to protect, opening a shared recreation and asking the assistant about it, gains no friction at all. Anything that changes saved state or sends data outward raises a `showChoice` dialog offering *Allow once*, *Trust this sitch* (session-only, never persisted) or *Don't allow*, and a refusal is phrased so the model reports it and stops rather than retrying around it. `CHAT_READ_ONLY_CALLS` is `TRANSIENT_CALLS` minus exactly one entry: **`getShareLink`**, which is transient for serialization but **uploads** the current state and returns a public link — under an untrusted sitch that is the propagation step, where steering the model into sharing makes the victim's own browser mint the artifact the attacker wanted. `File → Open Local Sitch` is deliberately treated as local, and the reasoning (a file picker carries no signal distinguishing your own saved work from an attachment, and any marker written into the file would be attacker-writable) is recorded in the module so it reads as a decision rather than an oversight.

- **Sitch text handed to the assistant is now explicitly fenced as untrusted** (`df6cdd6c`; `fenceUntrustedText()`, `UNTRUSTED_TEXT_MAX` and `CHAT_FENCED_RESULT_FIELDS` in `src/PromptSafety.js`, `_fenceUntrustedResultFields()` in `src/CSitrecAPI.js`, a new UNTRUSTED CONTENT paragraph in `sitrecServer/chatbotSystemPrompt.txt`, +40 in `tests/promptInjectionDefenses.test.js`). `getNotes`'s `text` field — whatever the sitch's author typed — is wrapped in a delimiter carrying a random 8-hex token, so injected text cannot close the fence and continue outside it by typing the closing marker, and is capped at `UNTRUSTED_TEXT_MAX` (32,000 characters) so a hostile sitch cannot flood the context window or, on the BYOK path, the user's own token bill. The shared system prompt now instructs the model that such text is evidence to read, quote and analyse — never an instruction, never a reason to call a function — and that if it appears to ask for an action the model should quote it and let the user decide. Fencing is applied to chat-sourced calls only; a UI or MCP caller gets the raw value. The code is explicit that this is **advisory** and that the boundary which actually holds is the capability gating above — it is here because it reliably catches the low-effort majority at no UX cost.

- **Closed four bypasses of the chat URL guard** (`b2fcaa0b`; `src/PromptSafety.js`, `src/CDirectLLMClient.js`, +67 in `tests/promptInjectionDefenses.test.js`, new triage rule in `scripts/security-scan-ai-surface.mjs`). The deny-list that stops a model-chosen URL ever being fetched is the load-bearing boundary here, and follow-up review of `8a7b3e12` found four ways past it. (1) `CSitrecAPI._normalizeMediaSource` strips a leading `!` and `data/` before use, and a leading `!` is not a URL scheme — so `!https://evil.example/x` resolved as a same-origin relative path, passed the guard, and was then peeled back to the external URL by the callee; the guard now applies the same normalization before the origin check. (2) `isSameOriginOrRelative` returned `true` for any non-string on the reasoning that a non-string is not a URL — but the browser coerces, `String(["https://evil/x"])` is the bare URL, and both `TextureLoader` and `img.src` accept it; any present denied param that is not a same-origin string is now refused. (3) `importMedia` is the same primitive as `createSynthOverlay` on a sibling that fetches immediately via `newVideo()`, and honours `filename` and `url` aliases its own doc string does not mention, so all three names are now covered. (4) `updateSynthElement({patch:{imageURL:…}})` never touches a top-level `imageURL`, so a flat (function, param) list could not see it — the deny-list now takes **dotted paths**; that one does not fetch immediately but persists on the node and fires on the next texture load, surviving a save and reload. Also fixed: the JS prompt parser returned `""` for a present-but-empty `@@SECTION` while PHP failed closed with a 500, so a truncated deploy would fail safely on the server and quietly ship a prompt with a hole in the browser — both now throw. A new CI rule enumerates every LLM-callable function taking a URL, file or path and fails on any that is not triaged as denied, `llmCallable:false`, or reviewed-safe with a stated reason, making a new exfiltration primitive a deliberate act rather than an oversight.

- **Fixed menu labels being written as HTML** (`8a7b3e12`; four `innerHTML` sinks changed to `textContent` in `src/js/lil-gui.esm.js`, new `tests/lilGuiXssPatch.test.js`; `sanitizeLabelForPrompt()` in `src/PromptSafety.js` applied in `CSitrecAPI._getControlSummary`). lil-gui wrote GUI labels with `innerHTML`, and those labels carry untrusted data — track names from a loaded KML or CSV, titles from a sitch fetched via `?custom=&lt;any URL&gt;` — so a shared link could run script on the Sitrec origin, which now holds provider API keys. All four data-derived sinks use `textContent`. The same untrusted labels are interpolated into the model's system prompt, so `sanitizeLabelForPrompt` flattens line separators (including U+2028/9, which are invisible in an editor) and caps length before folder titles, control names and option values reach `getMenuSummary()`.

- **A partial Content-Security-Policy** (`5b4cb61f`; `HtmlWebpackPlugin` meta in `webpack.common.js`): `object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self'; form-action 'self'`, each checked against the codebase first — Sitrec creates no `&lt;object&gt;`/`&lt;embed&gt;`, never sets a `&lt;base&gt;` tag, and posts no forms off-origin. `base-uri` matters most: an injected `&lt;base&gt;` silently repoints every relative URL on the page, turning small HTML injection into full script control. `script-src` and `connect-src` are deliberately **not** set and the reason is recorded in the config and in `docs/APIKeys.md`: `connect-src` cannot be restricted while `?custom=&lt;any URL&gt;` loads a sitch from an arbitrary origin and map tiles come from a long, growing host list, and `script-src` would need `unsafe-eval` anyway for Scripted Video's `AsyncFunction` and OpenCV's WASM. The directive that would actually contain an exfiltration is blocked by a feature, not by effort; tightening it needs the arbitrary-URL sitch loader reworked first.

### Documentation

- **New `docs/APIKeys.md` — "Your API Keys: where they are stored and how they are protected"** (`5b4cb61f`; linked from the *API Keys…* dialog as *Details…*, registered in `src/docsRegistry.js` under the Advanced section as **Help → Documentation → *Your API Keys: Storage &amp; Security***). Covers where keys are stored, where they are not, which provider each one is sent to, and what protects them — and, as a deliberate section of its own, what does **not**: browser extensions, the limits of the at-rest obfuscation, and the partial CSP above. It carries a `chatDesc`, so the assistant reads this page to answer "is it safe to enter my key" rather than improvising, and it recommends scoping the key and setting a spending cap at the provider.

### Internal

- **The assistant's system prompt now has a single source of truth** (`8a7b3e12`; new `sitrecServer/chatbotSystemPrompt.txt`, parsed by both `sitrecServer/chatbot.php` and `src/CDirectLLMClient.js`, inlined for the browser by an `asset/source` rule in `webpack.common.js`, cross-checked by `scripts/security-scan-ai-surface.mjs`). The prompt prose lives once as `@@SECTION` blocks; only genuinely dynamic formatting (the menu and doc loops in `buildSystemPrompt`) stays in code. It sits under `sitrecServer/` because that directory is copied wholesale into every deployed build and `COPY`d in the Dockerfile, while webpack inlines it for the serverless and desktop builds, which have no `sitrecServer/` at all. The two previously hand-synced copies had already drifted — the browser copy was missing the camera point-vs-lock rules, the multi-part-request rule, the entire "[Tool Results]" handling section and the help-doc link instruction. Both parsers use the same explicit `(?:^|\n)` anchor, because JS's `/m` also matches after a lone CR and after U+2028/9 while PCRE's does not, and a CI job asserts the PHP and JS parsers still agree.

## Version 2.129.2 (2026-08-14)

### Bug Fixes

- **Fixed the Assistant header's *AI Model* drop-down closing itself the instant it opened** (`fbfbd37d`; one early return added to the `click` handler registered on `this.div` in `CNodeViewChat`'s constructor, `src/nodes/CNodeVIewChat.js:227`). The Assistant view's header menu mirrors the Settings control — `mirrorMenuItem('chatModel', m, {name: 'AI Model'})` in `CNodeViewChat.addTabButtons` (`src/nodes/CNodeVIewChat.js:81`), against `this.chatModelController`, published with `registerMirrorSource("chatModel", ...)` in `src/CustomSupport.js:603` — so the affected control had existed for exactly two releases (the per-view header menus shipped in 2.129.0, their width fix in 2.129.1). Clicking it flashed the option list up and shut it again, while the same control at **Sitrec → Settings → *AI Model*** worked normally. A native `&lt;select&gt;` opens its list on **mousedown**, but the `click` event fires later, on **mouseup**, and bubbles. `CUIBar` appends its bar to the view's host div (`host.appendChild(bar)`, `src/CUIBar.js:59`), so a click on the header bubbles into the chat view's own `click` handler, which focuses `this.inputBox` for any click that is not `this.closeButton` or `this.newChatButton` — and `inputBox.focus()` blurred the `&lt;select&gt;`, which is precisely what closes an open drop-down list. Measured in a built tree before the fix: focusing the header's `&lt;select&gt;` and dispatching a bubbling `click` on it moved `document.activeElement` from `SELECT` to `INPUT.cnodeview-input`. The Settings copy was never affected because it lives in a docked menu-bar GUI under `#menuBar`, a sibling of the views, so its clicks never pass through a view's div. The guard is a single `this.uiBar.bar.contains(e.target)` because `CUIBar.addMenu` builds the dropdown (`gui.$children`) as a DOM *descendant* of the bar even though it is `position: absolute` and paints outside the bar's box — the same property that lets `CUIBar`'s own document-level `pointerdown` close handler get away with one `contains()` — so the one test covers the title, the icons and every row of an open menu. Deliberately **not** fixed at the `CUIBar` end, where `mousedown`, `mouseup`, `dblclick` and `contextmenu` are already swallowed at the bar (`src/CUIBar.js:66`): adding `click` to that list would also stop the document-level `click` listener registered at `src/lil-gui-extras.js:2985`, which dismisses a right-click context menu on an outside click, leaving context menus stranded open whenever a view header was clicked. Verified after the fix by counting calls to `inputBox.focus` (the call itself no-ops in an unfocused automation tab, so the count is the observable): clicking the *AI Model* select makes **0** calls, down from 1; clicking the chat body still makes 1, unchanged; clicking the "Assistant" menu title makes none.

## Version 2.129.1 (2026-08-14)

### Bug Fixes

- **Fixed the per-view header menus each opening at a different width** (`src/CUIBar.js`, `CUIBar.addMenu()`: `gui.$children.style.width = 'var(--width, 245px)'` replacing `min-width: 180px`, which arrived with the header menus in `28188b7a` and shipped in 2.129.0). The docked global menus are plain lil-gui roots in `#menuBar` slots (`CGuiMenuBar`, `src/lil-gui-extras.js`), created with no width option, and lil-gui's own stylesheet sizes `.lil-gui.root { width: var(--width, 245px) }` (`src/js/lil-gui.esm.js:1875`) — nothing in Sitrec sets `--width`, so every docked dropdown is 245px, inherited from the root box its in-flow `$children` fills. A header menu cannot inherit that. `addMenu` deliberately overrides the ROOT to `width: max-content` so the title tab fits its own text — at lil-gui's 245px the title overflows a narrow view's bar and shoves the pin and close icons off the right edge — and the dropdown is `position: absolute` so it is out of that flow. It was therefore shrink-to-fit on its own content with only `min-width: 180px` as a floor, and *Main*, *Look* and *Video* each came out as wide as their own longest row. The dropdown now asks for the width from the same source the docked menus take it from, instead of inheriting it, so it matches them exactly (measured 245px against the Terrain menu's 245px in a built tree) and still follows a `--width` override should a theme ever set one. Nothing else moves: `DROPDOWN_MIN_PX` (80) is unrelated — it clamps dropdown *height* in `fitDropdownToWindow` — and `chromeRect()` measures the live `$children` rect, so the HUD clip-path column (`hudClipPath()`, `CNodeView._clipHUDsBelowHeader`) tracks the new width with no further change. `tests/CUIBarChrome.test.js`, `tests/ViewUIBarMenus.test.js` and `tests/MenuMirror.test.js` pass unchanged; none assert the dropdown width.

## Version 2.129.0 (2026-08-12)

### New Features

- **Per-view header menus, mirrored from the global menus** (`c7197d0b`, merged as `386a1b2b`; new `src/ViewUIBarMenus.js` exporting `viewMenuKey()`, `FRIENDLY_VIEW_NAMES`, `viewControlLabel()`, `VIEW_UIBAR_FOLDERS`, `VIEW_UIBAR_MENUS` and `populateViewUIBarMenu()`; +439 in `src/MenuMirror.js`, now a lil-gui extension exposing `Controller.shareAs(key)`, `Controller.mirrorTo(gui)`, `GUI.addMirror(key)` and `GUI.mirrorFolderFrom(folder)`; new `src/GUIRootRegistry.js`; `hasOpenMenu()`, `chromeRect()`, `closeMenus()`, `fitDropdownToWindow()` and the exported `hudClipPath()` in `src/CUIBar.js`; `populateViewUIBarMenu()` and `_clipHUDsBelowHeader()` wired into `CNodeView.createViewHeader`/`_updateHeaderShown`; new `viewMenus.*` i18n block in `src/i18n/en.js`; new tests `tests/ViewUIBarMenus.test.js`, `tests/MenuMirror.test.js`, `tests/CUIBarChrome.test.js`, `tests/GUIRootRegistry.test.js`, `tests/perViewLayerMask.test.js`; user docs in `docs/UserInterface.md`). Each big view's `CUIBar` title menu — **Main**, **Look**, **Video** — was already created but always empty, so it never opened. It now holds the controls that affect only that view. **Nothing is re-implemented**: every row is a `MenuMirror` twin of the existing Show/View/Video/Camera controller, so there is one piece of state, one `onChange`, and nothing new serialized. The two halves are decoupled and order-independent — the creation site publishes itself with a chained `.shareAs(viewMenuKey(view, slot))` (see `CNodeLabels3D.setupMeasurementUI`, `CNodeDisplayNightSky`, `CNodeDisplaySkyOverlay`, `CNodeDisplayCameraFrustum`, `CNodeViewCanvas`, `CNodeVideoView`, `CNodeVideoViewFilters`, `CNodeVideoInfoUI`, `CNodeAnnotateOverlay`, `CNodeView3D`, `CMotionAnalysisUI.createMaskingFolder`, `CustomManagerSetup`, `SituationSetup`), and `VIEW_UIBAR_MENUS` here declares the ordered contents, so a control built late in the sitch load (the night-sky overlays, the video Rotation dropdown) drops into its declared slot when it appears, and a slot whose source the sitch never creates simply has no row. `placeInOrder()` re-inserts each twin at its registry index because rows arrive in load order, not registry order. Sub-folders (`Night Sky`, `Video Overlay`, `Adjustments`, `Masking`) are pre-created **hidden** and revealed by the `onMirror` callback only once something lands in them, and `hasVisibleItems()` keeps a menu with nothing visible from opening at all. Header labels are deliberately short (`viewMenus.&lt;slot&gt;` in `en.js`) because the menu you opened already names the view; tooltips are inherited from the source, so the long-form text is one hover away. Supporting UI work: only one menu per bar may be open, a capture-phase `pointerdown` closes it on a press outside the bar, an open menu latches the bar visible via `CUIBar.onMenuStateChange` → `_updateHeaderShown()` (the dropdown hangs *below* the strip, so moving down to click a row would otherwise leave the hover region and fade the menu out from under the click), and `fitDropdownToWindow()` caps `$children.maxHeight` to the space below the title with `overflow-y: auto`, so a view docked low on screen no longer runs its menu off the bottom.

- **"Optimize For Star Tracking" — a verified search over the Video Adjustments for the settings that identify the most stars** (`3c0ca363`; new `src/starTrack/StarAdjustOptimize.js` (+1074) exporting `addStarOptimizeControls()` and `calibrateFitness()`; +305 in `src/starTrack/StarTrackerUI.js` exporting `starTrackerDetectOptions()`, `starTrackerVideoMask()`, `starTrackerAppliesAdjustments()`, `starTrackerAutoSigma()`, `getStarTrackerTweaks()`/`setStarTrackerTweaks()`, `captureStarTrackerResult()`/`restoreStarTrackerResult()`, `scoreStarTrackerIdentification()` and `setStarOptimizeMenuBuilder()`; new `CNodeVideoView.getFramePixels()`; `addStarOptimizeControls(guiVideoEffectsFolder)` in `CNodeVideoViewFilters.addFiltersToVideoNode`; a new "Optimize For Star Tracking" section in `docs/StarTracker.md`). Reachable from two places — **Video → Video Adjustments → *Optimize For Star Tracking***, and **Video → Star Tracker → *Optimize Adjustments for Frame*** immediately below *Full Analysis* (registered through `setStarOptimizeMenuBuilder` rather than an import, because `StarAdjustOptimize` already imports `StarTrackerUI` and a direct import would close a cycle). Both sets swap to *Enough (Accept)* / *Abort (Reset)* plus a *Star Tracking* status row while a run is in progress, wherever it was started from. **Stage one** is a genetic search (`POPULATION_SIZE` 10, `ELITE_COUNT` 3, `MAX_GENERATIONS` 30, `MAX_NO_IMPROVE` 4, one generation per event-loop turn) over the six `GENES` — `videoBrightness`, `videoContrast`, `videoShadows`, `videoHighlights`, `videoDehaze`, `videoBlur` — with search bounds narrower than the sliders' own ranges. The idea the whole file rests on: **a candidate picture is not allowed to say whether its own detections are real.** `StarDetect.estimateBackground` thresholds at `bg + threshSigma * sigma` against the *local* noise with `sigma` floored at 0.5 and only the high side clipped, so crushing the blacks collapses MAD to zero and inflates every `peakSNR` at once — scored on its own pixels the search found that in seconds (contrast 2.13, shadows −51, dehaze +68, "58 stars", **zero** identified against the catalog). So `buildReference()` measures the frame **once** with those six controls neutral and every detection is credited by what that fixed evidence map holds at its location; the score combines anchor quality over the identifier's own 25 quad anchors (isolation and shape as gates, then ranked by brightness, exactly as `StarIdentify` picks them), the same credit over `K` detections, a purity term where only *unsupported* detections cost anything, and a tonal term pricing clipping and noise-floor collapse. Candidates are scored through `starTrackerDetectOptions()` and `starTrackerVideoMask()` — the same detector settings and the same mask the analysis will later apply — so it never tunes for detections the analysis is going to discard. **Stage two** is scored on real catalog identification via `scoreStarTrackerIdentification()`, which runs `runStarTracker({singleFrame: true, quiet: true})` followed by `identifyStars({scoring: true})`: it measures what the user's current settings identify (which also raises `K` if their baseline is deeper than 25), re-ranks stage one's best `RERANK_COUNT` = 3 candidates on identification, then `runTweakSweep()` sweeps *Detect threshold* (`THRESH_SWEEP`, skipped entirely when *Auto detect threshold* is on, since a Full Analysis would re-derive it anyway) and *Min blob area* (`MIN_AREA_SWEEP`) around the winner. **The run is vetoed** if nothing beats the baseline — ties go to the user. Abort, veto and a stage-two failure all restore the genome, the tweaks (with their provenance flags), the previously published analysis and the synced camera's bake; the applied path instead re-runs the winner through `showWinningAnalysis()` so the overlay on screen describes the settings now in force, with the stars named. The honest cost, stated in the code and the docs: on a video that leaves a **single-frame** analysis where a whole-clip one may have been. `identifyStars({scoring: true})` skips `refreshSyncedCamera()`, so a search cannot swing a camera the user synced from a whole clip. Measured on the reference still: 16 detections / 8 identified become 20–28 detections / 14–29 identified in 16–27 seconds. A local-only harness `window.__starOptimizeCalibrate` (`calibrateFitness()`, gated on `isLocal` inside `addStarOptimizeControls` because `checkLocal()` resolves after module evaluation) scores genomes both ways and checks that no candidate identifying nothing outscores one that does — currently best-dead 2.7 against worst-live 35.3. Not yet exercised: `K` above 25.

- **ECEF `x, y, z` accepted anywhere Sitrec takes a coordinate, and pasted text now goes through the Go To chain** (`b96273ed`, corrected by `a7010f32`; `parseECEF()`, `parseLatLonAlt()`, `parseLLATriple()`, `splitNumericTriple()`, `plausibleAltitude()`, `NUMBER_TOKEN`, `ECEF_MIN_ALT`/`ECEF_MAX_ALT` in `src/CoordinateParser.js`; new `src/GoTo.js` exporting `goToFrame()` and `applyGoToString()`, extracted from the "G" handler in `src/updateFrame.js`; `CDragDropHandler.uploadText()`; `resolveLocationString()`, `attachCoordinateInput()`, `attachLatLonInputs()` and `goToLatLon()` in `src/CoordinateInput.js`; `CNodePositionLLA`; `positionLLA.lookup.tooltip` in `en.js`; +185 in `tests/CoordinateParser.test.js`; a new ECEF section in `docs/GIS.md`). An `x, y, z` triple in metres now parses in the **G** (Go To) prompt, a position's *Lookup* box, its *Lat*/*Lon* boxes and in text pasted or dropped onto the app. Nothing in three numbers says "ECEF", so the only available test is to convert them and see where they land: the triple is kept only if the resulting altitude sits between `ECEF_MIN_ALT` (−1000 m) and `ECEF_MAX_ALT` (1,000,000 m), written as a range test so the NaN from `x=y=z=0` fails it. It is read as **WGS84** (`ECEFToLLA`), because that is what ECEF means outside Sitrec (EPSG:4978), with Sitrec's own earth model (`ECEFToLLA_radii`) tried only as a fallback. That ordering is load-bearing: sitches default to a spherical earth (`Sit.useEllipsoid` false) and the two models name the same point 0.19° of latitude (21 km on the ground) and 10.7 km of altitude apart at 45°. Because the WGS84 altitude is always the higher of the two (the ellipsoid radius never exceeds the equatorial radius), WGS84 can only fail the window by reading too high, so the fallback can only rescue a triple, never misplace one — reversed, a WGS84 point 10 km up reads as 730 m underground on the sphere, passes, and lands 21 km out. `a7010f32` then removed the precedence rule between ECEF and `lat, lon, alt` entirely: the first version tried LLA first on the assumption that "a real ECEF x is millions of metres and can never pass for a latitude", which **fails at the poles** where x and y are zero — `0, 0, 6356752` is the WGS84 north pole and was navigating to lat 0, lon 0 at an altitude of 6356 km. `parseLatLonAlt()` now applies the same altitude window to the LLA reading (`plausibleAltitude()`), which makes the two mutually exclusive: a triple only reaches the surface if its magnitude is ~6400 km, and one whose x and y are small enough to pass for degrees can only manage that along z, so read as a lat/lon its altitude lands near 6400 km and is declined. A triple whose altitude is outside the window and is not an Earth position either (a geostationary subsatellite point at 35,786 km, or a negative altitude) still returns as a lat/lon rather than being dropped — dropping it would fall through to `parseLatLonPair`, which reads `-120.5, -2000` as degrees and minutes and silently invents a longitude of −153.8. Separately, an altitude that arrives with a location is now **kept**: `parseLatLonAlt` reports `alt` as `undefined` when the text carried none (not zero), so `CNodePositionLLA`'s Lookup only falls back to `customAltitudeFunction` when nothing was given, and `goToLatLon(lat, lon, above, back, alt)` frames a point in the air from 1 km instead of the 100 km fly-up that would leave it a speck. Finally, `CDragDropHandler.uploadText()` now calls `applyGoToString()` — frame number, then date/time, then coordinate, then place name — so anything typeable into Go To works as a paste, replacing a `split`/`parseFloat` that fed `NaN` straight to the camera for any two- or three-word snippet.

### Improvements

- **The Star Tracker analyses the frame you can see, not the raw decode** (`11f6b43d`; `params.applyAdjustments` and the *Apply adjustments* checkbox after *Use mask* in `setupStarTrackerMenu`, `sourceFrameOf()` and the rewritten `framePixels()` in `src/starTrack/StarTrackerUI.js`; the readback later moved into `CNodeVideoView.getFramePixels()` by `3c0ca363`; a row in `docs/StarTracker.md`). On by default, and a no-op when no adjustments are set. With it on, every frame the analysis measures carries the video view's own Video Adjustments — levels, curves, sharpen, blur, brightness, invert, echo — so an analysis can no longer report stars that are not visible on screen, or miss ones only the adjustments bring out. The pixels come from the view's own `getAdjustedVideoFrameSource()`, the same call `renderCanvas()` makes, so there is one definition of "adjusted" rather than a second that drifts: its pixel stages are baked into the returned image, its cheap GPU-side ones come back as a CSS filter string applied on the readback draw, and the `fullABOverlay` is composited after. That draw must stay synchronous with the call, because the canvases returned are owned and reused by the video view and the live render loop overwrites them the moment the function awaits. The In-point frame mapping moved into `sourceFrameOf()` so the decode and the adjustment call agree on which frame they are asking for — the filter caches key on the source frame, and passing a global frame would make an In-locked view re-filter every frame it had already filtered. Echo accumulates preceding frames while `getImage()` purges outside a 30-frame window (shorter than the 100 frames echo allows), and `renderCanvas` only widens that window while the view is rendering, so `framePixels` now declares `echoFramesNeeded` itself — before the decode that does the purging, and raise-only, since lowering it would evict frames the view still wants.

- **Unrecognised pasted or dropped text now says so** (`b96273ed`; `CDragDropHandler.uploadText()`). Previously a snippet that did not split into two or three numbers was only `console.log`ged. It now reports `"…" is not a frame number, a date/time, a coordinate, or a place we could find`, with the echoed text truncated at 120 characters so a stray paste of a whole document does not fill the screen.

- **Consistent per-view control naming** (`c7197d0b`; `viewControlLabel()` in `src/ViewUIBarMenus.js`, plus label edits in `src/i18n/en.js` — English only, per the locale rule). Every control that can be on in one view and off in another now reads `"&lt;Thing&gt; in Main"` / `"&lt;Thing&gt; in Look"`: `showAllTracksInLook` "Show All Tracks in Look View" → "All Tracks in Look", `vectorsInLookView` "Vectors in Look View" → "Celestial Vectors in Look", `featuresInMain` "Features/Pins in Main" → "Features in Main", `groundVideoInLookView` "Ground Video in Look View" → "Ground Video in Look", `equatorialGridLook` "Equatorial Grid in Look View" → "Equatorial Grid in Look", and the sky-overlay pair, previously composed as raw view ids ("mainView Star names", "mainView Only label planets"), now compose through `viewControlLabel()` as "Star Names in Main" / "Only Label Planets in Main".

### Bug Fixes

- **Fixed *Equatorial Grid in Look* doing nothing when the main-view grid was off** (`c7197d0b`; `showEquatorialGridMain` replacing `showEquatorialGrid` in `CNodeDisplayNightSky`, new `perViewLayerMask()` in `src/LayerMasks.js`, conversion in `modDeserialize`, `nightSky.equatorialGridMain` in `en.js`, `tests/perViewLayerMask.test.js`). The grid was a master flag plus a look-view include, so the look row could be ticked and mean nothing. It is now two independent per-view flags like every other pair, and `updateVis()` builds the layer mask from both. `perViewLayerMask()` carries the trap it exists to avoid: only `MASK_HELPERS` (main) and `MASK_LOOK` distinguish the two renders — `MASK_MAINRENDER` also carries `WORLD|TARGET`, which the look camera tests too, so masking with it to mean "main only" leaks into the look view. A zero mask also clears `.visible`, since an object with a zero mask is skipped but its children are still walked. Legacy saves carrying the old master key convert in `modDeserialize`, reproducing the old meaning: master off meant "nowhere", whatever the look flag said.

- **Fixed colour pickers, sliders and drop-downs degrading to plain text boxes in the floating *Edit:* menus — in released builds only** (`c7197d0b`; `mirrorGUIControls` in `src/CustomManagerMirror.js` now delegates to `GUI.mirrorFolderFrom` → `Controller.mirrorTo`, deleting ~190 lines of a second, drifted implementation). The deleted copy identified controller kinds with `controller.constructor.name === 'ColorController' | 'OptionController' | 'NumberController'`. Terser mangles class names, so in a production build every controller fell through to the generic `target.add(object, property)` branch: colour swatches became text fields, ranged numbers lost their sliders and min/max, and drop-downs lost their option lists. Local development builds were unaffected, which is why it survived. `MenuMirror`'s `controllerKind()` reads lil-gui's own CSS classes on `domElement` instead, which the minifier cannot touch, and also carries across `_maxMax`, `decimals()`, `elastic()`, `noSlider()` and the unit-type metadata.

- **Fixed mirrored menu rows losing their tooltips** (`c7197d0b`; `Controller.prototype.tooltip` in `src/lil-gui-extras.js`). `tooltip()` set the DOM attribute but never stored `_tooltip`, while both mirroring paths read the text from `_tooltip` — so every twin came out tooltip-less. The text is now kept as readable state as well.

- **Fixed a view's HUD overlays painting over its header bar and any open header menu** (`c7197d0b`; `CUIBar.chromeRect()` and the exported `hudClipPath()`, `CNodeView._clipHUDsBelowHeader()`). The MQ-9 / Wescam OSD frames, the video-info panel and the compass are separate views positioned `relativeTo` their host — sibling divs with a higher z-index, since `updateZOrder` stacks by area and they are the same size — and the header lives inside the host's stacking context, so no z-index could lift it above them. They were already pointer-transparent, so clicks always landed; this is purely about what is visible. Each companion is now clipped by exactly the shape the header chrome covers (a full-width strip, plus the narrow dropdown column when a menu is open — a 6-point polygon, degenerating to a top inset with no menu open), measured per companion because `clip-path` is box-relative, so a corner compass well below the bar is left untouched. The full box is handed back when the header is disposed.

- **Fixed `.listen()` being a silent no-op outside the docked menu bar** (`c7197d0b`; new `src/GUIRootRegistry.js`, called from `CGuiMenuBar.updateListeners`; `registerGUIRoot`/`unregisterGUIRoot` in `CUIBar.setShown`/`dispose` and in `CustomManagerMirror.createMirroredMenu`; `tests/GUIRootRegistry.test.js`). The fork removed lil-gui's per-controller `requestAnimationFrame`, so `.listen()` only sets a flag and something must walk the tree once a frame — and that walk covered only the docked menu-bar slots plus `activePersistentMenu`/`activeContextMenu`. In any other root — a mirrored *Edit:* popup that was not the most recently opened one, a mirror docked into a sidebar, and now the per-view header menus — anything that changed a value without going through a controller (a sitch load, the API, a script, dragging an object's 3D handles, or a twin in another menu) left the widget showing the old value permanently. Roots now register themselves; header menus register only while the bar is shown, since a hidden one would cost a full `controllersRecursive()` walk per frame and catches up the frame it reappears. Whole-folder mirrors force `.listen()` on both ends, because the Building/Track edit popups exist precisely to track values written directly by 3D-handle drags.

- **Fixed the *North Up* checkbox (View menu) showing a stale value after loading a sitch** (`c7197d0b`; `.listen()` added in `CNodeView3D`). `northUp` is serialized via `addSimpleSerial`, so a load writes the flag straight onto the view with nothing polling the checkbox.

- **Fixed Full Analysis quietly measuring over a *Min blob area* you had chosen** (`3c0ca363`; new `minAreaChosen` flag alongside `minAreaCalibrated`, `detectStarSize({measure})` in `src/starTrack/StarTrackerUI.js`). Stage 0 of *Full Analysis* chains *Detect Star Size*, which overwrote `params.minArea` unconditionally — so a value set by hand on the slider (or verified by the new optimizer) was replaced before the analysis ran, and the result differed from the one the slider promised. Three states are needed, not two: an untouched default must still be calibrated by the chained call, a *measured* value may be re-measured freely, and a *chosen* one survives until a measurement is asked for explicitly. Pressing **Detect Star Size (current frame)** still overwrites it (`{measure: true}`), because that button *is* the request to measure, and the status line now appends `(kept)` when the chained call leaves the value alone. A value chosen for a previous video stops shielding itself when the video changes.

- **Fixed pasting or dropping arbitrary text sending the camera to an invalid position** (`b96273ed`; `CDragDropHandler.uploadText()`). The old handler ran `text.split(/[\s,]+/).map(parseFloat)` and, on any two- or three-token snippet, passed the resulting `NaN`s to `droppedLLA()` and on to the camera.

### Documentation

- `docs/UserInterface.md` gains "The View Header" and "Per-view controls" sections describing the header menu contents per view and the "&lt;Thing&gt; in Main" / "&lt;Thing&gt; in Look" convention (`c7197d0b`).
- `docs/StarTracker.md` gains a full "Optimize For Star Tracking" section — the two stages, why a candidate may not grade its own detections, the measured before/after table, and the *Apply adjustments*, *Detect Star Size* and *Min blob area* rows rewritten for the new provenance rule (`11f6b43d`, `3c0ca363`).
- `docs/GIS.md` gains the ECEF input rules, including why WGS84 is tried before Sitrec's own earth model and how the altitude window separates an ECEF triple from a `lat, lon, alt` one at the poles (`b96273ed`, `a7010f32`).

## Version 2.128.0 (2026-08-11)

### New Features

- **Paint On Ground: a texture brush for the ground imagery, the texture-space sibling of "Remove Geometry"** (`f1ce4be1`, refined by `a310170c`; new `src/GroundPaint.js` exporting `CGroundPainter`, `GROUND_PAINT_DEFS` and `makeDefaultGroundPaintParams`, new `src/GroundPaintBrush.js` exporting `GroundPaintBrush`, new dependency-free `src/GroundPaintState.js` exporting the `PAINT_TEX_STATE` Symbol and `unpaintedTextureImage`; `buildGroundPaintGUI()`, `groundPaintParams`, `groundPainter` and the `groundPaintParams` serialization in `src/nodes/CNodeTerrainUI.js`; `forEachLoadedTileMesh()` in `src/nodes/CNodeBuildings3DTiles.js`; the two `unpaintedTextureImage` reads in `src/QuadTreeTileMaterial.js`; **Terrain → *Paint On Ground*** with *Paint Mode*, *Brush Radius (m)*, *Paint Color*, *Apply Paint*, *Export Paint (JSON)*, *Import Paint (JSON)* and *Clear Paint* — all labels hard-coded, no i18n keys added). Paints the ground **imagery**, where the existing manual tree/geometry brush moves or deletes **geometry**: same gesture, same persistence model, different target. **Nothing is ever baked in.** A stroke is recorded as an ordered list of *dabs* — `{lla:[lat,lon,alt], r, c?:0xRRGGBB, e?:1}` in geographic coordinates — and that list is what serializes with the sitch (via `CNodeTerrainUI.modSerialize`, merged not replaced on load so the GUI controllers and the painter keep their shared object reference). The painted pixels are always a **replay** of that list onto whatever textures happen to be loaded, which is what makes every awkward case fall out for free: a tile that streams in later gets the strokes as it arrives, a tile that subdivides, changes zoom or re-fetches gets them re-applied **at its own resolution**, and the source imagery is never destroyed — every painted texture keeps its original image, which is exactly what Option/Alt-erase paints back. **Two unrelated textured grounds are both painted**, so the paint follows whichever is actually being rendered. (1) The basemap quadtree tiles, where each tile is a lat/lon rectangle, so a dab is a plain ellipse in the tile image — a circle of *r* metres is a circle in Web Mercator (conformal) but an ellipse in the equirectangular 4326 grid, hence separate horizontal and vertical pixel radii, computed per dab from the brush radius stepped along the local east/north vectors through the real ellipsoid rather than from a metres-per-degree constant. (2) The Google Photorealistic 3D tile textures, which carry arbitrary glTF UVs, so there is no rectangle to draw into and the dab **sphere** has to be rasterized through the mesh. That is done **per triangle PLANE**: intersect the dab sphere with the triangle's plane for a true disc of radius √(r² − d²) about the projected centre, then clip the triangle against that disc (16 tangent half-planes, `DISC_SIDES`), accumulating all the resulting polygons into ONE UV-space path per dab per mesh so a single fill avoids the hairline seams that per-triangle fills leave along shared edges. The rejected alternative — interpolating the sphere's distance field along each edge — fails on adaptive photogrammetry meshes, where flat ground is a handful of huge triangles and a brush landing wholly **inside** one paints nothing at all; the plane-disc clip is correct whatever the triangle's size. `forEachLoadedTileMesh` walks every loaded tile mesh across **all** per-view renderers, because each view holds the tiles at its own LOD with separate geometry *and* separate textures; unlike the tree flattener it is deliberately not gated on the tile source, since painting imagery is as meaningful for Cesium OSM buildings as for Google photogrammetry. **State hangs off the objects themselves**, so it dies with them and needs no registry that would keep disposed textures alive: a `Texture` carries `{canvas, ctx, orig, applied, gen}` under the `PAINT_TEX_STATE` Symbol, and a 3D-tile `Mesh` carries its own applied count plus generation stamp, because several meshes can feed triangles into one shared texture. The list is append-only during a stroke, so a texture or mesh whose count is below the list length just needs the new tail — that is what makes the per-frame reapply pass (`REAPPLY_BUDGET = 8` textures per pass, so a backlog spreads over frames) cheap and safe to call repeatedly, and `_anyPainted` lets a sitch with no paint exit before touching a single tile. **Anything that is not an append — undo, redo, *Clear Paint*, *Apply Paint* off, loading a sitch — bumps a generation counter** rather than trying to reach every painted texture; anything stamped with an older generation is reset from its original and replayed the next time the pass sees it. That is load-bearing, not tidiness: a pruned basemap tile's material survives in `materialCache` and can be handed back to a later tile, so without the stamp cleared paint would reappear. **The fallback-material fix that had to come with it**: `buildMaterialFromParent`/`buildMaterialFromAncestor` in `QuadTreeTileMaterial.js` now resample `unpaintedTextureImage(parentTexture)` instead of `texture.source.data`, because while a tile is painted its `texture.image` **is** the painter's canvas — deriving a child from it baked the paint into the child's source image, which the painter then stashed as that child's `orig`, so erase, undo and *Clear Paint* restored the paint instead of removing it on exactly those fallback tiles. Deriving from the clean image is also better in its own terms: the painter replays the dabs onto the child at the child's resolution a frame later, sharper than an upscaled copy of the parent's paint. **The brush** (`GroundPaintBrush`) is structured like the geometry brush and for the same reasons: document-level listeners in the **capture** phase so a stroke starting on a render canvas can `stopPropagation()` and pre-empt the view's own camera-drag handlers (camera navigation stays on the middle and right buttons, which are never intercepted); mouse coordinates tracked locally rather than read from the global `getMousePosition()`, which goes stale precisely because we stop propagation and a stale position re-picks in the *other* view; and the ray built from the **displayed** projection via `prepareCameraForLOD`/`restoreCameraAfterLOD`, because the look view renders a wider frustum offscreen and shows a magnified central crop, so the live camera projection is about 2× too wide for picking. A press is ignored unless it landed on an `HTMLCanvasElement`, which is what keeps the lil-gui panel usable while *Paint Mode* is on. The pick goes through `raycastLocalGround`, so it lands on whichever surface is actually in front — 3D tiles when loaded, basemap terrain otherwise — and a bare-ellipsoid fallback hit (`isTerrain` false) paints nothing, there being no texture there. A stroke **begins** even when the press is not over the ground, so a swipe starting on sky paints as the brush crosses the surface; consecutive dabs closer than 0.3 × radius with the same colour/radius/erase state are deduped, which still leaves a continuous stroke; `window.blur` ends an in-progress stroke so its undo entry is still recorded. The cursor is a `LineLoop` ring lying flat on the ground at the brush radius, `depthTest` off so it does not z-fight the surface it rests on, tinted with the paint colour or red (`0xff4040`) while erasing, refreshed per frame from a cheap fingerprint of pointer + both candidate cameras + brush radius so an idle hover neither re-picks nor keeps the render loop awake — and `updateWhilePaused` now includes `paintMode` so the ring tracks the surface while the camera moves with the pointer held still. **Undo** is the same shape as the geometry brush: the list is append-only and applied idempotently, so there is no "remove the last dab" — moving to any state means resetting the textures and replaying the chosen list, and a whole gesture collapses into one entry (*Paint On Ground brush stroke*). **Export/Import** write the dab list to a standalone versioned JSON file (`type: "sitrec-ground-paint"`, `version: 1`, plus the sitch name) named `<sitch>-groundpaint.json`; import is fully validated **before** anything is replaced, so a bad file leaves the current paint untouched, is undoable as a single step, and force-enables *Apply Paint* (recorded in the undo entry, or an undo would leave the checkbox flipped) because imported paint the user cannot see reads as a failed import. It is deliberately not routed through the `FileManager`: the strokes belong to the terrain UI's serialized state, and a file that became part of the sitch would re-import and double up on every reload. Defaults: *Paint Mode* off, *Brush Radius* 8 m (range 0.5–200, step 0.5), *Paint Color* `0x6b7a52` (a muted olive), *Apply Paint* on — the last persisting independently of *Paint Mode*, so the saved paint keeps applying with the brush put away, and can be switched off to see the original imagery without discarding a stroke. A dab whose footprint is under `MIN_DAB_PIXELS = 0.35` px on a given tile is skipped for that tile, so a whole stroke does not pile up into a speck of noise on a coarse ancestor.

- **Shift-click straight lines and `[` / `]` brush sizing for Paint On Ground** (`a310170c`; `applyBrushLine()`, `_pushDab()` split out of `applyBrush()`, `handleBrushSizeKeys()` and `MAX_LINE_DABS = 2000` in `src/GroundPaint.js`; `_lastPaintPoint` and `resetPaintAnchor()` in `src/GroundPaintBrush.js`). Shift-clicking paints a straight run of dabs from wherever the brush **last painted** — the end of your last drag, or your last click — so shift-clicks chain into a polyline and a shift-click after a freehand drag continues from where the drag stopped rather than from where it began. The anchor is updated from the *picked point* on every click and continuously through a drag, deliberately including dabs the 0.3 × radius dedupe rejected: the brush was still there, and that is what "where I last painted" means. It fires only on the **click**, so dragging still paints freehand (and a shift-*drag* is a line to the press point followed by a normal stroke on from there). The line is **expanded into ordinary dabs** rather than stored as a segment record: a segment would need its own rasterizer in both painters — a capsule cut by a triangle plane is a stadium, not the disc the 3D-tile path clips against — and expanding it means the line serializes, erases, undoes and replays through exactly the existing code with no new geometry to get wrong. It is interpolated in **lat/lon/alt**, not by lerping the ECEF endpoints: a straight chord through the Earth sags below the surface (~2 m over 10 km, ~49 m over 50 km), which would drop the 3D-tile dab spheres under the ground they are meant to paint. The longitude delta is unwrapped the **short way round**, or a 20 km line across the antimeridian (179.9 → −179.9) becomes a 359.8° trip the other way — and since the step count came from the true ECEF distance, the dabs would be smeared into a sparse dotted ring around the planet instead of the local line asked for. Each step is snapped to the ground through `TerrainModel.getPointBelow` (an elevation-map lookup, not a mesh raycast — cheap per step, and its few-metre error is well inside the brush radius) so a line crossing a valley follows it. Spacing is 0.4 × radius, above the dedupe gate; a line needing more than 2000 dabs is **refused with an explanation** naming the distance, the dab count and the limit, rather than silently thinned. `[` and `]` shrink and grow the brush using the same keys and the same polled 50 ms repeat as the video mask brush, active only while *Paint Mode* is on so the keys stay free otherwise; the step is **proportional** (15% per press, ~40 presses across the range at any size) rather than that brush's sqrt curve, because this radius is in metres over 0.5–200 where a fixed step either crawls at the top of the range or overshoots the bottom, and the bounds are read from `GROUND_PAINT_DEFS` so the keys cannot drive the value off the end of its own slider. *Clear Paint* and undo/redo call `resetPaintAnchor()`, so a shift-click cannot draw a line from a place that is no longer part of anything on screen.

- **Colour key on the video overlay: make specific colours in the look view come through the blend at full strength** (`a310170c`; `applyColorKeyFromUnderlyingView()`, `keyColor` (`addSimpleSerial`) and the `<id>_keyTolerance` `CNodeGUIValue` in `src/nodes/CNodeViewCanvas.js`; the call site at the end of `renderCanvas` in `src/nodes/CNodeVideoView.js`; **View → *Key Color* and *Key Tolerance %***, immediately under the existing *Vid Overlay Trans %* — labels hard-coded, no i18n). The overlay blend is uniform: the whole video canvas is drawn over the look view at one opacity, so anything in the 3D view is at best a ghost. The key punches chosen colours back through — every pixel of the **underlying** view within tolerance of *Key Color* is copied on top of the video, last, once the frame is fully drawn. **Why that reads as full strength at any transparency**: CSS composites the overlay as `t·overlay + (1−t)·underlying`, and a keyed pixel now holds the *same* colour in both layers (it was copied from the one below), so the two terms sum back to that colour whatever `t` is. The intended use is annotation — paint magenta on the ground with *Paint On Ground*, key on magenta, and the painted region reads solid over the video while everything else stays a faint blend. Tolerance is not a convenience: the 3D view **shades** the paint (day/night lighting), so the rendered pixels sit *near* the paint colour rather than on it; the tooltip says to raise it until the shaded and antialiased edges fill in. Default *Key Color* is magenta (`0xff00ff`, rare in real imagery), default tolerance 0 — which means off, and off returns before touching a pixel. Tolerance is a percentage of the largest possible RGB distance (`√(3·255²)`), tested as squared Euclidean distance with a per-channel box test first, so the box rejects the overwhelming majority of pixels in one comparison and only survivors pay for the multiplies. **Alignment is measured, never assumed** — this is where a naive implementation goes wrong. The two canvases share a div but do not cover the same rectangle: a 3D view is letterboxed inside its div to hold the video's aspect ratio (measured: `canvas.style.left` 31 px, 773 of the div's 835 CSS px), their backing resolutions are unrelated (880×495 vs 1670×870 at DPR 2), and the overlay's 2D context carries its own transform. Mapping full canvas to full canvas stretched the keyed layer by the letterbox ratio and shifted it by the inset, producing a visible **double image** of anything keyed. The mapping is therefore derived from **both canvases' bounding rects converted into this canvas's backing pixels**, and the composite is done at the identity transform 1:1 — correct for any letterbox, any device pixel ratio, any pair of backing resolutions, and whatever transform the caller drew its frame with, and it covers the look view's video-matched pixel zoom for free (that canvas holds the displayed magnified crop, and its bounding rect is where the crop lands on screen). Verified sub-pixel at both edges of the view (0.00 / −0.25 px at the right, inside its own bounding box at the left) with the errors not flipping sign across the view. Extraction is **nearest-neighbour on purpose** (`imageSmoothingEnabled = false` on both the extract and the composite): interpolation would invent blends of the key colour and its surroundings along every edge, which the tolerance test cannot distinguish from genuinely near-key pixels, so the keyed area would creep outwards as tolerance is raised to cope with lighting. The scratch canvas and its `ImageData` are reused across frames (reallocating a screen-sized buffer per frame is what makes naive per-pixel canvas work slow) and pixel work is confined to the sub-rect the source actually landed in, the cleared letterbox margins staying transparent. The composite restores identity transform, `filter: none`, `globalAlpha 1` and `source-over` defensively, since the caller drew its frame with its own transform, filter and alpha and any of those leaking in would misplace or tint the keyed layer. The underlying view is a WebGL canvas without `preserveDrawingBuffer`, so its drawing buffer is only readable inside the animation frame that drew it — which holds, because every view's `renderCanvas` runs in one frame and an overlay's parent is created (and so rendered) before it; if it ever did not, the read comes back empty and the pass simply keys nothing rather than erroring. Both settings serialize with the sitch.

- **MQ-9 HUD: the ACFT altitude readout cycles MSL and HAT in feet *and* metres** (`a0a3aa6a`; new `formatAltitude()` replacing the MSL/HAT if/else in `renderCanvas`, `acftAltMode` now `% 4`, in `src/nodes/CNodeMQ9UI.js`; click the ACFT altitude row on the MQ-9 overlay, **Show → Views → *MQ9UI***). The readout was feet-only, toggling between MSL and HAT. It now cycles four modes on click — MSL (ft), HAT (ft), MSL (m), HAT (m) — with the unit shown explicitly (`5,239FT MSL` / `1,597M MSL`), matching the unit-suffix convention the SLR and GRN rows already use. **Feet keep mode indices 0 and 1** so previously saved sitches, which serialize `acftAltMode` as a raw integer, come back in the units they were saved with; metres are appended as 2 and 3. `formatAltitude()` splits the mode into a datum bit and a unit bit, rounds the exact altitude **once in its own unit** rather than rounding to metres and converting, and keeps the terrain-elevation sample behind the HAT branch so MSL mode does no per-frame elevation lookup. The TGT altitude row (`targetAltMode`) is untouched by this change.

- **EXIF/Metadata panel: container and stream facts alongside EXIF, and the window's own state saved with the sitch** (`0c2f863c`; new `CVideoData.getMediaInfo()` with overrides in `src/CVideoMp4Data.js`, `src/CVideoPatchedData.js` and `src/CVideoAudioOnly.js`; `buildMediaHTML`, `formatBitrate`, `formatBytes`, `formatDuration`, `sectionHeaderHTML`, `getState`/`setState` and `clampIntoView` in `src/EXIFInfoPanel.js`; `exifPanel` in `modSerialize`, the stash-then-apply `applyEXIFPanelState()` and `syncEXIFInfoPanel(videoData)` in `src/nodes/CNodeVideoView.js`; the **Video → *Show EXIF/Metadata*** entry — labels hard-coded, no i18n; 15 new cases in `tests/EXIFInfoPanel.test.js`). The panel now opens with a **Media** section above the EXIF one: size, duration, frames, frame rate, container brand, video codec, video bitrate, video track size, audio codec, audio bitrate and audio format (sample rate + channels), each rendered only when the media can actually answer it — the base `getMediaInfo()` supplies what a plain image knows (size, frames, fps) and each subclass adds what it knows, undefined fields simply not being shown. `CVideoMp4Data` reads duration, container brand, codecs, bitrates, track size and the audio track out of **retained MP4Box state** parsed at `onReady`, so it is a read and not a re-parse; note its fps comes from the demuxer's measured samples/duration and the bitrate/size figures are MP4Box's per-**track** numbers rather than the whole file. `CVideoPatchedData` merges the wrapped source's codec facts with its **own** frame count and fps, that virtual uniform-cadence timeline over a VFR file being the wrapper's whole point. `CVideoAudioOnly` deliberately does **not** extend the base: its 640×360 is the waveform visualisation canvas and its fps is a synthetic 30 invented to give the timeline something to step through, so reporting either as media metadata would be untrue — it reports duration, codec, bitrate, sample rate and channels only, and no picture size. Bit rates arrive in bits/second and span three orders of magnitude between an audio and a 4K video track, so the unit is picked per value (bps/kbps/Mbps); bytes and durations likewise. Raw mode now emits `{media, exif}` rather than the EXIF blob alone, so *Copy Raw* is worth having on a video carrying no EXIF at all. The panel's own window state — open/closed, position, size, compact/raw — round-trips through `modSerialize`/`modDeserialize`. That restore is **stashed, not applied**, in `modDeserialize`: `CNodeView`'s constructor calls `applyEarlyMods()`, which dispatches to the override *before* this class's constructor body has created `exifInfoPanel`, and touching the panel there aborted construction and broke loading of every saved sitch — so whichever runs second (the normal-path call, or the constructor) applies it. Restoring before the media has loaded is safe: the panel reads "no metadata" until the load callback feeds it.

### Improvements

- **The EXIF panel's Video-menu entry is renamed, gated on the view holding media, and no longer moves when toggled** (`0c2f863c`; `hasMedia()`, the rewritten `updateEXIFInfoButton()` and the new `refreshEXIFUI()` convergence point in `src/nodes/CNodeVideoView.js`; the panel's default `title` in `src/EXIFInfoPanel.js`). *Show/Hide EXIF Panel* is now *Show/Hide EXIF/Metadata* and the panel title *Image EXIF* is now *EXIF/Metadata*, since "Image EXIF" was simply wrong on an MP4 and the panel now reports container facts as much as camera ones. The entry is gated on `hasMedia()` — the view holding a video or image — rather than on that media *having EXIF*, because every video has size, fps, codec and bitrate to show even with no EXIF whatsoever; the EXIF-GPS button keeps its own stricter gate on `placement.hasLocation`. While the entry exists the controller is **relabelled in place** rather than destroyed and recreated, so toggling the panel no longer shuffles its position in the menu. Because the button now outlives the media, it is explicitly destroyed in `dispose()` (node disposal runs before the menu bar is torn down on a sitch change). Six duplicated pairs of button-update calls collapse into `refreshEXIFUI()`, which also re-syncs the panel, making it the single convergence point for the whole EXIF UI.

### Bug Fixes

- **Fixed the plane-homography camera fit returning physically impossible cameras as successful fits** (`293ed6e1`; `dltHomography` now returning `{H, rankRatio}` with the new `DLT_RANK_FLOOR = 1e-6`, the `±MARGIN = 12` scan extension and endpoint rejection, the clamped bracket in `refineFocalByGoldenSection`, and the cheirality gate in `fitCameraByPlaneHomography`, all in `src/CameraPlaneHomography.js`; surfaced through `this.updateStatus(result.reason)` at **Camera → Fit Camera to Points → *Method* → *Plane homography***; new `tests/CameraPlaneHomography.test.js`, 13 cases). Nothing in a closed-form pipeline naturally throws — the DLT always returns a vector, the focal scan always has a lowest sample, and the decomposition always produces *some* rotation — so the solver could report `ok: true` for cameras that cannot exist. Three gates were missing. **(1) Degenerate control layouts.** Taking the last right-singular vector as the homography silently assumes a one-dimensional null space; with three or more points collinear, on the ground **or** in the image, it is not, and the answer is an arbitrary mix of equally valid null directions, returned with total confidence. `dltHomography` now also returns `s[7]/s[0]`, and a ratio at or below `1e-6` is rejected with *"These control points are degenerate for a homography — three or more are collinear, on the ground or in the image. Move one off the line."* Measured after Hartley conditioning: a well-spread 3×3 grid 2.8e-1, four points in general position 2.2e-1, clustered but valid 2.4e-1, three of five collinear (still usable) 1.0e-1, near-collinear at 2% off 2.6e-3, collinear in the image 4.2e-17, collinear on the plane 0 — about four orders of magnitude of clearance on each side of the threshold. **(2) Focal-search endpoints.** A score still falling as the scan ran out was taken as a minimum: two swapped pixels in an eight-point set drove the scan to its 1° limit and returned a **46,700 px** reprojection error as a fit whose *Observability* read *Good*. The scan now samples 12 steps **past each end** at the same ratio, so every supported focal length has neighbours on both sides and the supported boundaries (1° and 170°, both legitimate) are interior — without moving any existing sample position, since indices 0…N land on exactly the focals they always did, and an extra sample can only win when the score is genuinely still falling outside the supported range, which is the case being rejected anyway. An endpoint win is now rejected with a message that says **which** end and what each means: below the range is wider than 170°, above it is narrower than 1° — and a camera narrower than 1° is a real thing Sitrec fits routinely, this method simply not searching that far, so the message names the 3D points solver as the right tool. The golden-section bracket is additionally clamped to `[LO, HI]`, because at index 0 or N the bracket reached one step *past* the boundary and refinement could converge outside the range just validated (returning, say, 170.4° as ok); the clamp is a no-op for every interior minimum, and the out-of-range refinement test is mutation-verified — it fails with the clamp removed. **(3) Cheirality.** `evaluateCamera`'s `behind` count was computed and thrown away here, while the direct solver has always rejected on it. `decomposeAtFocal` only checks that the camera came out *above the ground plane*, which says nothing about whether the control points are in front of the lens; a camera that puts landmarks behind itself is not a camera whatever its score, and the same gate now applies, reporting how many points are behind. **Valid-path results are unchanged**: every numeric output of both solvers across nine scenarios, serialised at full float precision, is byte-identical to before — only the deliberately rejected cases differ. The commit also carries a substantial comment pass over both solvers pitched at a reader who has not met SVD, Levenberg-Marquardt, Huber loss or the DLT, correcting four inaccuracies in the existing comments: `lambdaDown` was described as a divisor where the code multiplies, Gauss-Newton was called Newton, the IRLS weights were said to reproduce the Huber *cost* where they reproduce its *gradient*, and `intersectRays` was described as operating on rays where it minimises against infinite lines and is called with directions pointing away from the solution. The `CameraPointFit.js` changes are those comments plus a `c` → `col` loop-variable rename; no functional change.

- **Fixed the MQ-9 HUD's "MSL" altitude actually being height above the ellipsoid** (`a0a3aa6a`; `formatAltitude()` in `src/nodes/CNodeMQ9UI.js`). `lla.z` from `ECEFToLLAVD_radii` is HAE, so the row labelled MSL was showing ellipsoid height — too high by the geoid undulation: 45 ft at the test sitch (11.4 N, 43.2 E, N = −13.63 m) and up to roughly 350 ft where EGM96 peaks. It now subtracts `meanSeaLevelOffset(lat, lon)`, which is the contract documented at `SphericalMath.js:183` and what `CNodeWescamMXUI`, `CNodeLabels3D` and `CNode3DObject` already do. HAT is verified bit-identical, because `getTerrainElevation` reports terrain in the same HAE datum and the ellipsoid cancels in the subtraction. Fixed as part of adding the metres modes specifically so the new modes would not inherit the wrong datum.

- **Fixed the Sitch Browser's Featured list ignoring "Date (newest)" when not signed in** (`2f1967fb`, corrected within this release by `3f95b500`; `sitchDatesForUser()` and `refreshFeaturedDates()` plus the `date` field on the `?featured=1` response in `sitrecServer/metadata.php`; `date` carried through `featuredSitches`, the `featuredOnly` sitch record and the feature-a-sitch path in `src/CSitchBrowser.js`; **File → Open**, the Sitch Browser). Dates came only from `getsitches.php?get=myfiles`, which returns nothing when logged out, so every featured sitch fell back to `date: ""` and a stable sort over all-equal keys left them in `featured.json` insertion order — the newest featured sitch appearing **last**. Featured sitches owned by another user hit the same gap even when signed in. `metadata.php` now stores a date per featured entry and returns it from `?featured=1`, keeping that public, cacheable path free of per-sitch storage probes: `sitchDatesForUser()` reads the newest **version-file** mtime per sitch (S3 or local, mirroring `getsitches.php` so a screenshot or metadata write does not look like a save), and dates are written on the two paths that already touch `featured.json` — the admin featured-list write (which rescans the whole list, one storage listing per distinct user, and so also backfills entries featured before dates existed) and the screenshot version bump that follows a save (one prefix-scoped listing for just that sitch). **The GET only ever reads.** An admin-only self-heal was added to it and then removed inside this same release: it read `featured.json`, spent seconds scanning storage, then wrote back the stale pre-scan copy, so a featured edit or screenshot-version bump landing in that window was reverted — losing additions, removals or cache-busters — and it could not extinguish itself either, since `refreshFeaturedDates` leaves the date empty for a sitch with no version files, so a single featured-but-deleted sitch would re-trigger a full scan and write on every admin page load.
