Entries stored before dates existed therefore report an empty date until the next featured-list edit rescans them all.

- **Fixed the EXIF/Metadata panel refusing to open, self-closing, or opening blank** (`0c2f863c`; `setMetadata`, `show()` and the `renderContent()` call at the end of `createPanel()` in `src/EXIFInfoPanel.js`). `show()` returned early when there was no metadata and `setMetadata` called `hide()` on being handed none, so the panel could not be opened on media without EXIF and closed itself out from under a user whose selection changed. It is now a persistent window that reports whatever it has, and its content is rendered at construction so it is never blank on first open — which is also what makes restoring it from a save before any media has loaded work.

- **Fixed a second, empty video view contributing a duplicate EXIF entry to the shared Video menu** (`0c2f863c`; `hasMedia()` gating in `updateEXIFInfoButton()`, and the new `isMirrorView` prototype getter in `src/nodes/CNodeVideoView.js` / `src/nodes/CNodeMirrorVideoView.js`). The Video menu is shared by every video view, so a view holding no media must not contribute to it. Mirror views are excluded outright — they re-show another view's `videoData` and that view already owns the entry — via a **prototype getter** rather than an instance flag, so the answer is already available while the base constructor runs, before `this.in.mirror` has been wired up.

- **Fixed a restored EXIF/Metadata panel landing off-screen with no way to drag it back** (`0c2f863c`; `clampIntoView()` called from `show()` in `src/EXIFInfoPanel.js`). Geometry restored from a save was measured in whatever window the save was made in, so a sitch saved on a wide screen and opened on a narrow one could place the panel entirely outside the viewport — and the title bar is its only drag handle, and carries Close. The panel is now pulled back inside its container on every `show()`, which also covers a window that has since been made smaller: the left edge is clamped to a 16 px margin, the top only far enough to keep the header reachable, then `clampBelowMenuBar` has the final say. A container that has not been laid out yet reports 0, which is not a usable bound, so the fallback is the window rather than pinning to the corner (`||`, not `??`).

- **Fixed an open EXIF panel showing one clip's numbers under another clip's filename** (`0c2f863c`; `refreshEXIFUI(videoData)` / `syncEXIFInfoPanel(videoData)` and the `loadedCallback` call site in `src/nodes/CNodeVideoView.js`). The panel was only re-synced when it was opened, so an open panel showed stale data as the selected video changed. It now refreshes from the **selected** video, not from whichever one just finished loading: a multi-video restore completes out of order, so a late completion for a non-selected slot would otherwise paint that clip's size, codec and bitrate under the selected clip's filename. `loadedCallback` passes its own `videoData` as the fallback for the one case where `this.videoData` is not yet assigned — the first media to load.

- **Fixed the terrain brushes' serialized dab lists aliasing live state** (`a310170c`; `copyDabs()` used by `modSerialize`/`modDeserialize` in `src/nodes/CNodeTerrainUI.js`). Both the pre-existing *Remove Geometry* list and the new *Paint On Ground* list were copied by a plain object spread, which copies `dabs` **by reference**, so a serialized blob shared the live array — and both lists are mutated in place, by their brushes (append) and by their reset (`length = 0`). Anything holding a snapshot across a later stroke, undo or *Clear Paint* would silently see it change underneath, and a cleared list would empty the snapshot. Both directions now deep-copy, so a later edit cannot write through into a blob already handed out, nor a handed-in blob be mutated by a later edit. Verified through real `JSON.stringify`/`parse` and through `getCustomSitchString`. No concrete user-visible failure was demonstrated — in the normal save path the blob is stringified immediately — so this is recorded as a correctness fix rather than a reported bug.

- **Fixed assets in sitches saved from a branch or worktree build 404ing on every other install** (committed with this release; the new re-rooting fallback immediately after the `rewriteBases` loop in `loadViaDefaultAssetResolution`, inside `loadAsset` in `src/CFileManager.js`). A saved sitch embeds **absolute** asset URLs: the save records the URL each asset resolved to, which is `SITREC_APP + "data/" + name`, so it carries whatever app path that install happened to serve from. Only saves are affected — the shipped sitch definitions hold relative names (`ExtraFiles.js` has `constellationsLinesAstrometry: "nightsky/constellations.lines.astrometry.json"`), which resolve correctly against whatever `SITREC_APP` is current. The pre-existing rewrite in this block already handled the general problem, but only for four hardcoded `".../sitrec/"` prefixes (plus `https`/`http` variants of the `LOCALHOST` env value), i.e. saves from a **main** build. A branch or worktree build is served from a folder named after the git branch — `buildFolder` in `config/config-install.js` is the current branch unless it is `main` or `HEAD` — so it serves at `/<branch>/`, and a sitch saved from one embeds e.g. `https://local.metabunk.org/shadows/data/nightsky/constellations.lines.astrometry.json`. That matches no base, is never rewritten, and 404s on every other install — **permanently**, once that branch build is deleted, since nothing will ever serve that path again. Measured: that exact URL returns HTTP 404 (153 bytes) while `/sitrec/data/nightsky/constellations.lines.astrometry.json` returns HTTP 200 (35,989 bytes). Observed on the *Google 3d tiles shadow test* regression sitch, saved 2026-05-21 from a `shadows` branch build, which logged that 404 plus `PAGEERROR: Network response was not ok` on **every** load; after the fix an isolated-browser probe of the same sitch reports zero failed requests and zero page errors. **The insight the fix rests on**: for an app data asset the identity of the file is the part from `data/` onwards, and the app path in front of it is an artefact of wherever it was saved, carrying no information the loading install needs. So any `".../data/..."` URL is re-rooted onto this install's `SITREC_APP`, from the **first** `/data/` segment (the right one, since the app path necessarily precedes it), with the query string preserved. **Three gates keep that narrow.** (1) `!resolvedFilename.startsWith(SITREC_APP)`, so an asset already on this install is untouched and the two rewrites cannot double-apply. (2) The host must be `localhost`, `local.metabunk.org`, or the `LOCALHOST` env value — compared against both `parsed.host` and `parsed.hostname`, since that env value may or may not carry a port — so a third-party URL that merely happens to contain `/data/` is never hijacked. (3) The whole block is wrapped in try/catch on `new URL()`, leaving an unparseable value exactly as it was; this branch is already gated on `isHttpOrHttps`, so that is belt-and-braces rather than an expected path. Restricting it to dev hosts is the correct gate rather than a gap: a production URL is publicly reachable from anywhere and needs no rewriting, and it is precisely the dev-host URLs that no other machine can reach. Note the test is on the **saved** URL's host, not the loading install's, so the repair fires wherever the sitch is opened — a dev-saved sitch loaded on production is re-rooted onto production. Scope is every asset that goes through `loadAsset`: `CSituation.loadAssets` feeds it each entry of the sitch's `files`/`files2` plus the night-sky list, so models, tracks, KML, CSV and night-sky data alike, in any sitch saved from any branch or worktree build — while `videoFile` is explicitly skipped by that loop and takes a different path. Keyed on `/data/`, so an app URL carrying no such segment is not re-rooted. **Deliberately not fixed**: the save side still persists a resolved absolute URL for what is a static app asset, rather than the relative path it came from. The load side was chosen precisely because it also repairs sitches that are **already saved and already broken**, which a save-side change could not do. No tests accompany this fix.

## Version 2.127.0 (2026-08-11)

### New Features

- **Export Camera as KML (Photo): the look camera and its matched video frame as a Google Earth PhotoOverlay** (committed with this release; new `src/ExportCameraKML.js`; one import plus a `.perm()` button on `guiMenus.camera` in `src/index.js`; i18n `misc.exportCameraKML` in `src/i18n/en.js`; the *Export Camera as KML (Photo)* button in the **Camera** menu). Writes a KMZ — a zip whose root `doc.kml` refers to `files/frame.jpg`, since Google Earth will not fetch a `data:` URI — containing a `<PhotoOverlay>`: a `<Camera>` saying where the photographer stood and which way they faced, plus a `<ViewVolume>` giving the angles the photo's edges subtend. Google Earth flies to the Camera and pastes the frame into that volume, so if Sitrec's camera solution is right the photo lines up with the terrain, imagery and 3D buildings behind it — that alignment IS the test, which a plain `<Camera>` (viewpoint only, nothing to compare against) could not provide. Saved through `file-saver` as `<getExportPrefix()>_camera_<frame padded to 5>.kmz`, with `jszip` pulled in by dynamic `import("jszip")` so it stays out of the entry chunk. **Three coordinate conventions meet here and each is converted explicitly.** *Altitude*: `ECEFToLLAVD_radii` gives height above the ELLIPSOID, while KML's `altitudeMode absolute` means height above MEAN SEA LEVEL, so `meanSeaLevelOffset(lat, lon)` (EGM96, up to ~100 m) is subtracted — `altMSL = altHAE − N`. `absolute` is deliberate: GE Pro writes `gx:altitudeMode relativeToSeaFloor` in its own saves, which over land means height above the TERRAIN, and feeding an MSL altitude into that would lift the camera by the ground elevation beneath it. *Tilt*: KML measures from straight down (0 = nadir, 90 = horizon, 180 = zenith) against Sitrec's elevation-from-horizontal, so `tilt = elevation + 90`, elevation coming from `getAzElFromPositionAndForward`. *Roll*: a new exported `extractRoll(camera)` takes the signed angle about the view axis between the camera's up column of `matrixWorld` and a zero-roll reference (local up from `getLocalUpVector` with its along-view component removed), positive when up has tipped toward the camera's RIGHT — a right bank — returning 0 at the looking-straight-up/down degeneracy where roll and heading describe the same rotation. Measuring from the camera BASIS rather than reading the PTZ `roll` slider is what makes it correct whichever controller drives the camera; the sign agrees with Sitrec's existing horizon convention (`extractRollFromMatrix` in `src/SphericalMath.js`, positive = right bank) and is therefore the negation of the roll slider's value, since `CNodeControllerPTZUI` applies it as `camera.rotateZ(radians(roll))` (measured: slider +15 exports −15). `extractRollFromMatrix` itself is not reusable here: it references `V3(0,1,0)`, the fixed world Y axis, which in ECEF is "up" only at latitude 0, longitude 90E — its own header note flags this as a landmine for reuse. Nor is the ECEF-correct helper that note points to, `azElTurretImageRoll` (`src/TurretRoll.js`): that synthesizes the image roll an az-el turret would show from a line of sight and an aircraft's bank, where this measures the roll a camera already has from its own basis. **Field of view.** `camera.fov` is the vertical angle subtended by the FULL VIDEO FRAME, not by the look view — the look view is widened to `2·atan(tan(fov/2)/fovCoverage)` at render time and in `prepareCameraForLOD` when the video letterboxes — and the frame's angle is the one a PhotoOverlay needs. `viewVolumeFromCrop(fovV, width, height, crop)` builds a focal length in frame pixels, `f = height / (2·tan(fovV/2))`, and takes `atan(px/f)` for each of the four edges INDEPENDENTLY. They are symmetric only when the whole frame is used: `renderVideoFrameToCanvas` mirrors `drawAdjustedSourceFrame`'s source-rect computation in normalized [0,1] coordinates (same `in.zoom.v0 > 100` gate, same `panOffsetX/panOffsetY`, same clamp to `[0, 1−span]`), so a zoomed and panned video window — which makes `drawAdjustedSourceFrame` crop — yields a correct OFF-CENTRE frustum rather than a wrong symmetric one, and the balloon says the window was zoomed and the field narrowed to match. **Pose is read as RENDERED, not as stored.** Two of the look view's controls rotate the camera at render time rather than in the camera node — Camera Tweaks' X/Y offset (`applyCameraOffset`) and traverse display targeting (`applyDisplayLookAt`) — so the camera sitting in the node between renders can be aimed somewhere the look view is not. `getCameraKMLPose` brackets its read with those same two calls in the same order the render uses (`applyDisplayLookAt` outermost in `CNodeView3D`'s render, `applyCameraOffset` inside `renderTargetAndEffects`; `prepareCameraForLOD` composes them the same way), unwinding in reverse inside a `finally` so a throw cannot leave the live camera visibly rotated. The bracket is gated on `view.camera === camera` so one view's offsets can never be applied to another view's camera. Only the ORIENTATION half of `prepareCameraForLOD` is taken — the rest of it would apply the `fovCoverage` widening plus zoom and aspect, and this export needs the un-widened field. **`near` is derived, not chosen.** `PHOTO_WIDTH_M = 10` fixes the photo rectangle at ten metres across and `photoPlaneDistance` inverts the width relation for the distance: `near = 10 / (tan(rightFov) − tan(leftFov))`, falling back to 10 on a degenerate field. This is the rule Google Earth Pro itself follows — a GE Pro-authored PhotoOverlay with a ±0.1° × ±0.055° view volume writes `near=2806.68`, and 2806.68 · (tan 0.1° − tan −0.1°) = 9.80 m; the distance is large only because the lens is narrow. Holding the SIZE is what makes it work across Sitrec's 0.35°–80° FOV range: only the ViewVolume angles decide what the photo covers, so fixing the distance instead would give a wide-angle sitch a kilometres-wide billboard hanging over the terrain it is meant to be compared against, and a long-lens one a sub-metre speck. **Presentation.** The KMZ carries a `<Style id="sitrec-camera">` giving the overlay a camera icon on the globe (`IconStyle` → `camera.png`) and in the Places list (`ListStyle`/`ItemIcon` → `camera-lv.png`), both by public `maps.google.com/mapfiles/kml/shapes/` URL because GE Pro's own list icon `:/camera_mode.png` is an internal resource path that resolves only inside GE Pro; `<kml>` declares the `gx` and `atom` namespaces and the `<PhotoOverlay>` children are emitted in KML schema order, which Google Earth is forgiving about but other readers validate. Numbers are trimmed to 8 decimals for lat/lon and 4–6 for angles, with `-0.0000` (what an exactly level or exactly north camera produces) stripped to `0.0000`, and heading rounded before wrapping so a camera a hair west of north lands on `0.0000` rather than a literal `360.0000` that trips readers validating heading < 360. The `<description>` balloon carries sitch name, sitch time (`GlobalDateTimeNode.frameToDate(frame).toISOString()`), frame number, lat/lon with both MSL and HAE altitude, heading/elevation/KML tilt/roll, vertical FOV, and the image's FOV and pixel dimensions. **The image** comes from `videoView.drawAdjustedSourceFrame(frame, canvas)` — the same call the "Render Source Video" and "Export Video Frame" paths use — at the video's native resolution (dimensions swapped for a 90°/270° rotation) with the video window's rotation, colour adjustments, filters and A/B overlay applied, encoded by `canvas.toBlob("image/jpeg", 0.92)`. **Limitation, reported rather than hidden**: the look view's anamorphic Y-compress is applied after projection (`projectionMatrix.elements[5] /= yCompress`) and cannot be expressed by the square-pixel pinhole this export writes, so a `yCompress > 1.0001` adds a note to the balloon and a `console.warn` instead of silently exporting a squashed frame as if it were square-pixel — the same limitation, and the same treatment, as the camera fitter's status warning added in 2.124.0. **Fallback**: when there is no `video` view, no `videoData`, or the frame cannot be drawn, `cameraPlacemarkKML` writes a plain `.kml` with a Placemark carrying just the `<Camera>` and `<Point>` (no PhotoOverlay, no Style, no gx/atom namespaces) and a balloon line saying no video frame was available — a PhotoOverlay with no photo shows in Google Earth as an empty frame. `showError` covers the three hard failures: no `lookCamera` node, a position that did not convert to finite lat/lon/altitude, and a JPEG encode that returned no blob. The button is created in `initializeOnce` right after the permanent `cameraTweaks` folder shell and marked `.perm()` so it survives `menuBar.destroy(false)` on sitch load, like the *Export for FOV Editor* button above it — which places it below the permanent Location / Heading / FOV (Zoom) / Lens folders and above the per-sitch camera controls, with Camera Tweaks pushed to the end afterwards by the existing `moveToEnd` at the bottom of sitch setup. `extractRoll`, `getCameraKMLPose` and `viewVolumeFromCrop` are exported for testability; no automated tests accompany this release.

## Version 2.126.0 (2026-08-10)

### New Features

- **Lat/Lon Grid: a latitude/longitude graticule mode for the Ground Grid** (committed with this release; all in `src/nodes/CNodeGroundGrid.js`; i18n `groundGrid.latLonGrid` / `groundGrid.minPixelSpacing` / `groundGrid.maxPixelSpacing` in `src/i18n/en.js`; the *Lat/Lon Grid* checkbox and *Min Pixel Spacing* / *Max Pixel Spacing* sliders in **Objects → *Grid: ⟨name⟩*** and the mirrored floating *Edit: ⟨name⟩* menu). Switches the Ground Grid (added in 2.125.0) from meters-spaced lines to a graticule whose lines sit at ABSOLUTE multiples of powers of 10 degrees — a line is at exactly 28.733° or −117.71°, pinned to real coordinates at any grid size and zoom — with major and minor always adjacent powers (major = 10 × minor, derived in the shader) and latitude and longitude each picking their own power independently, since meters-per-degree differs between the axes (`getMetersPerDegreeCached` evaluates the static `metersPerDegreeAt` at the grid center, its cache invalidated in `updateMesh` when the bounds change). Step selection (`pickPow10`) keeps the MINOR spacing on screen within the new bounds: the smallest power of 10 at least *Min Pixel Spacing* (default 10, slider 2–100) wide, demoted if that exceeds *Max Pixel Spacing* (default 200, slider 20–1000) to the largest power not wider than the max — max wins when the bounds conflict, which also covers min > max — clamped to [1e-7°, 10°]; zooming in past the max subdivides a decade (0.0001° → 0.00001°), zooming out past the min coarsens one. Selection is per VIEW, not per frame: the main and look views render the same meshes with different cameras, so it runs in each mesh's `onBeforeRender` (`_latLonBeforeRender`, attached by `attachLatLonHooks` to every tile mesh, its skirt and the flat mesh — skirts share the material, so each must push its own offsets or it draws with another tile's; the `createOverlayTileFromTerrainTile` / `buildFlatMesh` overrides keep newly built meshes baked and hooked). `updateLatLonUniforms` estimates meters-per-pixel for the rendering camera — perspective from the camera's distance to the grid center and a focal length in pixels from `fov` and the drawing-buffer height, orthographic from `(top − bottom) / (zoom · heightPx)` — and must set `overlayMaterial.uniformsNeedUpdate = true` on every draw, the documented three.js requirement when changing a shared material's uniforms in `onBeforeRender`; without it a draw reuses the uniforms uploaded for the previous mesh or view — one view rendering with the other view's steps. Precision: absolute degrees don't fit float32 (a 1e-6° step at −117° needs ~9 significant digits), so each mesh bakes a per-vertex `aLatLon` attribute holding lat/lon RELATIVE to a per-tile reference (its first vertex), computed in JS doubles (`bakeLatLonAttribute` via `ECEFToLLAVD_radii`; a skirt shares its tile's reference), and `onBeforeRender` pushes per-mesh `tileLatOff`/`tileLonOff` uniforms — the tile reference minus an origin snapped to a multiple of the current MAJOR step, anchored under the camera and clamped to the grid bounds, so the values reaching the GPU are tiny exactly where fine lines are on screen. In the shader, `latLonMode` selects the line coordinates — `tileLonOff + vLatLon.y` / `tileLatOff + vLatLon.x` in degrees with per-axis steps, vs. the existing UV-times-size meters — while the always-drawn border keeps its own meters-based coordinates in BOTH modes, and meters mode reduces to the previous rendering (the `fwidth` floors drop to 1e-12, border 1e-9, since degree-valued coordinates run orders of magnitude smaller than meter-valued ones). While the mode is on, *Major Step*, *Minor Step* and *Rotation* are disabled — docked folder and mirrored floating edit menu alike, via each controller's `_mirrorControllers` (`applyLatLonMode`, also run when the GUI is built so a loaded save starts gated correctly) — and rotation is forced to 0, since a graticule only makes sense axis-aligned: `updateMesh` re-zeroes it against the 3D rotation handle and stale saved values, and the constructor zeroes it when constructed with `latLonGrid: true`. The step VALUES are untouched — the shader merely ignores them — so the meters grid returns with its old spacing on toggle-off; the rotation is NOT restored (no stash exists — the grid stays axis-aligned until re-rotated). *Min/Max Pixel Spacing* are conversely disabled while the mode is off. A per-view legend shows the spacing each view is actually drawing — *Major: 0.001°, Minor: 0.0001°*, splitting into *Lat Major: …, Minor: … | Lon Major: …, Minor: …* when the axes resolve to different powers — as a small DOM label bottom-center of the view (`updateLatLonLegend`, the view found by matching the rendering camera against `ViewMan` in `findViewForCamera`), colored to the grid's major color, hidden when the mode is off or the grid is hidden (a `show()` override), and removed in `dispose()`. Serialization adds `latLonGrid` / `minPixelSpacing` / `maxPixelSpacing` (defaults false/10/200) to the grid's `type: "grid"` record, flowing through custom-sitch saves and the overlay undo paths like every other grid parameter.

## Version 2.125.0 (2026-08-10)

### New Features

- **Ground Grid: a draped measurement grid on the terrain** (committed with this release; new `src/nodes/CNodeGroundGrid.js`; `createGridAtPoint`, the `type: "grid"` dispatch in `addOverlay`/`deserialize` and the `groundGrid_` id prefix in `src/C3DSynthManager.js`; `addGrid` and the kind-aware edit label in `src/CustomManagerMenus.js`; `kindName` in `src/nodes/CNodeGroundOverlay.js` and `src/nodes/CNodeGroundOverlayEvents.js`; i18n `custom.contextMenu.addGroundGrid` and the `groundGrid.*` block in `src/i18n/en.js`; **right-click the ground → *Add Ground Grid***, controls in **Objects → *Grid: ⟨name⟩*** and the mirrored floating *Edit: ⟨name⟩* menu). `CNodeGroundGrid` subclasses `CNodeGroundOverlay` with `noGUI`, so it inherits the whole overlay machinery unchanged — terrain-tile draping, corner/rotation/move handle editing with per-gesture undo (whose descriptions now read *Move/Rotate/Resize grid*), edit mode with the floating mirrored menu via `showOverlayEditingMenu`, goto, and delete-with-confirmation — but replaces the image texture with procedural anti-aliased lines in a `ShaderMaterial` fragment shader (`loadTexture()` is a no-op; there is nothing to download). The UV is scaled to meters (`gridWidth`/`gridHeight` uniforms kept in sync by `updateGridUniforms`, refreshed from `updateMesh` so drag/resize/undo immediately re-space the lines), each fragment computes its distance in meters to the nearest step multiple and divides by an `fwidth`-derived meters-per-pixel, so lines hold a constant screen-pixel width at any distance, with ±0.5 px smoothstep edges; a density fade `smoothstep(2.0, 5.0, step/mPerPx)` dissolves lines whose spacing drops under ~5 screen px instead of letting them alias into shimmer. Major lines composite OVER minor lines (`alpha = aMajor + aMinor·(1−aMajor)`, color un-premultiplied on output) so each keeps its own color at crossings, and the outline is always drawn at the major width and color so a grid with both steps at 0 stays visible and draggable. The material carries the overlay's log-depth + `depthBias` handling — including the orthographic `vDepth == 1.0` case, where the log formula collapses to a constant and the linear rasteriser depth is used instead — and terrestrial refraction via `applyTerrestrialRefraction_clip` / `installTerrestrialRefractionOnShaderMaterial`, so the grid drapes and bends exactly like the terrain it lies on. Units: `width`/`height`/`majorStep`/`minorStep` are stored in meters and edited through `gridParams` proxies in the current "small" units (`Units.small2M`/`m2Small`; altitude's proxy converts on through `scaleF2M`, since the base overlay stores altitude in feet per its `buildFlatMesh` contract), so the grid keeps its real-world size across unit switches; `updateUnitLabels` re-suffixes the five unit-bearing labels — mirrored floating-menu copies included, via `_mirrorControllers` — and the `changeUnits`/`updateDesc` hooks re-sync labels and values on a live unit switch or during deserialization. Controls: *Name*, *Visible*, *Edit Mode*, *Width*, *Height*, *Major Step* / *Minor Step* (0 = off), *Major Line Width* (default 1.5 px) / *Minor Line Width* (default 1 px), *Minor Brightness* (0–1, default 0.4), *Rotation*, *Altitude*, *Major Color*, *Minor Color*, *Lock Colors* (default on — minor follows major and its picker is disabled, mirrored copies too, in `applyColorLock`), *Opacity*, *Go to Grid*, *Delete Grid*. Creation via `createGridAtPoint`: 1000×1000 current small units with 100/10 steps, `resolveBounds` converting center + width/height to N/S/E/W bounds through `metersPerDegreeAt` (static, so it can run before `super()`). Serialization uses a `type: "grid"` discriminator in the manager's shared `overlays` list — `addOverlay` and `C3DSynthManager.deserialize` dispatch on it — with the full parameter set (bounds, rotation, altitude, steps in meters, line widths, `minorBrightness`, colors, `lockColors`, opacity), flowing through custom-sitch saves, the create-undo, and `deleteOverlay`'s undo alike. `kindName` ("overlay"/"grid") drives the delete confirmation, the undo descriptions and the context menu's *Edit Grid: ⟨name⟩* label, leaving every overlay-facing string byte-identical. Finally, `onContextMenu` is overridden to a no-op: the base handler places/removes photo-matching lock points on right-click in edit mode, which grids — having no image to match — do not use, so the right-click falls through to the normal ground context menu.

### Bug Fixes

- **Fixed floating edit menus freezing while 3D handles were dragged** (committed with this release; `CGuiMenuBar.updateListeners()` in `src/lil-gui-extras.js`). The lil-gui fork removed the stock per-controller `requestAnimationFrame` listen callbacks in favour of one central poll per rendered frame (`GUI.updateListeners()`, driven from `src/indexRender.js` via `Globals.menuBar.updateListeners()`) — but `CGuiMenuBar.updateListeners()` walked only `this.slots`, the docked menu-bar GUIs. Standalone floating menus (`createStandaloneMenu`) are independent GUI roots tracked in `activePersistentMenu`/`activeContextMenu`, never in the slots, so their `.listen()` controllers were never polled — and the mirrored edit menus depend on exactly that: `setupDynamicMirroring` (`src/CustomManagerMirror.js`) syncs user edits between the pair through `onChange`, and enables `.listen()` on the mirrors precisely for external changes, i.e. code writing the bound values. A 3D handle drag is such a change: the overlay writes its state and calls `updateGUIControllers()`, which repaints the DOCKED folder's controllers directly — so the Objects folder tracked the drag while the floating copy froze at whatever values it opened with. `updateListeners()` now also polls `activePersistentMenu` and `activeContextMenu`. This gives the new grid live width/height/rotation in its floating menu during handle drags, and fixes the same pre-existing staleness in the ground-overlay edit menu — and in any other standalone mirrored menu (the building and cloud edit menus use the same mechanism).

## Version 2.124.0 (2026-08-10)

### New Features

- **Flat Earth rendering mode, experimental** (`3d1fed3d`, `15437e91`, `afacad65`, merged in `0bd2a318`; new `src/scenarios/FlatEarthScenario.js`; registered in `src/CScenarioManager.js` with `activeInMods: mods.FlatEarth?.flatEnabled === true`; **Physics → Scenarios → Flat Earth** with *Flat Earth Rendering*, *Flatness* and *Center on Look Camera* — labels hard-coded, not i18n). Renders the scene as a flat disc under a north-polar azimuthal equidistant projection laid onto the plane tangent at the sitch origin, so the local terrain stays approximately where it was while the rest of the planet unwraps around it. RENDER ONLY by design: physics, tracks, LOS and every CPU-side calculation stay on the globe — the mismatch is the point; the mode exists to see what actually goes wrong when a globe's worth of data is drawn on a disc. The mechanism copies the refraction shader patching: a chained `onBeforeCompile` injects a vertex warp — gated by the shared uniform `uFlatOn` — into stock `<project_vertex>` materials, the terrain and globe shaders, and fat lines, applied as a delta onto the CPU-double-precision `mvPosition` so the float32 error at ECEF scale is a static sub-metre distortion rather than per-frame jitter. The camera is warped too, but only for the duration of each world-scene render (`warpCameraPose`/`restoreCameraPose`): moved through the point warp and rotated through the warp's numerical Jacobian (aim-preserving — the projection's anisotropic stretch skews directions), then restored, so a low-altitude camera far from the origin no longer films the warped ground from underneath and controls/readouts only ever see the physical globe-space pose. *Center on Look Camera* generalizes the warp to an OBLIQUE azimuthal equidistant projection centred on the camera footprint — the observer-centred AE map, distances and bearings true from the camera, re-centred every render as it moves. *Flatness* (0–1, default 1) is a per-view curvature drop: geometry sinks straight down by sqrt(r²+d²)−r at horizontal disc distance d from the view camera, with r = R/(1−f) evaluated in the cancellation-free form d²/(sqrt(r²+d²)+r); 1 is perfectly flat, 0 reproduces the true earth's drop on the flattened layout, and nothing draws at d ≥ r. Ground picking stays correct through the warp: `Globals.flatEarthPickGround` routes `raycastLocalGround` (the single source of the ground point under the cursor — orbit/zoom anchor, V/B measure, C/X camera placement) through a flat-space ray march against the served elevation surface via the newly exported `sampleGroundSurface`, with beyond-rim rays reported as open sky rather than clamped to the antipode. Tile selection is flat-aware end to end: quadtree culling spheres are warped via `Globals.flatEarthWarpSphere` so subdivision reaches the disc rim, subdivision runs under the warped camera pose (`Globals.flatEarthWarpCamera` in `CNodeTerrainUI`, restored in the finally), and Google 3D tiles get a `FlatAwareTilesRenderer` subclass overriding `calculateTileViewError` — warped bounding spheres, stretch-scaled geometric error, and a disc-space chord sagitta that refines antipode-adjacent tiles until the shader's 0.5° singularity cap culls the tear cleanly; tile materials are patched at creation via `Globals.flatEarthPatchMaterial` (terrain factories + `DayNightStandardMaterial.fromMaterial`), closing the LOD-swap gaps the 500 ms scene sweep left. State serializes through a `CNodeFlatEarth` node (`flatEnabled`/`flatness`/`centerOnLookCamera`, FloodSim-style); its `dispose()` turns the mode off, making sitch teardown the reset point — enabling Flat Earth in one sitch cannot leak into the next, and only a save with the mode actually ON re-activates it. Enabling with no anchor point (`Sit.lat/lon` undefined) hard-disables instead of rendering with stale projection uniforms. Disabled is a 100% no-op: the module is not even imported until the Scenarios menu is opened, and after a disable `uFlatOn=0` takes every patched shader down the original `gl_Position` path bit-identically while culling/visibility restores use strong Sets so tiles detached during LOD churn still restore. Known deliberate gaps: sprites and the night/day sky scenes are not warped, shadows and reflections stay geometric, and the grey polar caps are hidden while flat (they z-fight massively once flattened into the disc plane).

### Improvements

- **Faster startup** (`36c838e5`, refined by `18bb2655` from the PR #114 cloud review). Three loading changes from the 2026-08-09 loading review. (1) The sitch catalog (`getsitches.php`) is prefetched right after `setupConfigPaths` in `src/index.js` and awaited where it is used in `initializeOnce`, so the download overlaps the login/settings round-trips, node registration and menu building instead of serializing after them; from the review, an HTTP-error response is mapped to null (fetch only rejects on network failure, and a 5xx body would otherwise reach `JSON.parse`) so the use-site fallback fetch actually runs. (2) The geotiff library plus its pako/float16 dependencies (~340 KB of source) moves out of the entry chunk behind a cached dynamic import — new `src/geotiffLoader.js` exporting `loadGeoTIFF()`, same promise-cache discipline as `proj4Loader`/`openCVLoader`; consumers (`CFileManagerParse.js` TIFF/GeoTIFF import, `QuadTreeTile.js` GeoTIFF elevation tiles, `TIFFUtils.js`) were already async. Entry chunk 6.83 MB → 6.80 MB raw, −11 KB brotli. (3) The Astrometry.net asterism line set (`constellationsLinesAstrometry`) — the one night-sky file the build provably never reads in the default style — moves from `NightSkyFiles` to a new `DeferredNightSkyFiles` (`src/ExtraFiles.js`, loaded via `ensureNightSkyFiles()`); `CNodeDisplayNightSky.rebuildConstellationLines()` fetches it on first switch of *Asterism Style* (Show → Celestial) to *Astrometry.net*, or when a sitch saved in that style loads, with a last-request-wins guard (`_constellationRequest`) so switching away mid-fetch can never overdraw the style the dropdown shows, and `propagateLayerMaskObject` re-propagation so late-added lines appear in the look view. The star chart (`CNodeStarChartView`) tolerates absent line data and kicks the load itself; from the review, its redraw-skip signature now includes `FileManager.exists(lineKey)` for the current style, so a render landing mid-fetch cannot cache a signature the file's arrival fails to invalidate — the chart could otherwise stay lineless until unrelated input changed the signature. Rejected optimizations are documented at their code sites so they are not re-tried blind: parallelizing the sitch asset loop (`src/CSituation.js` — registration order would become completion order, and order-sensitive sitches laid out their views differently on every run), prefetching the geoid (`src/index.js` — asset parsers convert MSL altitudes before `ensureGeoidLoaded`, today with the grid absent, so making it arrive in time for parse silently shifts every parse-time altitude by the local geoid offset), and deferring the tile-decode worker pool (`src/js/get-pixels-mick.js` — shifted first-tile decode latency enough to change regression screenshots); the commit message records a fourth reverted attempt (lazy exifr) with no in-code comment.

- **AI assistant star names on any sitch** (`36c838e5`; `_loadIAUStarNames` in `src/CClientNLU.js`, comments corrected in `18bb2655`). The assistant's local "point at ⟨star⟩" / "lock on ⟨star⟩" handling (POINT_AT/LOCK_ON intents feeding `pointCameraAtRaDec`/`lockCameraOnRaDec`) resolves proper star names from the IAU-CSN catalog, which loads only with night-sky sitch assets — on any other sitch the names were simply never available, and the loader latched `_iauLoaded = true` BEFORE its null check, freezing "no names" in as the permanent answer for the session. It now reads `FileManager.get("IAUCSN", false)`, kicks `ensureNightSkyFiles("IAUCSN")` on a miss, and stays unlatched so the next lookup parses the arrived file. `CStarField.loadCommonStarNames` gained the matching missing-file guard — names are an enrichment, and a missing file should cost labels, not the stars.

- **Y-compress made visible to the camera fit** (committed with this release; `updateYCompressIndicator` in `src/nodes/CNodeView3D.js`, fit status in `src/nodes/CNodeFitCameraPoints.js`). The on-screen `Y-compress=…x` indicator — shown on the main or look view whenever *Main Y-comp* (View menu) or *Look Y-comp* (Camera → Camera Tweaks) is above 1 — now prints two decimals (`yc.toFixed(2)`): values like 1.01 are exactly the ones worth surfacing, and one decimal displayed them as a reassuring "1.0x". And Fit Camera to Points now appends a warning to its status line when the look view's `yCompress > 1.0001`: *"Look Y-comp is 1.01x — the fit assumes 1.00, so the look view will not overlay the video exactly"*. The solver models a square-pixel pinhole and the anamorphic squash is applied after projection, so the fit cannot see it — even 1% is ~5 px of vertical mismatch at the frame edges when blending the video over the look view, while displaying as a plausible-looking image. Found during the Moorpark video-overlay investigation, where the fit and overlay pipeline were verified exact and this was the one app-side hazard left.

### Bug Fixes

- **Fixed the terrain *Flattening* slider dying after any terrain rebuild** (`15437e91`; `CNodeTerrainUI.recalculate`). Sitches with a flattening control (`flattening: true` wires a `CNodeGUIValue` labelled *Flattening* into the terrain node in `SituationSetup.js` — e.g. *Pt Dume → Mt Jacinto*) link that node as a terrain input, and `disposeRemove` correctly refuses linked nodes — so every terrain rebuild (changing the map type, toggling *3D Buildings*) asserted in dev builds, and in production disposed the still-wired node and rebuilt the terrain without the input, leaving the slider silently doing nothing until the sitch was reloaded. `recalculate` now snapshots the old node's inputs, removes it with `unlinkDisposeRemove`, and re-adds the inputs to the rebuilt node. Same commit, adjacent hardening: `CManager.disposeRemove` asserts now print the actual node id, and polar-cap visibility at terrain construction goes through `updateGreySphereVisibility()` instead of a raw `dynamicSubdivision` check, so a terrain rebuilt while Flat Earth rendering had the caps hidden no longer brings them back.

## Version 2.123.0 (2026-08-09)

### New Features

- **Fit Camera to Points: fit keyframes, and camera motion between them** (`b460c04f`; new `src/FitKeyframeMotion.js` exporting `interpolateFitCamera` and `lerpAngleDeg`; new `src/nodes/CNodeFitPointsMotion.js` with `CNodeFitPointsPositionTrack`, `CNodeControllerFitPointsHeading`, `CNodeFitPointsFOV` and `attachFitPointsMotion`/`detachFitPointsMotion`; the keyframe store plus `activateKeyframe`, `solveKeyframe`, `refitOtherKeyframes`, `syncMotionOptions` and `landMotionCamera` in `src/nodes/CNodeFitCameraPoints.js`; `KeyframeRegistry.register("cameraFit")`; `tests/FitKeyframeMotion.test.js`; **Camera → Fit Camera to Points → *Add Fit Keyframe* / *Delete Fit Keyframe* / *Fit Keyframe Motion*** and the read-only *Keyframes* row — labels hard-coded, not i18n). The fit can now hold the same landmarks observed at several video frames. The 3D half of every pair is SHARED — a landmark is a fact about the world, not about a frame — while each keyframe carries its own 2D pixel positions and the camera the solver recovered from them: `{frame, uv, solved: {position ECEF, azDeg, elDeg, rollDeg, vfovDeg, fitted} | null}`. `points` always mirrors the ACTIVE keyframe's 2D coordinates (the one at `fitFrame`), so every existing edit/solve/draw path keeps working on `points` unchanged; `activateKeyframe` saves the mirror out and loads the new keyframe's `uv` in, and clears `lastResult`/observability on the way because residuals are per-keyframe — the old arrows would be drawn against the new pixels. Keyframes appear as yellow diamonds on the frame slider (pull-based `getFrames`, so the registry costs nothing to maintain; `<`/`>` step through them), and scrubbing onto one activates it for editing — only while the gesture state is fully idle (`pendingAdd`, `draggingId`, `_undoBefore` all clear), because an activation mid-drag would swap the point set under the cursor and leave one undo entry spanning two keyframes. *Add Fit Keyframe* requires *Enable Fit*, refuses a frame that is already a keyframe, first solves the existing keyframe from its own correspondences if it has no fitted solution (a loaded sitch restores points but deliberately never re-solves — the camera may have been hand-adjusted since) and refuses the add if that fails; the new keyframe's markers are seeded where each landmark projects through the camera at that frame (`projectThroughState` via `currentCameraState`), so the crosshairs open exactly where the landmarks would be if the camera had not moved, and dragging them to where the landmarks really are is what states the motion. With two or more keyframes, `attachFitPointsMotion` registers a *Fit Points* option on `cameraTrackSwitch` (key `fitPoints`), `CameraLOSController` (key `"Fit Points"` — on that switch the key IS the label) and `fovSwitch` (key `fitPoints`) — the *Position*, *Camera Heading* and *Camera FOV* dropdowns under **Camera → Location / Heading / FOV (Zoom)** — and the *Fit Keyframe Motion* button selects all three at once (it refuses, naming the frames, while fewer than two keyframes carry FITTED solutions). `interpolateFitCamera` is deliberately pure (no three.js, no node graph — that is what `tests/FitKeyframeMotion.test.js` tests): componentwise linear interpolation of ECEF position — a straight line at constant speed, indistinguishable from a geodesic at these scales — with shortest-arc interpolation for azimuth and roll (`lerpAngleDeg`, so +179° to −179° is 2° and not 358°), holding the end solutions before the first and after the last keyframe rather than extrapolating, and serving FITTED solutions only. The position track sets `lazyInterpolated = true` so `CNodeSmoothedPositionTrack` passes it through un-baked — baking would round the corners at the keyframes. The heading controller's lifecycle copies the Star Track camera options, which solved these problems first: it is attached directly to `lookCamera` with its enabled flag set explicitly to the switch's actual post-attach choice (an ungated absolute-pose controller silently clobbers whichever heading source is selected), Tracking Wobble is kept last in the apply order, and `detachFitPointsMotion` selects the fallback while the option is still an input, then clears the enabled flag after `removeOption`. While motion owns aspects, a solve updates the keyframe store per aspect instead of yanking the switches back to Manual: `motionOwnsAspects()` in `applyResult` skips the manual-node writes and switch selections for owned aspects (the stored keyframe solution IS the write-back — the motion nodes read it directly), skips `ptz.refresh()` when FOV is owned because refresh copies `ptz.fov` into `fovUI`, the MANUAL store, and skips the positional cross-check when position is owned because the track applies on the next frame. The FOV node holds the manual `fovUI` value — deliberately uncached, so it keeps tracking it — until any real solve arrives, so selecting the source early changes nothing on screen; the heading node takes its FOV from whatever `fovSwitch` says, so heading and FOV stay independently selectable. Dropping below two keyframes withdraws the options, with `landMotionCamera` first writing the camera the user is looking at into the manual nodes so the fallback lands where the camera already is. Serialization: keyframes save per-keyframe `uv` plus the solved camera as geodetic lat/lon with ELLIPSOIDAL height (the same storage the landmarks use — converts back to ECEF exactly; MSL is only for the user-facing `fixedCameraPosition`), while `points`/`fitFrame` keep their pre-keyframe meaning, so an older build loading such a save still gets a working single-frame fit, and a pre-keyframe save loads as one keyframe with no solved camera. `parseKeyframes` validates atomically: a keyframe whose `uv` cannot be matched to the points is dropped WHOLE rather than padded (padding would silently invent observations), and a malformed solved camera becomes null while its observations survive. On deserialize with ≥2 keyframes the options are attached inside the mod pass, so a saved *Fit Points* choice resolves through `CNodeSwitch`'s `pendingChoice` the moment the option registers.

- **Fit keyframes: seeded markers are not observations** (committed with this release, on top of `b460c04f` — found auditing the feature before release; the `[vx, vy, 1]` seed form of keyframe `uv` entries and `p.seeded` on the mirror, `realObservationCount`, `invalidateKeyframes(scope)`, the `_dragMoved`/`_markerMoved` gesture flags, `runFit` returning a boolean, the `enabled` gate in `refitOtherKeyframes`, seed re-projection in `solveKeyframe`, and the own-world fix in `fitHomographyRefracted`, all in `src/nodes/CNodeFitCameraPoints.js`; seed-aware `fitPointsAdd`/`fitPointsMove` in `src/CSitrecAPI.js`). The keyframe design invents pixels: adding a landmark pushes a marker into every OTHER keyframe by projecting the landmark through that keyframe's stored camera, and *Add Fit Keyframe* seeds the whole new frame the same way. Feeding such a pixel back into a solve lets the old camera vote for itself — on a freshly added keyframe, where EVERY marker is still a seed, a solve would "converge" instantly on the seeding camera and report a perfect fit of nothing, a fabricated solution that then drives *Fit Keyframe Motion* and serializes as `fitted`. So the two kinds are now distinguished at the store: a `uv` entry is `[vx, vy]` for an observation a person placed and `[vx, vy, 1]` for a seed, mirrored as `p.seeded` and cleared the moment the user drags that marker (the API's `fitPointsMove` clears it on any pixel edit, exactly as a hand drag would); a pre-seed-flag save has plain pairs, whose pixels were all treated as observations when it was made and stay observations now, and older builds validate only the first two elements so the shape is compatible both ways. Solves consume only real observations: `runFit` filters to `kept` and refuses — "The markers on this frame are still seeded guesses — drag each to its landmark before fitting" — when fewer than 2 remain while seeds exist; `solveKeyframe` solves from `realIdx` and demotes below 2; `refitOtherKeyframes` skips a keyframe with fewer than 2 real observations as provisional rather than failing (it stays `?` without counting against the status line); `result.pointIds` lists only the points the solve actually used, so no residual arrow is drawn for a seed (that would claim a disagreement with a landmark nobody measured), and `currentResidualPx` scores real observations only (measuring a camera against its own projection reports agreement that means nothing). Editing observations demotes the solutions they invalidate to `fitted: false` rather than deleting them — the camera is kept as a seed for the next solve and a hold for the display, but motion stops flying through it (`interpolateFitCamera` already skips unfitted solutions) and the readout marks it `?`: a 2D marker drag or a new point demotes the active keyframe, a 3D handle drag, a landmark world move (UI or `fitPointsMove`) or a deletion demotes all of them, and the status/residual/observability readouts retract alongside ("Points edited — Fit Now to re-solve"), so with *Fit on Change* off nothing on screen claims a fit that no longer holds and nothing stale serializes as fitted; with it on, the refit that follows re-promotes immediately. Gestures that moved nothing invalidate nothing: `_dragMoved`/`_markerMoved` are set only when a position actually changes, so a bare grab-and-release of a marker is inert. `fitNow` now runs `refitOtherKeyframes` only when the active solve actually ran (`runFit` returns a boolean; a refusal refuses the whole operation), and `refitOtherKeyframes` itself returns early when the tool is disabled, because API paths reach it without the GUI. At refit time a keyframe's surviving seeds are re-projected through its stored camera so markers visually track a moved landmark, while contributing nothing to any solve. Two API alignments: `fitPointsAdd` passes caller-supplied world coordinates INTO `addPointAtVideo` rather than patching them on afterwards, so the seeds pushed into the other keyframes are projections of the real landmark and not of a surface guess about to be discarded; and `fitPointsMove` world edits invalidate all keyframes and trigger the refits when *Fit on Change* is on. Finally, `fitHomographyRefracted` now lifts each correspondence's OWN `sp.world` instead of indexing `this.points` in parallel — `spec.points` is compacted (seeds filtered out before the solver sees anything), so parallel indexing paired pixels with the wrong landmarks whenever a seed sat between two real observations.

- **Fit Points API: drive the fit from MCP, with tile-surface screen picking** (`12a4a2a9`; seven new entries in `src/CSitrecAPI.js` — `fitPointsStatus`, `fitPointsConfigure`, `fitPointsAdd`, `fitPointsMove`, `fitPointsRemove`, `fitPointsSolve`, `pickWorldPoint`; new `src/FitSurfacePick.js`; new `docs/FitPointsAPI.md`, deliberately in `INTENTIONALLY_UNREGISTERED` in `tests/docsRegistry.test.js` so it does not appear in the Help menu). An AI agent (or script) driving Sitrec over the MCP bridge can now run the whole fit-points workflow without synthesising mouse gestures: read the tool's full state (settings, points, status/residual, current camera), configure `enabled`/`useTiles`/`autoFit`/locks/`method`, add/move/remove control points (video pixels as `vx`/`vy` in original video pixels or `fx`/`fy` fractions 0–1, readable straight off a screenshot; world positions as lat/lon with `alt` HAE or `altMSL` — the doc flags that mixing the two datums is a silent ~25–40 m error), run the solve (`fitPointsSolve` calls the same `fitNow()` as the button, including its acceptance gate), and ask what surface point a view pixel is showing: `pickWorldPoint` casts a `mainView`/`lookView` fraction against the 3D building tiles and returns lat/lon/alt. Adds and moves honour the same `onCorrectFrame` gate as the UI, so observations from different frames cannot be mixed into one solve. `surfaceAlongRay` and `groundUnderCanvasPoint` moved from `src/FitPointHandles3D.js` to the new `src/FitSurfacePick.js` because importing them into `CSitrecAPI` from the overlay module closed an import cycle through `CNodeViewUI` that broke the CSitrecAPI Jest suite at load; the overlay module re-exports both, so its existing importers are unchanged. `docs/FitPointsAPI.md` documents the agent workflow, the coordinate and altitude conventions, and the field-tested gotchas (invisible-LOD ghost hits, the near-point position collapse and how to seed past it).

### Improvements

- **The *Show Algorithm Working* replay is removed** (committed with this release; `src/FitSearchPlayback.js` deleted; `showAlgorithmWorking()`, `stepPlayback()` and the `playback` member removed from `src/nodes/CNodeFitCameraPoints.js`; `CAMERA_FIT_DEFAULTS.trace`, `runLM`'s trace parameter and `bestTrace` removed from `src/CameraPointFit.js`; `spec.trace`, the sample recorder and the sweep subsampler removed from `src/CameraPlaneHomography.js` — the `cameraAtFocal` closure survives as the answer path). The button shipped in 2.121.0 (`a3b92a9e`) and is judged not worth carrying. The deciding defect: `runFit` ran the new press-to-convergence re-solve loop only when NOT animating (splicing several descents together would have shown a search that never happened), so a replayed solve could land a camera an ordinary *Fit Now* press would still improve — after this release's convergence work the two buttons disagreed about the answer, and the replay was a path that could apply a non-converged camera. With it gone the re-solve loop is unconditional, `runFit(explicit)` loses its `animate` parameter (and now returns whether a solve ran, which the `fitNow` → `refitOtherKeyframes` gating relies on), and the solvers no longer carry replay instrumentation on the hot path.

### Bug Fixes

- **Fixed Fit Camera to Points ignoring terrestrial refraction — the render bent light, and nothing that projects did** (`b2d9cd03`; new CPU twin `src/atmosphere/terrestrialRefraction.js` exporting `terrestrialLiftContext`, `liftCameraRelative` and `liftWorldPoint`; `currentTerrestrialLiftContext` in `src/atmosphere/refractionSettings.js`; apparent-position `projectToCanvas` and iterative `groundUnderCanvasPoint` in `src/FitPointHandles3D.js`; `spec.liftFactory`/`state.lift` through `runLM`/`stateFromParams`/`evaluateCamera` in `src/CameraPointFit.js`; `liftFactory()`, `surfaceUnderVideoPixel` and `videoPixelForPoint` in `src/nodes/CNodeFitCameraPoints.js`; `tests/terrestrialRefraction.test.js`; the settings live at **View → Atmospheric Refraction** — *Enable Refraction*, *Terrain and Buildings*). Since 2.113.0 the solid scene is lofted by k·d/(2R) in the vertex shader, but the fit handles, the click that picks a surface, and the solver matching video pixels to landmarks all went through the plain camera. Nothing at 1 km; 57 px of a 393 px pane on a 38 km sightline from 13 km up. A control point placed on a landmark in the main view sat a lane and a half off it in the look view, and the solved camera absorbed the bend as a pointing error — a self-consistent lie, because every landmark at similar range is displaced by a similar amount and a pitch error absorbs it, which is how a fit could read 0.5 px on a point while visibly disagreeing with the footage (measured: 0.013° of bend against an 0.084° field — fifteen per cent of the frame hidden inside a plausible number). The CPU twin works on the camera-relative ECEF vector (view space is that vector one rotation later, and the rotation commutes with the lift) and routes through the same `terrestrialBendAngle`/`saturateLift` as the shader chunk, so the formula cannot drift between CPU and GPU; it returns null when refraction is off, so every caller's fast path is "no context, no work" and a disabled build is bit-identical to before. `projectToCanvas` projects the APPARENT position (observer taken from `matrixWorld`, matching the shader's uniforms); `groundUnderCanvasPoint` iterates aim → project → correct (tolerance 0.25 canvas px, 4 passes, and the map is a contraction) so a pick lands under the cursor ON SCREEN rather than along the geometric ray, keeping the last real surface when a correction overshoots the horizon; `surfaceUnderVideoPixel` mirrors the same loop for click-to-place, so a new point seeds on the surface that RENDERS at the clicked pixel. The solver takes the bend as `spec.liftFactory` — rebuilt at each candidate position in `stateFromParams`, because the bend is a property of where the observer stands and the optimiser moves the observer — while the multi-seed scan stays straight-line (a seed only has to land in the right basin; the LM refinement that follows carries the bend, so the answer does even though the guess did not); `evaluateCamera` takes it too, so the is-it-an-improvement gate compares one physics. The closed-form homography gets it by fixed point (`fitHomographyRefracted`): lift the landmarks to where the currently believed camera would see them, solve straight-line, re-lift about the answer — two passes, since the second is already a correction to a correction. Verified in the app with 3D probes at each control point's exact ECEF: handle-to-scene offset went from a uniform 56.5 px to 1.1–2.9 px against a 1.0–1.4 px measurement floor, and the CPU lift agrees with the shader lift to 0.1 px.

- **Fixed one press of *Fit Now* not finishing the solve** (`b2d9cd03`; `maxRestarts: 8` / `restartTolerance: 1e-6` and the winner-restart loop in `src/CameraPointFit.js`; `SOLVE_PASSES = 6` / `RESOLVE_EPS = 0.01` and the re-solve loop in `runFit` in `src/nodes/CNodeFitCameraPoints.js`; `sigmaFloorRatio` `1e-8` → `1e-6`). A run that ends at `maxIterations` has not converged, it has run out of budget — on an ill-conditioned configuration that is the normal outcome, because progress along a nearly flat valley is slow and LM's lambda has to be re-earned after every rejected trial. And the seed set depends on where the camera currently is (the caller's state is one seed, and the focal scan stands off from the landmark centroid along the caller's direction), so each press found a basin the last one could not see: measured on a 3-point 38 km case, four presses ran 176.9 → 62.8 → 62.5 → 62.4 → 61.1 px RMS while moving the camera 54 km, 2.6 km, 1.1 km and 13.4 km, before the acceptance gate refused the fifth. To the user that is a fixed control point wandering every time the button is pressed; what was actually happening is that each press was doing the optimiser's remaining work by hand, one budget at a time. Two loops finish it now: inside the solver, the WINNING run restarts from where it stopped until it stops improving (restarting also resets lambda, which is the point — a run that ended with lambda large is not stuck, it is taking tiny steps; a well-conditioned fit reproduces the same cost on the first restart and stops immediately, so this costs nothing there); and `runFit` re-solves from its own answer up to `SOLVE_PASSES` times, keeping a pass exactly when its RMS improves — the same metric the acceptance gate and the *Residual* readout use. One press now lands the answer four presses used to reach, and further presses move 0 m. Related: `sigmaFloorRatio` was 1e-8 while `kappaSevere` is 1e6, so every mode between them was reported as "cannot be determined by these points — held near its previous value" and then stepped anyway — and near convergence stepped HARD, because the SVD gain σ/(σ² + λ) tends to 1/σ as lambda decays, so the weakest mode takes the largest step of all. Measured on 3 points all at one range at 38 km: 2.29 km of camera slide along the range/focal trade-off and a 5.7% field narrowing per press, for an RMS change of 0.01 px. The floor is now 1/`kappaSevere`, freezing exactly where the diagnostics draw the line, which makes the promise the UI prints a fact.

- **Fixed the plane homography silently dropping its solved roll, and made the reported residual describe the applied camera** (`b2d9cd03`; `effectiveLocks()` and `scoreAgainstRealPoints` in `src/nodes/CNodeFitCameraPoints.js`, and the applied-residual cross-check in `checkAppliedCamera` with `APPLIED_RESIDUAL_SLOP = 0.5` / `APPLIED_RESIDUAL_FRACTION = 0.05`). The shipped defect: `applyResult` read the `lockPosition`/`lockFOV`/`lockRoll` flags that `syncMethodControls` greys out under the homography method — the decomposition recovers position, pointing and focal length together and cannot hold any of them fixed, but greying a control out only changes what the user can SET, not what `applyResult` reads, and it went on reading them. The visible consequence was roll, because *Lock Roll* defaults on: a homography that solved roll = 127.6° had it silently dropped, so the camera that got applied was not the camera that had been solved or scored — 254.9 px reported against 1145.8 px actually rendered, with the residual readout, the per-point lines and the acceptance gate all describing a camera the user did not have. `effectiveLocks()` now answers which locks the CURRENT solver can honour — none, under homography — while the saved flags are left alone, so switching back to the direct method finds them as the user left them. Second, the homography scores itself straight-line against whatever points it is handed, which under the new refraction path are lifted stand-ins (lifted about the previous pass's camera at that), so its self-reported rms answered a different question from the lift-scored current camera it was gated against — measured 123 px apart on a real sitch during this release's development. `scoreAgainstRealPoints` re-scores every homography result against the REAL landmarks through `evaluateCamera` with the same `liftFactory`, so the acceptance gate, the *Residual* readout, the dashed per-point lines and the outer re-solve loop all share one metric. And rather than enumerate the ways an applied camera can diverge from a solved one (a lock the solver could not honour, a switch that refused to select, a controller still driving the pointing), `checkAppliedCamera` now scores what actually got rendered against the same points and compares it with what was solved — absolute and relative slop both required, so a sub-pixel fit cannot trip it on rounding — reporting "the camera that was applied scores X px, not the solved Y px — something downstream did not take the fit" in the status line. It is the check that would have caught the dropped roll, and it makes this class of divergence impossible to miss silently.

## Version 2.122.0 (2026-08-09)

### New Features

- **Go To (`G`): one prompt for a frame, a date/time, a coordinate or a place** (`8095f7cf`; the `KeyMan.key('g').onDown` handler in `src/updateFrame.js`, with the old prompt body extracted unchanged into a new `goToFrame()`; new `src/CoordinateInput.js` and `src/DateTimeParser.js`; `docs/KeyboardShortcuts.md` and the `showKeyboardShortcuts` HUD list in `src/JetStuff.js`; **press `G`** — dialog title *Go To*, prompt *Frame, date/time, coordinates, or place name:*). Was *Go to Frame*: a `showPrompt` with `inputType: "number"` pre-filled with `String(Math.round(par.frame))`. It now opens blank and untyped, and resolves in a fixed order — a single bare number (`BARE_NUMBER = /^[-+]?\d+(\.\d+)?$/`, then `parseInt`) is a frame; otherwise `applyDateTimeString(text, GlobalDateTimeNode)`; otherwise `resolveLocationString(text)`, which parses every coordinate format locally before spending a geocoder round trip on a place name. The date/time attempt is safe to make before coordinates because `parseDateTimeString` requires the *whole* string to be date/time tokens and no coordinate format is (they all carry `°`, `′`, `″`, N/S/E/W or several decimals). The handler takes the event and calls `e?.preventDefault()`, because `showPrompt` focuses its input synchronously and the browser's default action would otherwise type the "g" that opened the dialog into it. A place lookup takes a ticket from a module-level `locationRequestSeq` and drops its result if a newer Go To has started, so two lookups in quick succession cannot leave the camera at the first place; frame and date/time never take a ticket, so they cannot cancel a lookup the user also asked for. Failure is a `showError` naming all four things it tried. `goToLatLon(lat, lon, above = 100000, back = 100)` matches the *Go To* button in the position menus (`CNodePositionLLA.goTo()` → `goToPoint(this.ecef, 100000, 100)`) and calls `moveTerrainTo()` first, because jumping somewhere far from the current terrain patch otherwise shows the bare grey sphere; the camera itself is fetched with `NodeMan.get("mainCamera", false)?.goToPoint?.()` since the key is global and not every sitch has one. The frame path is behaviourally identical to before — clamp to `lastSitFrame()`, widen `Sit.aFrame`/`Sit.bFrame` and dispatch `abFrameChanged` if the target falls outside, pause, clear `GlobalDateTimeNode.liveMode`, `updateFrameSlider()`, `setRenderOne(true)`.

- **Typed dates and times** (`8095f7cf`; new `src/DateTimeParser.js` exporting `parseDateTimeString` and `applyDateTimeString`; new `tests/DateTimeParser.test.js`). Accepts `12pm` / `9 am` (a bare hour *must* carry am/pm, or it would eat frame numbers), `noon`, `midnight`, `12:33am`, `15:20`, `15:20:30`, `17:33UTC` / `17:33 GMT` / `15:20Z`, `12/25`, `12/26/2000`, `Jan 5`, `Jan 6, 2020`, `5 Jan 2020`, and ISO 8601 including milliseconds — the form `Sit.startTime` is displayed in, so it can be pasted straight back. Two guards keep it from swallowing things that are not dates: `monthFromWord` matches a full name or its three-letter abbreviation exactly (so *May* is a month and *Mayfield* is not), and after every token has been consumed the leftover check `rest.replace(/[\s,]/g, "") !== ""` declines the whole string — which is what lets place names and every coordinate format fall through to the geocoder. Two-digit years are declined rather than have their century guessed, and a numeric zone offset (`+05:00`) is declined rather than silently ignored. `applyDateTimeString` writes `node.dateTime.*` exactly as `populate()` does and then calls `node.updateDateTime()`, so time-zone handling (`node.useTimeZone` / `getTimeZoneOffset()`), the live-mode reset and the recalculate cascade are identical to a slider edit; an explicit UTC/GMT/Z marker is read absolute regardless of the displayed zone. Only what was typed changes — unspecified fields are read back off `node.dateNow` in the frame the typed fields are in, so a time keeps the date and a date keeps the time of day. Impossible dates are declined rather than rolled over: `parseDateTimeString` rejects any day no year could make valid (`LONGEST_MONTH`), and `applyDateTimeString` probes `Date.UTC(year, month-1, day)` for a round trip, catching the one case the parser cannot — Feb 29 in a non-leap year, which `Date.UTC` would silently turn into Mar 1. The module is pure: it takes the date/time node as an argument rather than importing `GlobalDateTimeNode`, so it can be tested against a plain object.

- **Render Fade: *Render Whole Viewport*** (`ce24f9d4`, merged as `d786627c`; `fadeViewport` on `VideoExportManager`, `setupFadeMenu` and `exportFadeVideo` in `src/VideoExporter.js`, `exportViewportVideo` gaining `{plan, fadeOverlay, includeAudio}`; i18n `videoExport.fade.viewport.*`; **Video → Video Render &amp; Export → Render Fade → *Render Whole Viewport***, off by default). The fade schedule (`createFadeExportPlan`, with its `alphaAt`) can now drive the viewport compositor as well as the single-view one: `exportViewportVideo` accepts a pre-built plan instead of building the A-B one, and drives `fadeOverlay.transparency` — the same 0–1 the ***Vid Overlay Trans %*** slider writes, which `drawOverlay()` reads back while compositing — via a local `setOverlayAlpha`, called *before* `renderCompositeFrame` so that a settle re-render of the same output frame reuses the same alpha. `canvas.style.opacity` is kept in step only so the on-screen viewport fades along. Audio is passed explicitly (`includeAudio: false`) rather than read from `this.exportAudio`, so a fade export does not have to mutate the user's *Include Audio* setting; the progress widget reads *Exporting viewport fade...* when a fade is running. `exportFadeVideo` still requires the view named by *Render Video View* to have the overlay `findFadeOverlayView` identifies, whichever output path is chosen. Forcing that overlay visible for the render and restoring its `transparency`, `canvas.style.opacity` and visibility afterwards moved up out of `CNodeView3D.exportVideo` into `exportFadeVideo`'s `try/finally` — the one place both paths go through — so the "a fade asked for with the overlay hidden silently renders no fade" guard now covers the viewport path too.

### Improvements

- **One front door for typed coordinates** (`8095f7cf`; new `src/CoordinateInput.js` exporting `attachCoordinateInput`, `attachLatLonInputs`, `resolveLocationString`, `moveTerrainTo` and `goToLatLon`; wired into `src/nodes/CNodePositionLLA.js` — **Camera → Location** and the **Target** menu — and `src/nodes/CNodeTerrainUI.js`'s `latController`/`lonController` in the **Terrain** menu; new `tests/CoordinateInput.test.js`). Every box that takes a coordinate now goes through the same parser, so any format that works in one works in all: decimal, D M, D M S, hemisphere letters, the three degree glyphs `°˚º`, and MGRS, with a complete pair pasted into *either* box of a lat/lon pair filling in both. What was there before was hand-rolled inside each `CNodeGUIValue.onChange`, and had two limits worth recording. First, lil-gui's `NumberController` input handler does `parseFloat(this.$input.value)` and returns on `NaN` (`src/js/lil-gui.esm.js` ~line 954), so `onChange` never fired at all for text it could not read — `N40 26.767` and `S 45.5` were silently dropped, and only the latitude box handled pairs. Second, it was gated on `document.activeElement === $input`, so programmatic or automated entry parsed nothing. The new module registers on the same `input` event in the **bubble** phase, deliberately after lil-gui, so lil-gui keeps sole ownership of the plain-number path (`isPlainNumber`, clamping, elastic ranges) and we only correct the value when the text was something it could not read; and it captures the raw text in a separate **capture-phase** listener, because `updateDisplay()` rewrites `$input.value` to its own numeric parse whenever `_inputFocused` is false (lil-gui ~line 912) and would otherwise eat the longitude out of a pasted pair. Pairs split only on `insertFromPaste`/`insertFromDrop` or on `change` (Enter/blur), never mid-typing, so a half-typed `45.5, -1` is not grabbed and the box is not rewritten under the user; a single coordinate never rewrites the field either, so `45 30` stays editable for the seconds. `CNodePositionLLA` also lost its two duplicated terrain-recentre blocks in favour of `moveTerrainTo()`. (The Terrain lat/lon boxes are hidden while *Dynamic Subdivision* is on, as before.)

- **CoordinateParser: whitespace-separated pairs, and an opt-in loose mode** (`8095f7cf`; `parseCoordinate`/`parseLatLonPair` gaining a `ParseOptions` argument, new `splitAtSecondDegreeSymbol` and `splitWhitespaceHalves` in `src/CoordinateParser.js`; extended `tests/CoordinateParser.test.js`). Two degree glyphs in one string can only mean two coordinates — a single coordinate carries at most one, its minutes and seconds using `′`/`″` — so `25.299895° 60.430364°` and `40° 26' 46" 79° 58' 56"` now split at the last whitespace before the second glyph, everything before it (minutes and seconds included) belonging to the latitude. With no whitespace between them (`25.3°60.4°`) it declines rather than guesses. Bare whitespace is still not a pair separator by default, because `32 55` is ambiguous with `32°55'` and greedy pair-matching breaks live typing in a latitude field; callers holding a complete, submitted string (`resolveLocationString`, used by *Lookup* and Go To) opt in with `{loose: true}`, which accepts 2, 4 or 6 purely numeric tokens split down the middle and nothing else — so `Area 51` and `Highway 101 California` are still place names.

- **The *Lookup* box shares the same resolver, and reports failure through `showError`** (`8095f7cf`; `resolveLocationString` replacing the inline parse-then-geocode in `CNodePositionLLA`; i18n `positionLLA.lookup.tooltip` reworded to *"Enter coordinates in any format (decimal, degrees/minutes/seconds, N/S/E/W, MGRS) or a place name to move to"*). It already parsed comma-separated pairs, hemisphere-marked pairs and MGRS locally before falling back to the geocoder; what is new is loose mode's whitespace pairs and the degree-symbol pairs above, plus `alert()` on failure being replaced by `showError` on both the not-found and the caught-error paths. `resolveLocationString` returns `null` when `customLocationFunction` is undefined (serverless builds have no geocoder) — the *Lookup* control itself is still only created when it is defined, but the Go To key is global and needed the guard.

- **The night sky's star catalogue is credited to ESA/Hipparcos in the generated notices** (`965c7b7a`; a new *Hipparcos Catalogue (ESA)* entry in `DATA_FILES` and a corrected *Yale Bright Star Catalog (BSC5)* entry in `scripts/generateThirdPartyNotices.js`; an explanatory comment on `loadStarData()` in `src/nodes/CStarField.js`; surfaced at **Help → Documentation → Third-Party Notices**). `data/nightsky/sitrec_bsc_lite.bin` — the file the `BSC5` key in `src/ExtraFiles.js` actually points at, and the one the star field renders — is a repacked **Hipparcos** catalogue: 117,955 stars keyed by HIP number, magnitudes −1.44 to 14.08, in 22-byte records after a 28-byte header. Only the binary container is BSC5; the real Yale catalogue sits beside it unused as `BSC5.bin`, declaring its own 9,110 stars in 32-byte records. Verified by spot check: HIP 32349 reads 6.753 h / −16.71 / −1.44, i.e. Sirius. The Hipparcos credit had been added by hand to the checked-in `ThirdPartyNotices.txt` in `47185a0d` but never to the generator, and `ThirdPartyNotices.txt` is regenerated from `DATA_FILES` by the `postdeploy` / `postbuild-serverless` hooks — so the next regeneration would have dropped it and gone back to crediting Yale for the repack. It now lives in the generator, along with the Perryman et al. (1997) reference and a Yale entry that says plainly that its file is present but not loaded.

### Bug Fixes

- **Fixed video export drawing the 3D and the video overlay in different rectangles when *Match Video Aspect* is on** (`ce24f9d4`, merged as `d786627c`; new exported `getCanvasDisplayRect(view)` in `src/VideoExporter.js`, used by the overlay-child mapping in `CNodeView3D.exportVideo` and by the 3D-canvas blit in `VideoExportManager.exportViewportVideo`; new `getCanvasDisplayRect` tests in `tests/VideoExporter.test.js`; **Camera → *Match Video Aspect***). With `matchVideoAspect` on, the "Letterbox CSS" block in `CNodeView3D.renderTargetAndEffects` gives the canvas explicit px `width`/`height`/`left`/`top` so the 3D is centred in its div with black bars, matching how the video overlay pillarboxes itself in the same div. Both export compositors ignored that inset, and did so in mirror-image ways. The single-view export's composite canvas **is** that letterboxed canvas (`width = this.canvas.width`), yet it mapped overlay children with `width / this.widthPx` — the whole div — so every child was scaled and offset by the window-aspect / video-aspect mismatch; the viewport export's composite is in div space, and it stretched the 3D canvas across the full `view.widthPx × view.heightPx` while the overlays kept their own div-relative rects. Either way the sim and the video ended up in different rectangles, invisible when a view happened to sit near the video's aspect and glaring when it did not: on a 566×871 look view over a 0.5625 video the video landed 51 output px right of the sim. `getCanvasDisplayRect` reads the canvas's px style back (falling back to the full div for any canvas left at `100%`, or with a zero/absent style), and both paths now use it — overlays mapped into the canvas rect on one side, the canvas blitted into its letterboxed sub-rect with `(view.leftPx + rect.x)`, `(view.topPx + rect.y - ViewMan.topPx)` on the other. Views without a letterbox get the full div back, so *Render Single View Video*, *Render Viewport Video*, *Render Fullscreen Video* and *Render Fade* are all bit-for-bit unchanged there.

## Version 2.121.0 (2026-08-09)

### New Features

- **Fit Camera to Points: replay the search instead of jumping to the answer** (`a3b92a9e`; new `src/FitSearchPlayback.js` exporting `FitSearchPlayback` and `showTracedCamera`; `showAlgorithmWorking()`, `stepPlayback()` and the `playback` member in `src/nodes/CNodeFitCameraPoints.js`; `CAMERA_FIT_DEFAULTS.trace` and `runLM`'s new `trace` parameter in `src/CameraPointFit.js`; `spec.trace` and the `cameraAtFocal` closure in `src/CameraPlaneHomography.js`; **Camera → Fit Camera to Points → *Show Algorithm Working***, a button — label hard-coded, not i18n). A fit normally happens between one frame and the next: the camera is in the wrong place, and then it is in the right one. That hides the only part of it a reader can actually check. This button **re-solves** — `showAlgorithmWorking()` calls `runFit(true, true)` — rather than replaying a stored trace, so what is on screen is always the search that produced the camera being landed on; a stored trace could predate the last time a point moved. Both solvers gained an opt-in trace, off by default and never allocated when off. The direct solver takes it through `spec.options.trace` (merged over `CAMERA_FIT_DEFAULTS`, so it cannot clobber the other defaults); `runLM` snapshots the seed and then every **accepted** step only — rejected LM trials are not where the fit went — and only the **winning** run's trace is kept, because `bestTrace` is reassigned alongside `best` in the multi-seed refine loop, so the replay is the descent that actually produced the answer rather than a discarded seed's. `focalScale` is converted to `vfovDeg` on the way out, so a consumer replaying a trace never has to know about the base lens. The homography takes `spec.trace` and subsamples its existing 901-sample logarithmic focal scan (`N = 900`) down to `Math.min(140, samples.length - 1)` evenly spaced steps plus the focal it settled on — 142 entries in practice. Making that honest required a refactor: the "one focal length → one complete camera" block (decompose, place in the plane frame, convert to world, derive az/el/roll and VFOV) was extracted into a `cameraAtFocal(f)` closure, and the answer and every traced step now go through identical code, so the animation shows exactly the cameras that were scored. The answer path is otherwise unchanged — same below-the-plane failure message, same `diagnostics.heightAbovePlane`. **The two traces are different shapes, and that is the feature.** The direct fit is a *descent*: measured on a real seven-point fit, 12 accepted steps, VFOV 11.6° → 31.43°, RMS 69.4 px → 2.35 px. The homography is a *sweep*: every focal it scores implies a whole camera, so the replay slides the camera **8.2 km** along the focal/position trade-off while VFOV goes 162.3° → 31.25° and the score falls 0.633 → 7.5e-5. (The 162.3° start is the scan's 170° *horizontal* FOV end seen on a 16:9 image.) A camera travelling kilometres while the score barely changes is what an unobservable height looks like, which the `observability` string can only assert. Playback is driven off the **render loop**, not `par.frame`: `stepPlayback()` runs from `update()` and re-arms `setRenderOne(true)` each step, because `par.frame` is the video timeline and the search has nothing to do with it. The per-step hold is computed rather than fixed — `TARGET_FRAMES = 180` divided by trace length, clamped to `MAX_HOLD = 14` — because the two solvers differ by an order of magnitude in step count and a one-frame hold finished the 12-step descent in about a fifth of a second; so the ~140-step sweep runs one frame per step and the 13-entry descent runs 14, both landing near 180 rendered frames (a trace shorter than ~13 entries hits the ceiling and finishes sooner).
