## Version 2.87.5 (2026-06-20)

### Improvements
- **Larger, finger-friendly replay-sun slider in the SHF Starlink-flare predictor** (`tools/shf/skyview.js`, `horizonView`): the draggable "replay sun" below the horizon — the control that scrubs replay time — was enlarged for touch use. The sun disc radius grew 6.5 → 10, its rays and stalk scaled ~1.5×, and the transparent `replay-sun-hit` grab `<rect>` went from 32×50 px (`x=-16, y=horizonY`) to 68×62 px (`x=-34, y=horizonY-12`), now extending slightly above the horizon. The hit zone rides inside the translated `replay-sun` group, so it continues to follow the Sun as time scrubs. No behavioural change beyond the larger, easier-to-grab target on phones.

### Internal
- Removed the `setLayerMaskRecursive` import from `src/nodes/CNodeAtmosphericOptics.js` (added by the 2.87.4 Brocken-spectre look-layer fix). That helper lives in `threeExt`, which transitively imports `three/addons` ESM (`LineMaterial` etc.); Jest does not transform `node_modules` ESM, so `tests/atmospheric-optics.test.js` failed to parse in CI ("Cannot use import statement outside a module"). The webpack/browser build was unaffected. The call is now inlined as `this.brockenGroup.traverse(o => { o.layers.mask = LAYER.MASK_LOOK; })`, which is runtime-identical (visits the group root and every descendant mesh). CI-only; no user-facing change.

## Version 2.87.4 (2026-06-20)

### Bug Fixes
- Fixed the Brocken spectre / glory leaking into the main (god's-eye) view. The spectre is an observer-relative phenomenon — the glory sits at the antisolar point of the *look* camera — so it must only appear in the look (observer) view. In `CNodeAtmosphericOptics`, the world-space `brockenGroup` (the fog patch, glory rings, and shadow figure parented into `GlobalScene` so they depth-sort against terrain) was on the default WORLD layer and therefore rendered in every view. The group is now created with `this.brockenGroup.layers.set(LAYER.LOOK)`, and because each per-frame `_rebuildBrocken()` rebuilds child meshes that default back to the WORLD layer, `setLayerMaskRecursive(this.brockenGroup, LAYER.MASK_LOOK)` is re-applied at the end of every rebuild. Net effect: the spectre/glory (Atmospheric Optics → *Brocken Spectre*) now shows only in the look view, never the main view.
- Fixed the **Camera Motion (Background)** menu (Video menu) disappearing after the first custom sitch load of a session. `setupCameraMotionMenu()` in `CameraMotionFromVideo.js` builds the folder once, guarded by a module-level `folder` reference that is never reset. The folder lives under the permanent `guiMenus.video` shell, but neither the folder nor its controllers were themselves marked permanent — so `disposeEverything()`'s `menuBar.destroy(false)` recurses into them with `all=false` and destroys them on the next sitch reload. The never-reset `if (folder) return` guard then prevented any rebuild, so the menu vanished for the rest of the session after the first custom sitch. A `permAll(folder)` recursion now calls `.perm()` on the folder and every controller so they survive sitch reloads (same fix pattern as the Render Debug folder in `CNodeView3D` and the File Analysis menu in `VideoFolderAnalysisUI`).

### Improvements
- Windows install/management parity with the Unix scripts. `7cf21bda` adds a `sitrec.ps1` PowerShell management script (with a `sitrec.cmd` launcher that prefers `pwsh.exe`, falling back to `powershell.exe`) supporting `start`/`stop`/`restart`/`pull`/`versions`/`bake`/`update`/`logs`/`status`, substantially expands `install.ps1`, and brings `download-videos.ps1` in line with the shell versions. The shell installer (`install.sh`) now mounts the local `sitrec-videos/` folder by default with a new `--no-videos` opt-out (previously `--videos` was opt-in), so the later `download-videos` step no longer silently writes files the container cannot see.
- Clearer Docker/Podman "engine not running" errors on Windows. `c0675c8c` adds `Test-DockerReady`/`Test-PodmanReady` (`docker info` / `podman info` probes) and an `Assert-RuntimeReady` gate to `install.ps1` and `sitrec.ps1`. When the runtime is installed but its engine isn't running, the scripts now print an actionable message (start Docker Desktop / `podman machine start`, the WSL 2 engine hint, and the exact command to rerun) instead of a generic command-failed error.

## Version 2.87.3 (2026-06-17)

### Improvements
- Added a smooth **Rotate** (roll-about-view-axis) transform to **Camera Nudge** in the Long Exposure feature (Video ▸ Long Exposure ▸ Camera Nudge). Previously Camera Nudge produced only the damped-spring angular *jolt* (the bumped-tripod bounce from `nudgeOffsetAngles`); it can now additionally apply a steady roll about the camera's view axis, which curves otherwise-straight star/satellite light trails into arcs in the long-exposure render. In `src/nodes/CNodeControllerCameraNudge.js`, four params were added to `nudgeParams` and `defaultNudgeParams()` — `rotateStart` (default 0 s), `rotateDuration` (default 1 s), `rotateEase` (default 0.1), and `rotateTotalAngle` (default 0°, i.e. off) — driven by a new pure, deterministic `rotateOffsetRoll(t, p)`. That function sweeps `rotateTotalAngle` over `rotateDuration` starting at `rotateStart`, using a trapezoidal-velocity easing profile (the angular rate ramps up over the first `rotateEase` fraction of the duration and back down over the last, constant in between; `ease=0` → constant rate, `0.5` → full ease-in/out), and then HOLDS at the full angle for the remainder of the exposure. The roll is folded into `nudgeQuaternion()` as a `rotateZ` composed *after* the existing `rotateY(yaw)·rotateX(pitch)`, and the live controller's `apply()` matches that order (`rotateY`, `rotateX`, then `rotateZ`). `src/LongExposure.js` adds the four matching sliders (*Rotate Start (s)*, *Rotate Duration (s)*, *Rotate Ease*, *Rotate Total Angle (°)*) to the Camera Nudge folder. Because everything routes through the single analytic `nudgeQuaternion(t)`, the offline sub-frame splat renderer that draws the curved trails, the live look-view, and the trajectory overlay all pick up the roll with no renderer changes. Serialization flows through the existing `nudgeParams` mechanism; the default `rotateTotalAngle` of 0 is a no-op (`rotateOffsetRoll` early-returns 0), so existing sitches are unaffected and the change is regression-safe.

## Version 2.87.2 (2026-06-17)

### Bug Fixes
- Fixed the Docker entrypoint crashing at startup with `/var/www/html/shared.env.php: Permission denied` when the image runs under a non-root UID (rootless Podman with `--user`, OpenShift's arbitrary assigned UIDs, etc.). `docker/entrypoint.sh` regenerates `shared.env.php` and re-injects the `window.__SITREC_ENV__` `<script>` into `index.html` on every container start, but both files ship root-owned in the image. A non-owner UID cannot modify them in place — rootless overlay copy-up of a file you don't own is denied even at mode 666 — and the webroot's sticky bit also blocked deleting them. The fix is two-part: (1) the entrypoint now **delete-and-recreates** both files instead of overwriting in place — `rm -f "$ENV_PHP_FILE"` before writing the fresh `shared.env.php`, and for `index.html` it captures the `sed` output into `NEW_HTML`, then `rm -f "$HTML_FILE"` and `printf` a fresh file rather than using `sed -i`; (2) `Dockerfile` and `Dockerfile.release` add `RUN chmod 0777 /var/www/html`, which clears the sticky bit on the already-world-writable (1777) webroot so a non-owner UID can remove and recreate those files. Verified by reproducing the original error under `--user 1000:1000`, confirming the entrypoint then completes (both files generated correctly) for non-root and root, and that a full root run still serves HTTP with no regression.

## Version 2.87.0 (2026-06-17)

### New Features
- **One-line install-time baking** (`install.sh --bake <target-image>`): the one-line installer can now bake a self-configured image without first installing Sitrec. `curl … | bash -s -- --bake registry.example.com/sitrec:configured --env-file prod.env` builds a new image FROM the published `ghcr.io/mickwest/sitrec2:<base>` with the env file embedded as `ENV` layers, then **exits** — it does not create a `sitrec/` install directory or run a container. New flags `--bake <target>`, `--env-file <file>` (default `.env`), `--base <tag>` (default `latest`), `--push`, and `--tarball [path]` (save the baked image via `<runtime> save`, default name derived from the target with `sed 's|[^A-Za-z0-9_.-]|_|g'`). The env→`ENV` parser is inlined into a new `bake_image()` function and mirrors `docker/entrypoint.sh` and `sitrec.sh bake` (skips blanks/comments/empty values, strips optional `export `, splits on the first `=`, strips one surrounding quote layer, escapes `\`/`"`/`$`); it errors if the env file is missing or yields zero usable `KEY=value` lines, and prints the same security warning as `sitrec.sh bake`. A post-parse reconciliation block handles argument order: a bare `--tarball` parsed *before* `--bake` lands in the install-from-tar variables (`USE_TARBALL`/`TARBALL_PATH`), so when `BAKE_MODE` is set it is reinterpreted as `BAKE_TARBALL`/`BAKE_TARBALL_PATH` — otherwise bake mode would `exit 0` before the install path and the tarball would be silently dropped. `--bake-tarball`/`--save-tarball` are accepted as explicit aliases.
- **Deploy a specific image with `install.sh --image <image>`**: the normal install path and the air-gapped `--offline` flow now accept `--image` to install/run a chosen image instead of the hard-coded `ghcr.io/mickwest/sitrec2:latest`. The value (`INSTALL_IMAGE`, default `${IMAGE}:latest`) is written into the generated `docker-compose.yml` `image:` line and used for the support-file extraction `create`. This closes the loop with baking: `./install.sh --image registry.example.com/sitrec:configured` pulls a baked image from a registry, and `./install.sh --offline --image sitrec-configured:latest` runs one already loaded from a tarball (Podman often loads it as `localhost/<name>:tag`, so the exact loaded name must be passed). `--image` validates that an argument follows and that it doesn't start with `--`.

### Improvements
- **`sitrec.sh bake` can save a tarball** (`./sitrec.sh bake … <target-image> [--tarball [file]]`): the existing `bake` command (shipped 2.85.0) gains `--tarball`/`--save-tarball`, running `<runtime> save -o <path> <target>` after the build so a configured image can be written to a single `.tar` for USB/`scp` transfer to an air-gapped host. The path is optional; when omitted the filename is derived from the target image name (`sed 's|[^A-Za-z0-9_.-]|_|g'` + `.tar`). It composes with `--push` (save and push in one run). A parser guard prevents a bare `--tarball` placed *before* the `<target-image>` from swallowing the target as its path — the next token is only consumed as the tarball path once `TARGET` is known. Usage/help strings and the developer install guide updated to show the new option.

### Documentation
- Reworked the "Baking a Pre-Configured Image" section of `docs/dev/Installing-and-configuring.md` (now marked **Advanced** with a "most people don't need this" signpost): a quick-path tarball example, a unified options table (shared by `sitrec.sh bake` and `install.sh --bake`), Podman insecure-registry/`login` notes and a macOS `podman machine` caveat, a "deploy with `--image`" snippet, a secrets-out-of-the-image pattern, and a single-architecture caveat (a baked image is built for the host CPU architecture, since it adds layers rather than copying the base's multi-arch manifest). The air-gapped section is updated to use `install.sh --bake … --tarball` and `--image`, and the Configuration note now explains that `./sitrec.sh restart` recreates the container so `.env` changes apply without touching the saved `.env`. Several `github.com/MickWest/sitrec2` clone URLs corrected to `Sitrec2`.

## Version 2.86.0 (2026-06-16)

### New Features
- **Brocken Spectre** (Lighting → Atmospheric Optics (Halos) → Brocken Spectre): adds a physically-modelled Brocken spectre — the observer's own shadow cast onto fog with a colored glory around the antisolar point — to `CNodeAtmosphericOptics` (`src/nodes/CNodeAtmosphericOptics.js`, +442). Unlike the existing sky-dome halos, the spectre is built as **world-space, depth-tested geometry** in `GlobalScene` (a `brockenGroup`, named `atmosphericOpticsBrocken`, anchored at the antisolar point a settable slant distance below/in-front of the observer), so it depth-sorts correctly against terrain — hidden behind far peaks, occluded by nearer ones — like a real spectre on valley fog. `_syncBrocken(observerPos)` rebuilds it (via `_rebuildBrocken`) only when the Sun direction, observer position, or a parameter key changes, and only when the Sun is above the horizon. Three layered, depth-write-off components ordered by `renderOrder`:
  - **Glory** (`_buildBrockenGlory`): a per-pixel Airy-diffraction shader (`gloryShaderMaterial`, `uDroplet` uniform) on a single quad. Ring radii come from fog-droplet diffraction (x = π·d·sinθ/λ, intensity maxima at 5.14, 8.42, 11.62), with blue-inner/red-outer tinting and fainter secondary/tertiary rings; droplet diameter sets the angular scale (smaller droplets → larger glory). A single quad (rather than a tessellated mesh) avoids additive-MSAA edge streaks, and the shader includes the `logdepthbuf` chunks required by Sitrec's logarithmic depth buffer.
  - **Shadow Figure** (`_buildBrockenShadow`): a soft, diffuse humanoid silhouette hanging down from the antisolar point, drawn last so it darkens the bright glory center (the head reads as a dark form inside the rings).
  - **Fog Bank** (`_buildBrockenFog` / `_buildBrockenBand`): an optional synthetic fog patch centered on the antisolar point so the spectre is visible even when the scene has no real cloud/fog geometry.
  - GUI subfolder (added under the existing "Atmospheric Optics (Halos)" Lighting folder) with literal English labels: master toggle **Show Brocken Spectre** (`brocken`), **Glory (rings)** (`brockenGlory`), **Shadow Figure** (`brockenShadow`), **Fog Bank** (`brockenFog`), and sliders **Fog Brightness** (`brockenFogOpacity`, 0–1), **Fog Distance (m)** (`brockenDistance`, 50–5000, default 350), **Spectre Size°** (`brockenRadius`, 1–15°, default 5), and **Droplet Size (µm)** (`brockenDroplet`, 3–40, default 10, with a tooltip explaining the diffraction relationship — ~10µm hill fog gives a first red ring ≈6°). All nine properties are in `simpleSerials` and persist in saved sitches.

## Version 2.85.0 (2026-06-16)

### New Features
- **Getting Started link** (Help → Getting Started): a new top-level Help entry, alongside *What's New*, opening the rewritten `docs/CustomSitchTool.md` (retitled "Getting Started with Sitrec"). The Help menu and the AI assistant's doc list are now both built from a single source of truth, `src/docsRegistry.js` (`helpDocs` array + `getChatAvailableDocs()`): `src/index.js` iterates `helpDocs` (top-level entries flagged `top:true`, the rest under the Documentation folder) and `CNodeViewChat` derives its `getHelpDoc` doc names from the same `file` fields. Previously the two lists were maintained separately and had drifted — the chat list named files that didn't exist (`SavingLoadingSharing`, `ObjectTracking`), so `getHelpDoc` returned an error mid-conversation; deriving the chat doc-name from the menu's real `docs/<Name>.md` path makes that class of bug structurally impossible. New i18n key `menus.help.gettingStarted`.
- **Google Gemini chat models** (AI assistant model picker): `sitrecServer/chatbot.php` gains a `callGemini()` provider (generativelanguage REST, `gemini-2.5-flash-lite` default) plus `convertToolsForGemini()` to map the OpenAI-style tools array onto Gemini `functionDeclarations`. Wired into `getApiKeyForProvider()`, `getAvailableModels()`, and `runToolLoop()`. Gemini entries stay hidden from the model picker unless the server has `GEMINI_API` set (new key in `config/shared.env.example`).
- **Docker `bake` command** (`./sitrec.sh bake [--env-file <f>] [--base <tag>] [--push] <target-image>`): builds a self-configured image *FROM* the published `ghcr.io/mickwest/sitrec2:<tag>`, adding one `ENV` layer per variable in a `.env` file (no app rebuild — the existing entrypoint reads the baked `ENV` at container start). Optional `--push` ships it to a registry. Because Docker `ENV` is lowest priority, a deployment can still override any baked value with runtime `-e`/`env_file`. The env parser mirrors the entrypoint (skips blanks/comments/empty values, optional `export `, strips one quote layer, escapes `\`, `"`, `$`) and deliberately avoids the `[![:space:]]` trim idiom for macOS bash 3.2 compatibility. Documented under "Baking a Pre-Configured Image" in `docs/dev/Installing-and-configuring.md`, including the security warning that all baked values (API keys, S3 credentials) are recoverable from `docker history`/`inspect`, so only push to a private registry.

### Improvements
- **AI chat model line-up overhaul** (`sitrecServer/chatbot.php`): per-tier `$MODEL_PERMISSIONS` updated to current models — `gpt-5-mini` (new best-value default, replacing `gpt-4o`), `gpt-5-nano`, `gemini-2.5-flash-lite`, `claude-haiku-4-5`, admin-only `claude-sonnet-4-6` / `claude-opus-4-8` / `grok-4-fast`. Default model functions updated (`callOpenAI` → `gpt-5-mini`, `callAnthropic` → `claude-haiku-4-5`, `callGrok` → `grok-4-fast`).
- **Clickable links in AI chat replies** (chat view): `CNodeViewChat.addSystemMessage` now renders bot text through the new shared `src/linkify.js` (`linkifyToHTML`/`hasLinks`), so help-doc links and URLs are clickable; `CNodeNotes` was refactored to use the same helper so links look and behave identically in both. `linkify.js` HTML-escapes first, then matches absolute `http(s)` URLs *and* relative help-doc paths (`docs/<Name>.html`, `README.html`) resolved against `document.baseURI`. The chat system prompt now lists each doc with its `docs/<Name>.html` path and instructs the model to cite the exact path inline and in a "See also:" list, never inventing links.
- **AI chat reliability** (`sitrecServer/chatbot.php`): `callOpenAI` now sends a model-aware request body — GPT-5/o-series reasoning models only accept default temperature (custom values 400), so `temperature:0.2` is sent only for non-reasoning models, and GPT-5 requests `reasoning_effort:"minimal"` to avoid the multi-step tool loop hitting PHP/proxy timeouts. API errors from OpenAI and Gemini are now surfaced as the reply text instead of silently returning empty text. Anthropic calls add a `cache_control: ephemeral` breakpoint on the system block so the large tools+prompt prefix is prompt-cached across turns (~10% of input cost on repeats). The `getHelpDoc` truncation limit was raised from 8000 to 20000 characters.
- **"How/why" questions routed to the AI** (chat view): `CNodeViewChat.handleMessage` short-circuits text starting with "how"/"why" straight to the LLM, and `CClientNLU` adds a `NEVER_CORRECT` set of question/function words so fuzzy keyword matching can't "correct" *how* → *show* (one edit away). Previously "how do I have a track of az/el" was mis-parsed into an "Enabled…" toggle command.
- **Degrees-based trig in the chat calculator** (`CClientNLU`): the quick-calc path now evaluates against a local mathjs instance (`mathDeg`) configured so `sin/cos/tan/...` take degrees by default (Google-calculator style) and inverse trig returns degrees; explicit units (`cos(1 rad)`, `cos(30 deg)`) still win. It's a local instance, so the global mathjs used elsewhere (e.g. `CNodeMath`) keeps standard radians.

### Bug Fixes
- **Fixed dragging a sitch-browser sidebar link** (`d97d5d92`, `src/CSitchBrowser.js` / `src/DragDropHandler.js`): click-dragging a sidebar link (All, Featured, Private, Deleted, Unlabeled, List, Thumbnails) started a native link-drag carrying the page's own URL, which `DragDropHandler` then tried to load as a file ("Unsupported URL host or page type: local.metabunk.org"). Fix sets `draggable=false` on the sidebar anchors (they stay click-only and still work as pointer-based drop targets for dragging a sitch onto a Label) and adds an `internalDragActive` guard in `DragDropHandler` — set on `dragstart` (skipping already-prevented drags so the sitch-tile custom drag isn't tripped), cleared on `dragend`/`onDrop` — so any in-page drag is silently ignored and the drop-zone overlay no longer flashes. External file/URL drops are unaffected.

### Documentation
- Substantive content-accuracy pass across the user docs: `CustomSitchTool.md` rewritten as the Getting Started guide (load a Featured example, set location by name, set Start/Now Time, sync video, dynamic-subdivision terrain, add satellites); `TraverseMethods.md` updated for the actual menu labels ("Global Fit:" prefix, "Const Acceleration", Monte Carlo 1/2, new Physics method); `Wind.md` altitude range corrected to 0–60 000 ft; `UserInterface.md` terrain default corrected to ESRI World Imagery; `GIS.md` `LLA-ECEF-ENU.ts` extension fix; `gimbal-recreate.md` "Gimbal Analysis" menu label; `LensGhost.md` "[BETA]" menu prefixes. Developer install guide gains the `bake` section.

## Version 2.84.4 (2026-06-16)

A correctness pass on Atmospheric Optics (Halos), plus an opt-in admin telemetry feature and a build-tooling security bump.

### Bug Fixes
- **Halos now centre on the camera actually being rendered, refract with the sky, and respect observer altitude.** Reworks `CNodeAtmosphericOptics.js` (commit `553a429a`). `CNodeView3D.renderSky()` now calls `NodeMan.get("theHalos")?.syncToObserver(camera.position)` for both the main and look cameras, so the shared sky scenes no longer inherit the look-camera observer — the halos sit on the rendered Sun/Moon in whichever view is being drawn (the same per-camera re-sync already done for planet sprites). The new `syncToObserver(observerPos, date)` replaces the old `update()` body and drives three new behaviours: (1) **refraction coupling** — when the night-sky refraction shader is on, each optic's mesh directions are bent through `applyRefractionECI()` using `refractionOptsFromUniforms()` / `refractionUniforms.uZenithECEF`, so halos bend with the same refraction state as the Sun/Moon disks (`_applyOpticRefraction`, rebuild keyed on `_refractionKey()`); (2) **observer-altitude horizon fade** — `_updateHorizonFade()` derives the dip-of-horizon from the observer's geodetic height (`ECEFToLLAVD_radii`, `horizonElev = −acos(surfaceR/observerR)`) and offsets the per-vertex horizon cut (`_horizonSinLo/_horizonSinHi`), so the below-horizon fade is correct from altitude rather than pinned to a flat 0°; (3) a rebuild trigger when the observer moves (`observerPos.distanceToSquared(this._lastObserver) > 1`) or the refraction/horizon keys change.
- **Plate-crystal optic geometry corrected.** New exported, unit-testable centreline formulas replace the previous hand-placed shapes: `circumzenithalCenterAltitudeDeg()`, `circumhorizontalCenterAltitudeDeg()`, `sunDogOffsetsDeg()`, and the general `platePrismDeviationRay()` (60° ice prism, Bravais effective index along the conserved prism-edge component, `HALO_ICE_INDEX = 1.31`), with onset elevations `CZA_MAX_ELEV_DEG` / `CHA_MIN_ELEV_DEG` derived from `n` rather than literals. New `tests/atmospheric-optics.test.js` (95 lines) pins these. A zenith-singularity guard in `_setBasis()` now picks an alternate horizontal axis when `|Z.x|` is large, so a near-overhead Sun/Moon no longer produces a degenerate basis.
- **Lunar halos/dogs now scale by visual phase brightness, not illuminated fraction.** `_buildMoon()`'s old `illum = 0.35 + 0.65·k` (k from Sun–Moon dot) is replaced by `lunarOpticsPhaseScale(sunMoonDot)`, an empirical magnitude curve (`magDrop = 0.026·phaseAngle + 4e-9·phaseAngle⁴`, `10^(−0.4·magDrop)`); the build early-returns when `illum ≤ 0.002`, so a quarter Moon is far dimmer than half-of-full and thin crescents contribute essentially nothing — matching how faint real lunar halos are.

### New Features
- **UI menu-interaction logging** (opt-in, admin/self-host telemetry; off by default). New client module `src/UILogging.js`: `initUILogging()` (called from `index.js` right after `Globals.menuBar = new CGuiMenuBar()`) installs a capture-phase `mousedown` listener; `buildMenuPath()` walks the lil-gui DOM (`.controller > .name`, else `.title`, then up the `.lil-gui` folder chain) to build a slash-separated path like `"Camera/Smoothing/Camera Smooth Window"`, buffers `{ts, path}` (cap `MAX_BUFFER = 500`, `MAX_PATH_LEN = 300`), and flushes a batch every `FLUSH_INTERVAL_MS = 10000` ms — plus on `pagehide`/`visibilitychange→hidden` via `navigator.sendBeacon`. Gated three ways (defence in depth): no-op on serverless (`isServerless`), no-op unless `getEnvBool("LOG_UI_INTERACTIONS")`, and the server endpoint independently refuses to write when its flag is off. New server endpoint `sitrecServer/uilog.php`: gated on `getenv('LOG_UI_INTERACTIONS')` (returns a benign `{disabled:true}` 200 otherwise so stale clients don't error), rate-limited 30 req/min/IP via a temp-dir counter, sanitizes each path (strips control chars, length-caps to 300), and appends one JSON-Lines record (`ts, user_id, ip, path`) per event to per-day files `sitrec-upload/ui-stats/ui-YYYY-MM-DD.jsonl`. `config/shared.env.example` documents the new `LOG_UI_INTERACTIONS=false` flag (the live `shared.env` is gitignored).
- **Admin dashboard: "Top 10 Clicked Menu Items" card and "Top 200" drill-downs.** `sitrecServer/admin_dashboard.php` gains `loadTopMenuItems($dir, $top, $days=28)`, which streams the most recent 28 daily `ui-*.jsonl` files line-by-line into a path→count map and renders a new **Top 10 Clicked Menu Items** card. All four "Top 10 …" card titles (AI Users, Tile Users, Clicked Menu Items, S3 Users by Space) are now links to a new admin-only drill-down rendered by the same page via `?expand=<type>` (whitelist-validated against `['ai','tiles','menu','s3']`, `$EXPAND_LIMIT = 200`); `getS3Usage($limit)` and `loadTopMenuItems(..., $top)` were parameterized so the expanded view shows up to 200 rows.

### Security
- **js-yaml `4.1.1 → 4.2.0`** in `apps/video-viewer` (commit `b7a23e9f`, GHSA-h67p-54hq-rp68 / Dependabot #150), fixing a quadratic-complexity DoS in YAML merge-key alias handling. In-range bump (electron-builder needs `^4.1.0`), lockfile-only, dev/build-only — no production runtime exposure. A separate transitive lockfile refresh (commit `5229006d`: `@babel/*` toolchain, `launch-editor`, `linkify-it`, `markdown-it`, and `form-data`/`hasown`/`tar` in `apps/video-viewer`) carried no `package.json` or source changes.

## Version 2.84.3 (2026-06-15)

A security and CI-maintenance release. No shipped/runtime application code changed (`src/` is untouched).

### Security
- Dependency-only updates resolving six Dependabot advisories (commit `eaee79e4`; touches `package.json`, `package-lock.json`, `sitrecServer/composer.lock`, `tools/SitrecBridge/package.json`, `tools/SitrecBridge/package-lock.json`, no `src/` changes):
  - **esbuild `0.27.4 → 0.28.1`** in the main repo (pulled via `esbuild-loader 4.4.2 → 4.5.0`), fixing RCE via `NPM_CONFIG_REGISTRY` (high) and a Windows dev-server arbitrary-file-read (low). These are build-time-only tools, so production builds were never exposed at runtime, but the dev/build toolchain is now patched.
  - **esbuild `0.25 → 0.28.1`** in `tools/SitrecBridge` (same two advisories).
  - **guzzlehttp/psr7 `2.9.0 → 2.11.0`** in the PHP runtime (`sitrecServer/composer.lock`), fixing CRLF injection and Host-confusion-via-authority-reinterpretation (medium ×2). This is the one change that touches shipped server-side code: full-server and Docker deployments now run the patched PSR-7 HTTP library.
  - **ws `8.20.1 → 8.21.0`** in `tools/SitrecBridge`, fixing a memory-exhaustion DoS (high).
  - Verification: main app and SitrecBridge builds pass; production `npm audit --omit=dev` is clean; `composer` reports no advisories.

### Developer / Internal
- CI-robustness fix for the Docker image smoke test (`.github/workflows/docker.yml`), no shipped/runtime code. The job pulls the external Playwright base image (`mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:v1.58.2-noble`) from Microsoft Container Registry (MCR), which periodically rate-limits (`toomanyrequests`) or WAF-blocks (`unauthorized`) GitHub runners' shared egress IPs, intermittently failing the build. The fix: (1) a job-level `PLAYWRIGHT_IMAGE` env var as the single source of truth, referenced by the cache key, the load/pull step, and the test run; (2) an `actions/cache@v4` of the image tarball (`/tmp/playwright-image.tar`) keyed by `playwright-image-${PLAYWRIGHT_IMAGE}`, so the common path (`docker load` from cache) never contacts MCR; (3) on cache miss, the renamed *Load or pull Playwright image* step pulls with six attempts and `i*20 + jitter` backoff (was three short `i*15` tries), then `docker save`s the tarball for the next run. Bump `PLAYWRIGHT_IMAGE` in lockstep with the `playwright` devDependency.

## Version 2.84.2 (2026-06-15)

A refinement pass on the Atmospheric Optics (Halos) feature from 2.84.0. All changes are in `CNodeAtmosphericOptics.js`; the two new optics default OFF, so existing sitches and regression baselines are unaffected.

### New Features
- **Parry Arc** (Lighting → Atmospheric Optics (Halos) → *Parry Arc*): a new suncave arc riding just above the upper tangent arc, from rare "Parry-oriented" column crystals (c-axis horizontal with two side faces also horizontal). Drawn by the new `_buildParryArc()` as a parametric suncave band (apex `24°` above the Sun, drooping `12°` to the sides) with a red lower edge from `SPECTRUM_STOPS`. This is an approximate shape, not a full ray-trace, and it is faded out before high-Sun geometries where that approximation would become implausible. New serialized property `parryArc` (`addSimpleSerial("parryArc")`, default `false`).
- **Sun Glare** (Lighting → Atmospheric Optics (Halos) → *Sun Glare*): a new cosmetic warm aureole of forward-scattered light around the Sun, as seen through thin ice cloud — explicitly **not** a refraction optic (no toggle-dependent geometry). Drawn by `_buildSunGlare()` as a tight bright core (`exp(−v²·26)`) plus a broad faint aureole (`exp(−v²·2.2)·0.32`) out to `16°`, warm-white tinted (`[b, b·0.96, b·0.86]`). The aureole is windowed to zero at its rim with `1 − MathUtils.smoothstep(v, 0.45, 1.0)` so the additive mesh fades into the sky with no hard ring edge. New serialized property `sunGlare` (`addSimpleSerial("sunGlare")`, default `false`).

### Bug Fixes
- **Sun-dog refraction physics corrected.** `_buildDogs()` previously pinned each sun dog's great-circle distance from the Sun to a constant `22°` at all elevations (with a fixed `+0.6°` fudge), so the dogs never detached from the 22° halo as the Sun rose. The new code models plate-crystal (c-axis vertical) refraction through the 60° vertical-edge side-face prism: only the horizontal projection is deviated, via the Bravais effective index `nₑ = √(n²−sin²e)/cos e` (ice `N_ICE = 1.31`) giving the azimuth offset `Δaz = 2·asin(nₑ·sin30°) − 60°`. The on-sky distance then falls out of `cos D = sin²e + cos²e·cos(Δaz)` — so `D = 22°` only on the horizon and grows slowly *outside* the 22° halo as the Sun rises (≈22° at 10°, 23° at 20°, 25° at 30°, 28° at 40°), with the dogs lost to total internal reflection (early `return` when `nₑ·sin30° ≥ 1`) near 61° Sun elevation. The dog patch still anchors its sunward base ~1.5° inside the halo crossing (`deltaHalo`) so head and ring blend into a single pointed brightening at low Sun.

### Improvements
- **Sun dogs reshaped.** Each dog is now a compact, vertically-elongated teardrop (±8.5° elevation span, taller than wide) with a sharp reddish sunward head falling into a brief bluish tail, using pure additive Gaussian falloff (`sig = 0.11` head / `0.17` tail, colour graded red→white-blue by `cIdx`). The old hard `edgeFade` window and "comet tail" are gone, so nothing darkens at the patch edges — brightness simply reaches the sky value and blends with the halo on the sunward side. `_buildDogs` base brightness raised `0.85 → 0.9` so the dogs read ≥2× the 22° halo.
- **22° halo dimmed** so it reads as a delicate ring rather than a solid one: `_buildRing` base brightness for the sun halo lowered `0.55 → 0.33`.
- **Circumzenithal arc rebalanced**: base brightness lowered `1.0 → 0.5` (it was over-bright versus the halo and arcs) and narrowed to match the real CZA (`halfW` `1.9° → 1.2°`, real arc ~1.5° wide).

### Documentation
- The circumscribed-halo onset elevation wording was tightened in the *Tangent Arcs / Circumscribed* tooltip and accompanying code comment. Different references and visibility criteria put the transition in the high-20s to low-30s; the UI now treats it as an approximate range rather than an exact threshold.

## Version 2.84.0 (2026-06-15)

### New Features
- **Atmospheric Optics (Halos)** (Lighting → Atmospheric Optics (Halos)): a new `CNodeAtmosphericOptics` node (id `"theHalos"`, created in `addNightSky()` in `CNodeDisplayNightSky.js`) that renders ice-crystal atmospheric optics on the celestial sphere, locked onto the rendered Sun and Moon. Each effect is a reasonably-dense, vertex-colored, additive-blended indexed mesh built in world space from `getCelestialDirection()` + `getLocalUpVector()`, so it tracks the real Sun/Moon position with no render-pipeline changes. The master toggle is **Show Halos** (default OFF, so existing sitches and regression baselines are unaffected), plus an **Intensity** slider (0–3). Individual toggles: **22° Halo** (`halo22`, default on), **Sun Dogs (Parhelia)** (`sunDogs`), **Circumzenithal Arc** (only forms with the Sun below ~32°), **Circumhorizontal Arc** (only with the Sun above ~58°), **Parhelic Circle**, **46° Halo**, **Sun Pillar**, **Tangent Arcs / Circumscribed Halo**, **Moon Halo (22°)**, and **Moon Dogs (Paraselenae)**. The tangent arcs use a physical refraction model (horizontal hexagonal column crystals, Bravais effective index, both ±D branches), so the shape emerges correctly from Sun altitude with no per-elevation tuning: a narrow "V" at low Sun, opening into drooping gull-wings, then the upper and lower arcs closing into the circumscribed halo (a drooping oval around the 22° halo) in the high-20s to low-30s. Each effect forms only at its physically-correct Sun/Moon elevation, and a per-vertex horizon fade hides below-horizon parts. Sun optics render in `GlobalSunSkyScene` (group `atmosphericOpticsSun`) and fade out as the Sun sets so nothing shows at night; the Moon halo and moon dogs render in `GlobalNightSkyScene` (group `atmosphericOpticsMoon`), night-only, faint, and scaled by lunar phase brightness. Moon dogs are the lunar counterpart of sun dogs — faint, near-colorless bright spots ±22° either side of the Moon, just outside the moon halo — and share the sun-dog code path via the generalized `_buildDogs(stops, baseBrightness)` builder. Moon effects only draw when the Moon is above the horizon.
- **Lens Ghost** [BETA, admin + custom sitch only] (Video → [BETA] Lens Ghost): a new `CNodeLensGhost` node that overlays a simulated Sun internal-reflection ("ghost") disc on the video, to test whether a tracked disc could be a lens flare rather than a real object. It models the gnomonic Sun projection, the flat-window reflection with an adjustable forward lean (0–30°, the 2-theta mirror rule — control **Window Lean°**), anisotropic curved-mirror magnification (**Magnification X/Y**), image-roll coupling (**Roll Coupling**, the cause of horizontal reversal), and a defocused disc with an optional secondary-mirror donut (**Obstruction**). **Fit to Disc Track** fits the ghost to a tracked disc (auto-tracker or manual overlay) via a 1-D roll-scale search plus linear position fits. The node provides an on-video HUD (sun geometry, roll provenance, fit R²/RMSE — toggles **Show HUD**, **Show Geometry**, **Mark Source**) and plain-language warnings (stabilized video, magX≈−1 degeneracy, etc.). Created in `CustomManagerSetup.js` (not `SitCustom.js`, so older saves get it on reload) and gated by `Sit.isCustom && isAdmin()`. The commit also adds `BespokeView.js` with a generic `makeBespoke3DView()` factory (camera + view + Views-menu toggle + per-frame target framing + draw hook); its instance **[BETA] MQ-9 Light Path** (Views menu, same admin/custom gating, hidden by default) shows the boresight and incoming Sun ray at the MTS turret and shows the camera platform as an MQ-9. Two accessors `getTrackPixelXY()` / `getKeyframeSpan()` were added to `CNodeTrackingOverlay` to support the fit. Full physics write-up with diagrams in `docs/LensGhost.md`.

### Improvements
- **Scripted Video authoring UI** (Video → Scripted Video editor): the script editor gains an **Insert** toolbar button that opens an "Insert Script Step" palette for adding script steps (zoom/orbit/track/text/view-switch, etc.) from a form, generating readable DSL-style lines (`ScriptAuthoring.js` helpers `buildScriptSnippet`, `replaceLine`, `insertLineAfter`, `replaceNumberSpan`, etc.) that the parser then rebuilds into the event model — the script text stays the source of truth. The timeline widget (`ScriptTimelineWidget.js`) becomes directly editable: clicking a segment selects it (`selectEvent`), dragging a segment's right edge changes its duration (`_beginDurationDrag`), and dragging the segment body changes its start time/offset (`_beginOffsetDrag`), alongside the existing wheel-to-edit-duration affordance, with selection synced to the editor's highlighted line.

## Version 2.83.5 (2026-06-12)

### New Features
- **Long Exposure: Moonlight** (Video → Long Exposure, `moonlight` param, default OFF) — a new exposure mode that lights the scene with ONLY the Moon, producing a single image in which the dim moonlit landscape and the brighter star trails coexist the way they do in a real moonlit long-exposure photograph. Three coordinated pieces in `src/LongExposure.js`, `src/nodes/CNodeSunlight.js`, and `src/nodes/CPlanets.js`:
  - **Lighting override** (`CNodeSunlight.update`): when `theSun.moonlightMode` is set, after the normal sun calc the directional light is re-aimed at the Moon (`getCelestialDirection("Moon", date, camera.position)`, position scaled to 60000), ambient is forced to 0, and intensity becomes `this.sunIntensity * brightnessOfSun(moonAngle, darkeningAngle) * π * sunBoost * ratio`, where `ratio = 10^(-0.4(moonMag − SUN_APPARENT_MAG))`, `SUN_APPARENT_MAG = -26.74` (new module constant) and `moonMag` is read from the NightSky Moon sprite (fallback −12.7). The override MUST live inside `update` because every view render re-runs it and would clobber any external light write; tying intensity to `this.sunIntensity` lets the Long Exposure HDR-background boost flow through linearly. Surfaces facing away from the Moon go fully dark, shadows (if enabled) fall from the Moon, and a Moon below the horizon yields a dark scene (stars still record).
  - **Point-source ↔ rendered-scene scale tie** (the core of why it looks right): the splat flux scale (`satMag`, an astronomical zero-point) and the rendered moonlit ground (engine lighting × HDR boost) were on unrelated absolute scales — a mag-4 star deposited 1.0 while moonlit ground sat at ~1e-6, an ~20-stop gap, so no single EV could show both. After the boost is calibrated, moonlight mode computes a single `splatScale = 10^(0.4(moonMag − satMag)) · π · bgTargetLin / (GROUND_ALBEDO_REF · bgBoost · ωpix)`, where `ωpix` is the camera solid-angle-per-pixel from the projection matrix elements and `GROUND_ALBEDO_REF = 0.3`. Every point-source deposit is multiplied by it (`eSub = flux * splatScale / nSub` in `splatInterval`; `splatScale = 1` in all other modes). This is the physically-correct point/extended ratio (star/ground = E_star / (L_ground·ωpix)); the Moon's own brightness cancels via the boost, making it self-calibrating. Verified on the LE Moonlight test sitch (full moon behind camera): at the default EV ~19.7 the ground reads mean ~111 (visible front-lit landscape) while the sky reads mean ~1.7 with peaks ~247 (sparse bright star trails on dark sky) — both in one exposure; before the fix that EV blanketed the sky in saturated white.
  - **HDR machinery reuse and result auto-develop**: `BG_BOOST_CAP` is raised from 1024 to 1e9 in moonlight mode (moonlight is ~20+ stops below the daylight calibration). The HDR-background calibration block now runs when `(P.hdrBackground || P.moonlight)`, iterates up to 10 times (was 4), and its unmeasurably-dark branch steps the boost up ×1024 per iteration instead of jumping straight to the cap — a jump-to-cap couldn't walk back down by halving, a real bug that 100×-overexposed the first moonlight result. The result window opens pre-developed: `evInit = round(log2(bgBoost)·10)/10`, the EV slider's max is extended (`evMax = max(10, ceil(evInit)+4)`), and the live preview tone-maps at `previewGain = bgBoost` (raw moonlit values would preview black). `showResultWindow` now honors `opts.evInit` / `opts.evMax`. The mode is exposed by a serialized GUI checkbox "Moonlight" (`.perm().listen()`); `renderLongExposure` sets `theSunNode.moonlightMode = true` for the whole exposure (warns and ignores if no `theSun` node) and clears it in the `finally`.

### Bug Fixes
- Fixed the Moon's apparent magnitude never being set on the NightSky Moon sprite. `CPlanets.updateMoonMesh` (`src/nodes/CPlanets.js`) stored `ra`/`dec` under `storeState` but left `planetSprites.Moon.mag` at its init value of 0; it now stores `Astronomy.Illumination("Moon", date).mag` (≈ −12.7 full, ≈ −10 quarter). The regular planet path already stored `illumination.mag`, but the Moon branches separately and was missed. Besides being required by the new Moonlight mode, this corrects the existing HDR moon-disk renormalization in long exposures, which had been calibrating to a magnitude-0 Moon instead of its true ~−12.7 — so the Moon disk now burns out/trails with correct brightness in any long exposure where it is in frame.

### Documentation
- `docs/LongExposure.md` gains a "Moonlight" row in the controls table describing the moon-only lighting, the point-source-to-ground recalibration via plate scale, the pre-developed result window, and the below-horizon behavior.

## Version 2.83.4 (2026-06-12)

### Improvements
- **Long Exposure: HDR Background** (Video → Long Exposure, default on) — recovers background dynamic range in dark scenes. In a night scene (e.g. ambient 0.01) the entire lit background of the 8-bit base render lands in a handful of codes, so pushing the result's EV slider up reveals posterized color bands. Because Three.js lighting is linear, `renderLongExposure` (`src/LongExposure.js`) now temporarily boosts the scene lighting so the background renders using the full 8-bit range, then divides every decoded frame by the same factor before accumulation (and before the Moon-disk renormalization), leaving the float buffer at true brightness with ~boost× finer quantization. Calibration runs on the first sample: `bgPercentile()` measures the decoded scene-linear frame's 99.9th-percentile per-pixel max channel (stride-2 sampling), and up to 4 iterations re-render that sample via the new `decodeFrame()` closure — an exact ratio step toward a target just under saturation (display-linear 0.9, mapped through `acesInverse` when the look view tone-maps), backing off ×0.5 when the percentile reads clipped (≥ `bgClipLin`), capped at `BG_BOOST_CAP = 1024`. A final boost ≤ 1.01 is treated as 1, so the feature is inert in bright scenes. `scaleSceneLights()` applies the boost to the `theSun` node's `sunIntensity`/`ambientIntensity` (that node rewrites the global light intensities every update) AND to the `lighting` node's matching properties (so a mid-render `recalculate()` can't push unboosted values back), falling back to `Globals.sunLight`/`ambientLight` directly when neither node exists; `restoreSceneLights()` runs in the `finally`, so lighting is restored on completion, Enough, or error. New `hdrBackground` param in `defaultParams` (default true), serialized with custom sitches like the other Long Exposure params. Measured on the LE HDR Background Test sitch: boost calibrated to 268.9×; unique colors in the dark region at EV+8 went from 712 (off) to 85,892 (on) with mean luma preserved (70.4 vs 77.6); lights verified restored after the render. `docs/LongExposure.md` gains an HDR Background controls-table row and a nuances bullet: content that doesn't respond to the scene lights (the atmosphere's sky glow) is recorded proportionally darker — negligible at night, the only time the boost engages.

## Version 2.83.3 (2026-06-11)

### Bug Fixes
- Fixed terrain tiles being wrongly culled — and tile subdivision being wrongly blocked — when the camera sits below the WGS84 ellipsoid. The distant-tile horizon/globe-occlusion cull in `QuadTreeMap.calculateTileVisibility` (`src/QuadTreeMap.js`) feeds the camera's geodetic altitude (`altitudeAboveSphere`, an alias of `altitudeHAE`) into `distanceToHorizon` and `hiddenByGlobe`, formulas that assume the observer is above the surface. With a negative altitude, `distanceToHorizon` takes the square root of a negative number and `hiddenByGlobe` takes `acos` of a value greater than 1 — both return NaN, every NaN comparison is false, and tiles that genuinely intersect the view frustum fell through to the `horizonOccluded` rejection path, making the terrain vanish. Some look-camera setups legitimately sit below HAE because the scene uses local terrain/geoid offsets. Both gates now short-circuit when `cameraAltitude <= 0`: `calculateTileVisibility` accepts frustum-passing tiles without applying the horizon formulas, and the prospective-child subdivision guard `anyProspectiveChildVisible` returns `true` instead of blocking subdivision (which left the parent rendered as a coarse leaf). A new unit test, `tests/QuadTreeMapVisibility.test.js`, exercises both paths with a camera 10 m below the ellipsoid.

## Version 2.83.2 (2026-06-11)

### New Features
- **Lock Camera Heading** (Video → Long Exposure, `lockHeading`, default ON) in `src/LongExposure.js`: the exposure holds the camera orientation exactly as it is when the render starts — a tripod doesn't track. At render start `renderLongExposure` captures `lockQuat = camera.quaternion.clone()` with any live Camera Nudge offset removed (`nudgeQuaternion((par.frame ?? 0)/fps).invert()`), so the lock is the un-nudged base heading at the current frame. A new `applyHeadingLock(t)` runs after `updateWorld(f)` and before `renderOnce(f)` on both the direct render path and the settle `renderFrame` callback: it sets `camera.quaternion = lockQuat × nudge(t)` and calls `updateMatrix()` / `updateMatrixWorld(true)`, so whatever camera mode is active (To Target, Celestial Lock, Horizon Flare Region…) the exposure behaves as if *Use Angles* were locked on the current spot in the sky, with the Camera Nudge shake still composed on top. Only orientation is overridden — camera POSITION still follows its controllers. The HDR splat math is consistent automatically: the existing per-sample pose recovery (`qBase = qRendered × nudge(t)⁻¹`) yields exactly `lockQuat`, so the sub-frame slerp between samples is rotation-free as it should be. `docs/LongExposure.md` gains a matching controls-table row.

## Version 2.83.0 (2026-06-11)

### New Features
- **Duration (Minutes)** (Video → Long Exposure): the exposure now runs for a set number of minutes of sitch time from the FIRST frame of the sitch, replacing the previous A-B in/out range (the button is renamed *Render Long Exposure*, dropping "(A-B)"). New `durationMin` param (default 5, slider 0.1–720) in `src/LongExposure.js`. If the duration runs past the sitch's own end, `Sit.frames` / `Sit.aFrame` / `Sit.bFrame` are temporarily extended so the world keeps evaluating (sky rotation, satellites continue; tracks hold their last position), and restored in the render's `finally` block.
- **Frame Step** (Video → Long Exposure): samples every Nth frame (`step` param, default 30, slider 1–600) for ~30× faster renders. The accumulator normalizes per sample (`framesDone` counts samples, average is `1/framesDone`), so exposure brightness is identical at any step. Point-source trails (stars, planets, satellites, lights — including strobe dashes) remain continuous and photometrically exact because `splatInterval` integrates sub-frame across the whole inter-sample interval; only background/scene motion becomes stepped. The splat subdivision cap is raised 512 → 4096 since inter-sample intervals are step× longer. The progress widget reports samples ("N of M frames, step S") and the live-preview cadence adapts (`previewEvery = max(1, round(30/step))`).
- **Occlusion Mask** (Video → Long Exposure, default ON): splatted sources are now hidden behind terrain, buildings, and models. `computeOcclusionMask` renders `GlobalScene` through the look camera with a white `MeshBasicMaterial` override on black into a `WebGLRenderTarget` (same camera layers as the live view); `maskOccluded` tests each splat sub-sample by projecting the source through the MASK's stored pose, so the test depends only on direction from the camera position — exact under rotation-only motion (panning, Camera Nudge). The mask is rebuilt automatically whenever the camera position moves more than 0.25 m. A planet setting behind a hill now has its trail clipped at the ridge. Applies to HDR splats only (`hdrPoints && occlusion`); an aircraft's body still doesn't hide its own far-side lights.
- **Horizon Reddening** (Video → Long Exposure, default OFF): chromatic extinction is now opt-in. Off = achromatic dimming — the V-band coefficient (with the green-channel Forbes term) applied equally to all channels, for splats and model lights alike. On = per-channel dim-and-redden (see the extinction overhaul below).
- **Star Tint** (Video → Long Exposure, `starTint`, default 1.0, slider 0–2): intrinsic blue-white star color — a linear RGB lerp from flat white toward `[0.78, 0.90, 1.10]`, the bright-star population average (hot A/B stars dominate prominent trails). Stars only: planets stay photometrically white, model lights keep their own colors. With reddening on, horizon extinction first neutralizes the blue before warming, matching real star-trail photos.
- **Refraction** checkbox (Video → Long Exposure): a convenience mirror of View → Atmospheric Refraction, kept two-way in sync via a live proxy over `Sit.refractionEnabled` (guarded with `Sit?.` since `Sit` doesn't exist when the menu is built). The refracted behavior itself (splat positions, horizon culling, and extinction altitude following refracted directions) already existed — this just surfaces the switch where long-exposure users need it.

### Improvements
- **Atmospheric extinction physics overhaul** (expert-reviewed) in `src/LongExposure.js`: zenith is now geodetic (`getLocalUpVector`) instead of geocentric (also fixed in `boostMoonDisk`); observer pressure-altitude scaling `exp(−h/8400 m)` from `altitudeHAE` (an airborne camera sits above most of the extinction) with a matching dip-aware horizon cull (−√(2h/R)); Kasten-Young airmass is capped at the grazing-tangent value `AIRMASS_TANGENT = 28` and held (not extrapolated) below 0° apparent altitude; corrected clear-air channel ratios `EXT_RGB = [0.72, 1.00, 1.77]` at 620/550/460 nm; heterochromatic Forbes correction via per-channel effective airmass `X/(1 + aX)` with `EXT_FORBES_A = [0.0012, 0.0030, 0.0058]` at k_V = 0.16, scaled with the actual coefficient; default `extinctionK` 0.2 → 0.15 (clear sea-level air). Net effect: a horizon B−R differential of ~3.4 mag (R/B ≈ 22) at defaults instead of the unphysical ~6.7 mag (≈ 470×) the old monochromatic plane-parallel law produced. Model lights' slant-path extinction also gains mean-path pressure-altitude scaling (plane-to-plane paths at cruise altitude run through far thinner air) and per-channel treatment when Horizon Reddening is on.

### Documentation
- `docs/LongExposure.md` updated throughout: Duration-from-start workflow (with timeline extension), Frame Step, Refraction, Occlusion Mask, Horizon Reddening, and Star Tint control descriptions, plus rewritten "Exposures are real time" and occlusion-limitation notes.

## Version 2.82.1 (2026-06-11)

### New Features
- **Flaring satellites in HDR long exposures** (`src/LongExposure.js`, inside the *HDR Point Sources* path of `renderLongExposure`). During an HDR exposure the LDR satellite point cloud (`nightSky.satellites.lightCloud` points and mainViewPoints) is hidden, and only satellites that are actually flaring — glint angle inside the flare cone (`sats.flareAngle`) — plus the ISS when sunlit (`sd.number === 25544`, constant `ISS_MAG = -2`) are splatted as HDR point sources; everything else is omitted from the photograph, as in reality. The glint is recomputed fresh every frame for every lit satellite (`getSatelliteNormal` + camera-ray reflection vs `Globals.toSun`) rather than reusing the display's `isFlaring` state, which `updateSatellites` staggers across ~10 frames — so streak entry/exit are exact, not stagger-truncated. Flare flux peaks at `SAT_FLARE_PEAK_MAG = -4` using the shared `flareRamp` cone falloff from `tools/shf/flarePhysics.js` (the same function the live night-sky display uses), but the falloff band fades in MAGNITUDE space by `SAT_FLARE_TAPER_MAGS = 13` mags: a linear flux ramp is photometrically instantaneous here (peak is ~1600× pixel saturation, so it crosses the entire visible range in its last ~1%) and streaks would start and end at full brightness — the magnitude-space taper makes each streak brighten smoothly from nothing, hold full peak through the core, and fade back to nothing. Satellites get the same Kasten-Young `extinctionFactor` as stars and the same sub-frame `splatInterval` continuous splatting (per-satellite `prevSatPos`), so fast movers leave smooth flare streaks. Active only when the night sky has TLE data loaded and satellites are displayed (`showSatellites !== false`).

### Improvements
- Long-exposure renders now hide the night sky's constellation lines (`nightSky.constellationsGroup`) and equatorial grid (`nightSky.equatorialSphereGroup`) for the duration of the exposure, in both simple-average and HDR modes, restoring their visibility afterwards — chart furniture never belongs in a simulated photograph.
- The long-exposure tone map replaces its hard highlight clamp with a soft shoulder. Previously the non-ACES path in `tonemapBufferInto` (`src/LongExposure.js`) clamped each channel with `min(1, x)`, so any saturated streak flat-topped into identical featureless white. A new `softClip` function (knee at `SHOULDER_KNEE = 0.7`) keeps values linear below the knee and applies a Reinhard-style rolloff `t / (1 + t)` above it, so highlights grade smoothly into white instead of clipping. Because `tonemapBufferInto` is shared, the shoulder applies to both the in-progress preview (scale = 1/framesSoFar) and the result window (gain = 2^EV). The ACES path is unchanged — ACES has its own built-in shoulder.

### Bug Fixes
- Fixed the Long Exposure menu (folder, all its controls, and the Camera Nudge subfolder and its controls) disappearing after switching sitches. The menu is built once at startup (`addLongExposureMenu()` in `src/index.js`) and the GUI rebuild on sitch change destroys all non-permanent controllers; every item in `CLongExposureManager.setupMenu()` is now flagged `.perm()` so the menu survives the rebuild.

### Documentation
- New user guide `docs/LongExposure.md` ("Long Exposure Simulation") covering the A-B averaged exposure workflow, HDR point sources, satellite flare streaks, and Camera Nudge, with three example renders (`docs/docimages/longexposure-stars.jpg`, `-planes.jpg`, `-shf.jpg`). Linked from the in-app Help menu via `addHelpLink("menus.help.documentation.longExposure", "docs/LongExposure")` in `src/index.js`, with the new i18n key `menus.help.documentation.longExposure` in `src/i18n/en.js`.
