## Version 2.69.0 (2026-06-01)

### New Features
- **Replay mode — animated, time-driven wide-view playback (new default)** (`tools/shf/app.js` `startReplay`/`stopReplay`, `tools/shf/skyview.js` `horizonProjection`/`flareBrightnessAt`/`skyBodiesSVG`/`MOTION_SAMPLE_MS`). The Starlink Horizon Flares tool's "view from here" horizon panorama now defaults to an animated replay that plays the prediction the way it will actually look. `horizonMode` (module-level, persists across renders this session) cycles `dots → streaks → replay` via the ★ button (`.hv-toggle`), with `replay` as the initial value. A single `requestAnimationFrame` loop (`startReplay`) advances replay time at 1× real time; each satellite brightens/holds/fades over its real duration via the shared `flareBrightnessAt(f, t)` and drifts along its real apparent path (`az = f.azDeg + dAzDeg·(t−peakMs)/MOTION_SAMPLE_MS`, same for el), with the faint timelapse streaks drawn behind at ~12% opacity (`streakMul`) for context. Playback starts at `peakMs` — the **busiest minute** of the visible set (`renderResults` bins the shown flares into 1-minute buckets and picks the fullest), loops `t2→t1`, and skips long dead gaps (`anyActive`/`nextStart`: if nothing is visible and the next flare start is >1.5 s away, jump to ~0.6 s before it, so each flare still plays at 1×). A draggable Sun under the horizon (`.replay-sun` / `.replay-sun-hit`, a 32px-wide hit rect with pointer capture) sits at the Sun's true azimuth (`sunAzimuthAt`, shared with the hourly markers) and scrubs time: `xToTime` maps pointer-x to the nearest of 120 pre-sampled instants across the window. A monospace `HH:MM:SS` readout (`.replay-time`, top-left above the horizon) and the stars/planets (`.replay-bodies`, redrawn by `skyBodiesSVG`) update once per second (throttled on `Math.floor(t/1000)`), so the sky rotates with replay time. Replay flare dots are soft-edged via a `objectBoundingBox` radial gradient (`#rflareDot`: solid to ~88% of the radius, feathering to transparent over the outer ~12% — no real bloom), sized `r = 1.0 + 2.0·b` by brightness. `renderScreen` calls `stopReplay()` whenever the page leaves results, and a fresh scan tears down any prior animation.
- **Timelapse-streak mode** (`tools/shf/skyview.js` `horizonView` streak branch; `tools/shf/flareEngine.js` core tracking; `tools/shf/flarePhysics.js` `flareCoreAngle`). The ★ `streaks` mode draws each flare as a "timelapse exposure" — a 2px white line tracing the satellite's apparent path over the flare (peak ± apparent-motion × time-offset, `back`/`fwd` in `MOTION_SAMPLE_MS` units), with a `userSpaceOnUse` linear-gradient brightness profile along the line: 0 at both ends, peaking at the run's brightest point. The profile is a **ramp-HOLD-ramp** with a full-brightness plateau across the cone "core" rather than a single triangle peak: `flareEngine` now records `coreStartMs`/`coreEndMs` on every flare (first/last time the glint sits inside the full-brightness core, where `glint < flareCoreAngle(spread)` — the new `flareCoreAngle` = `spread·(1−rampFraction)`, the plateau of `flareRamp`), carried through `makeFlare`; when a core is present the gradient repeats the bright stop at both core edges (flat top), otherwise it falls back to a single peak stop. The shared `flareBrightnessAt` uses the same control points, so replay and the streak agree on each flare's curve.
- **LIVE / real-time toggle** (`tools/shf/skyview.js` `liveButton`/`liveBadge`, `tools/shf/style.css` `.replay-live-btn`/`.replay-live`, `tools/shf/app.js` `renderHorizon`). A red "LIVE" badge above the time readout doubles as a button (`.replay-live-btn`), drawn only when "now" falls inside the flaring window (`nowInWindow = Date.now() ∈ [t1,t2]`, passed as `liveButton`/`opts.liveButton`). Toggling it on re-renders the horizon with `realtime` and anchors replay time to the wall clock (`ctl.realtime` → `ctl.t = clamp(Date.now())` each frame, scrubbing disabled), so the view shows what is flaring right now; a second red indicator (`liveBadge`, hidden by default) appears below the Sun and moves with it. Both `.replay-live` elements are shown only while real-time mode is active. This `liveButton` explicitly **replaces the old clock button**; colours are CSS-driven (grey with the dot at opacity 0 when off so nothing shifts, red box/dot/text when `.on`) and it shares the 46×16 geometry of the passive badge so the two read identically.
- **Zoom button (1× → 2× → 4×)** (`tools/shf/app.js` `horizonZoom`/`ZOOMS`/`zoomWin`, `tools/shf/style.css` `.hv-zoom`). A magnifier button stacked just above the ★ cycles the wide view through 1×/2×/4×. Zoom narrows the projection window (`zoomWin`: `halfWidthDeg`/`elMaxDeg ÷ factor`) so flare/star/Sun **positions** spread out around the same centre while every drawn element (text, dots, lines — all absolute px) stays the same size. `renderResults` rebuilds the SVG and the matching `horizonProjection(zoomWin(win))` so the animated replay layer maps identically to the static scene, preserving the current dots/streaks/replay mode and real-time state across a zoom change.

### Improvements
- **Shared flare-brightness model extended and single-sourced** (`tools/shf/flarePhysics.js`, `tools/shf/skyview.js`, `src/nodes/CNodeDisplayNightSky.js`). `flarePhysics.js` (added in this release window as the canonical cone-ramp / penumbra-fade / brightness-constants module with `isFlareVisible`) gains `flareCoreAngle`, and `skyview.js` extracts `flareBrightnessAt`, `skyBodiesSVG`, `horizonProjection`, and `MOTION_SAMPLE_MS` so the live replay layer, the timelapse streaks, the static dots, and the redrawn sky all derive position and brightness from one set of functions and can't drift apart. The main-app live night sky (`CNodeDisplayNightSky.js`) now imports `FLARE`/`flareRamp`/`penumbraFade` from `tools/shf/flarePhysics.js` instead of inline-duplicated constants (`0.04` base, `0.3` darkness multiplier, the `spread·0.25` cone ramp) and math — verified output-identical — so the standalone SHF tool and Sitrec's rendered flares share a single brightness definition. (The model lives under `tools/shf/` because that tool is served as raw ES modules and can only import from there; the webpack bundle imports down into it.)
- **Visibility cutoff applied throughout the wide view** (`tools/shf/app.js`, `tools/shf/flareEngine.js`). Only flares bright enough to actually be seen — the glint outshines the satellite's base brightness, per the shared `isFlareVisible`/`f.visible` flag introduced this release window — are counted and plotted. The live count filters on `f.visible`; `renderResults` plots `shown` (= the `f.visible` subset, falling back to all only if none qualify); the streak/dot/replay drawing clamps `intensity` and replay skips dots dimmer than `b ≤ 0.01`. Faint sub-base glints no longer inflate the result or clutter the panorama.
- **Motion arrow length now reflects flare duration** (`tools/shf/skyview.js` dots branch). In `dots` mode the amber motion arrow is now scaled by how far the satellite travels over the whole run (apparent motion × duration, `durDt = (endMs−startMs)/MOTION_SAMPLE_MS`, capped at `MAXL = 80`px), replacing the old fixed 15px length, so a long, fast pass reads as a longer arrow.
- **Hourly Sun-azimuth markers on the horizon panorama** (`tools/shf/app.js` `sunHourMarkers`/`sunAzimuthAt`, `tools/shf/skyview.js`, `tools/shf/astro.js` `sunEquatorial`). The "view from here" panorama draws a labelled amber down-arrow per whole local hour at the Sun's azimuth for that hour, in a headroom band above the sky. Because the flares track the Sun's direction, the markers turn the azimuth axis into a rough time axis. `sunAzimuthAt` is shared by these markers and the replay Sun so the draggable Sun lands on the same azimuths as the ticks above it.
- **Single-pass scan progress bar** (`tools/shf/app.js` `renderLoading`). The scanning loading bar was rewritten as one monotonic pass driven by the worker's real filter/refine progress — it starts at 0, never resets or jumps to ~25%, and (for fixed-location searches) caps the fill just below 100% to leave headroom for a possible extra dark window. Phase labels narrate each step above the bar.
- **Corrected limb/shadow explanatory diagram** (`tools/shf/index.html`). The info page's limb/shadow illustration was redrawn to show parallel sunlight grazing the limb, the satellite's flat panel held parallel to the ground beneath it, and a proper terminator plus Earth's-shadow umbra with the satellite sitting at the shadow edge.
- **"Open in Sitrec" launch camera reframed** (`src/fromApp.js` `frameMainView`). Launching a prediction into the main Sitrec app now places the overview camera up in space (~6000 km from the observer, on the anti-Sun side) looking down at the observer/aircraft at ~45°, so Earth's limb and the Starlink shell wrapping it fill the frame with the observer in the middle. Previously it was a low third-person establishing shot from ~14 km behind and ~7 km above the look camera.

### Bug Fixes
- **Off-view flares are clipped to the sky rectangle instead of squashed against its edges** (`tools/shf/skyview.js`). The horizon projection's `yOf` previously clamped elevation to `[0, elMax]`, which collapsed any streak or motion arrow running above the top (or below the horizon) onto the rim. `horizonProjection.yOf` is now **unclamped** and all flare drawing (streaks, dots, arrows, and the replay layer) is wrapped in `<g clip-path="url(#skyClip)">` — a `skyClip` rect covering the sky region — so overflowing geometry is cropped at the edge with its true direction preserved. This is most visible when zoomed in, where positions spread out and more geometry runs off-view.

## Version 2.68.3 (2026-06-01)

### Improvements
- **Browser/mouse Back and Forward now navigate between the Starlink Horizon Flares tool's screens** (`tools/shf/app.js`). The standalone SHF (Starlink Horizon Flares) tool is a single-page app with three screens — form, results, info — that previously toggled purely via the `hidden` attribute with no History API integration, so after running a search the browser (and mouse) Back button did nothing. The screen togglers were refactored into a single `renderScreen(name)` that flips visibility only (no history mutation) and preserves the old side effects — terminating the flare Web Worker (`activeWorker`) when landing on the form, and building the info-page SVG/SMIL visuals once via `buildInfoVisuals()`. Two thin wrappers, `navigateResults()` and `navigateInfo()`, push a `history.pushState({screen:'...'}, "")` entry before rendering (stateless, same URL); `navigateResults()` uses `replaceState` when already on results so re-running a search doesn't stack duplicate entries and a single Back always reaches the form. `init()` now seeds the form as the base entry with `history.replaceState({screen:'form'}, "")` and registers a `popstate` listener that renders `e.state.screen` (defaulting to `"form"`). The on-screen "‹ Edit" (results) and "‹ Back" (info) buttons now call `history.back()` instead of toggling directly, and the "i" info buttons call `navigateInfo()`, so manual and browser navigation share one path and never desync the stack — including Back from info, which pops to whichever screen it was opened from. The old `showForm`/`showResults`/`showInfo`/`hideInfo` functions and the `infoReturnScreen` module variable were removed; the history stack reproduces the info-return target losslessly, so no return-screen bookkeeping is needed. `onSubmit` now calls `navigateResults()` in place of the old `showResults()`.
- **The "Install App" suggestion in the Starlink Horizon Flares tool is now clearly separated and dismissable** (`tools/shf/index.html`, `tools/shf/style.css`, `tools/shf/app.js`). The install button lives outside the screen divs so it appears at the bottom of every screen, and sat directly below the results where users expect a Back control — reported as feeling like a dark pattern. The button is retained on every screen, but `.install-wrap` now sets `position: relative`, a hairline `border-top: 1px solid var(--line)` divider, a larger `margin: 32px auto 0`, and `padding: 20px 0 0` (previously `margin: 22px auto 0` with no divider), so it is visually set apart from the content above on every screen. A new dismiss "×" control (`#install-dismiss` in index.html, styled `.install-dismiss` top-right) hides the suggestion for the rest of the session: `installDismissed()` (a new try/catch-guarded helper) reads the `shfInstallDismissed` flag from `sessionStorage`, `updateInstallButton()` now gates the wrap on `isStandalone() || installDismissed()`, and `wireInstall()` wires the × to set the flag and re-gate. It reappears in a fresh tab/session. (The SHF tool is a standalone PWA, not part of the main Sitrec webpack bundle.)

## Version 2.68.2 (2026-05-31)

### Bug Fixes
- **Fixed the production deploy build failing after the `tools/starlink` → `tools/shf` rename** (`webpack.common.js`): 2.68.1 renamed the standalone tool directory `tools/starlink` → `tools/shf` but missed one path reference — the `TerserPlugin` `exclude` regex in the production-only minimizer config still read `/(Sit.*|tools[\\/]starlink[\\/].*)\.js$/`. That exclude exists because the SHF (Starlink Horizon Flares) tool is copied verbatim as native ES modules (`import`/`export`), which Terser's script-mode parser can't minify. After the rename the regex no longer matched the tool's files, so `npm run deploy` (which minifies) hard-failed with `ERROR in tools/shf/flareWorker.js from Terser plugin — Unexpected token: name (import)`. Dev builds (`npm run build`) were unaffected because they don't run the minimizer — which is why 2.68.1's dev builds passed but its production deploy build was broken. The fix updates the exclude to `tools[\\/]shf[\\/]` (and the adjacent comment). Verified with `npx webpack --config webpack.prod.js` compiling cleanly.

## Version 2.68.1 (2026-05-31)

### Improvements
- **Standalone tool directory renamed `tools/starlink` → `tools/shf`** (42 git renames; served URL `/<base>/tools/starlink/` → `/<base>/tools/shf/`). Pure rename, no behavior change. All path references were updated to match: `webpackCopyPatterns.js` (the `["index.html","sw.js"]` build-stamping loop's `from`/`to` that injects `__BUILD_V__`), `tools/shf/app.js` `sitrecBaseURL()` (regex now strips `/\/tools\/shf\/.*$/` so the *Open in Sitrec* handoff still resolves the right host/base), the `tools/index.html` launcher link (`href="shf/"`), `tools/shf/README.md` documented URLs, and the path comment in `src/fromApp.js`. Intentionally **not** touched, because they are unrelated to the tool directory: the `starlink` *sitch* (`data/starlink/SitStarlink.js`, `Sit.name === "starlink"`) that the handoff builds on, the `docs/Starlink` help link, the Celestrak `GROUP=starlink` query param, and the internal identifiers `sw.js` cache name `starlink-flares-<build>` and `TLE_CACHE_KEY`. Note: the historical 2.68.0 changelog entries above still reference the old `tools/starlink/` paths and are deliberately left unchanged.
- **Home-screen app name is now "SHF"** (`tools/shf/manifest.webmanifest` `short_name` "Flares" → "SHF"; `tools/shf/index.html` `apple-mobile-web-app-title` "Flares" → "SHF"). "Flares" is generic and collides with unrelated home-screen apps; "SHF" (initialism of *Starlink Horizon Flares*) is short enough never to truncate under an icon. The full manifest `name` "Starlink Horizon Flares" is unchanged, so the install dialog still shows the long name. Both `short_name` and `apple-mobile-web-app-title` are read at install time, so only newly-installed instances pick up the new label; already-installed copies keep "Flares" until reinstalled.
- **Accurate, platform-aware PWA install instructions** (`tools/shf/app.js`). The manual install-instructions path was rewritten. The old code used a single `isIOS()` check and showed Safari-only "Add to Home Screen" steps to *all* iOS users (and a generic message to everyone else) — wrongly telling iOS-Chrome users to use Safari, even though since iOS 16.4 every iOS browser can Add to Home Screen. A new `platformInfo()` detector distinguishes iOS Safari, iOS Chrome (`CriOS`), other iOS browsers (Firefox/Edge/Opera wrappers), Android, macOS Safari, desktop Firefox, and desktop Chrome/Edge (with an iPadOS `MacIntel`+`maxTouchPoints` fallback for the desktop-UA case). A new `manualInstall()` returns per-platform steps: iOS branches point at the correct Share-button location for that browser (Safari toolbar at bottom vs Chrome address-bar/⋯ menu vs the generic ⋯ menu, with an inline share-glyph SVG and a 16.4+ note for non-Safari); Android shows ⋮ → *Install app*; macOS Safari shows *File → Add to Dock* (Sonoma+ note); desktop Firefox explains it can't install PWAs and points to Chrome/Edge/Safari/mobile; desktop Chrome/Edge shows the address-bar install icon and the *Install Starlink Horizon Flares…* menu item. The automated `beforeinstallprompt` path (`onInstallClick`: confirm → `bip.prompt()` → `userChoice`) is unchanged — `platformInfo()` only drives instruction text, never which path runs.

## Version 2.68.0 (2026-05-31)

### New Features
- **"Open in Sitrec" handoff from the Starlink Horizon Flare tool** (`src/fromApp.js`, `src/CustomManagerSetup.js`, `src/nodes/CNodeControllerVarious.js`): The standalone flare tool's results screen gains an *Open in Sitrec* button that opens the main app at `?fromapp=1&…` with the prediction parameters. Sitrec builds a situation on top of the existing `starlink` sitch: a real-time (1×) timeline spanning the full flare window (first→last flare) starting on the peak flare at 30 fps (a 4-hour `MAX_FRAMES` backstop guards pathologically long inputs, then centers on the peak); a real origin→destination flight track built as MISB data and loaded through the normal `TrackManager` pathway so it becomes a `CNodeTrackFromMISB`, appears in the Contents menu, and wires into `cameraTrackSwitch` with no special-casing (fixed-location mode instead raises the ground camera 50 ft); a new *Horizon Flare Region* camera lock (`CNodeControllerHorizonFlareRegion`) that aims at the Sun's azimuth ~9° above the horizon and follows it, selected automatically by the launch; LOS display off; and the main 3D view framed from behind/above the look camera so the flare band and region fill the shot. The tool title became "Starlink Horizon Flare".
- **war.gov UAP case-code tile in the Sitch Browser** (`src/CSitchBrowser.js`): Typing a war.gov UAP case code (e.g. `PR050`) into the Sitch Browser search box surfaces a green synthetic tile ("Open UAP case record") as the first card; activating it loads that case's video exactly as if its war.gov URL had been dragged into Sitrec. `renderThumbnails()` prepends the tile when `extractWarGovPRCode()` matches the search text, with `_thumbCardOffset` keeping the DOM-child↔filtered-index mapping correct for selection, rubber-band, and scroll-into-view. The tile is selectable (blue border) but never added to `this.selection`, so context menu / delete / select-all ignore it; Down-arrow from the search box selects it as grid position 0, and Enter activates it like a double-click. `_triggerWarGovPRRecord` routes to the SAME handler a dragged URL uses, keyed on `NodeMan.exists("video")`: with a video node present it calls `DragDropHandler.handleDroppedText()` directly (no reload), otherwise it loads the custom sitch first so the dropped video has a node to land in — replacing the old `pendingDropTexts` + `setNewSitchObject` route that forced a full `disposeEverything()`/rebuild and failed on sitch-to-sitch swaps.
- **Starlink Horizon Flare tool — About page** (`tools/starlink/index.html`, `app.js`, `skyview.js`, `style.css`, new `tools/starlink/video/DOD_110779879-480p.mp4`): An "i" info button (upper-right of every screen) opens an About page describing the phenomenon, with a floated animated "what it looks like" naked-eye flare simulation (`flareSimSky()` in `skyview.js`), a live animated compass-rose direction preview reusing the results-screen `compassRose()`, an embedded full-screenable AARO explainer video ("Starlink Horizon Flares explained by AARO"), a detailed "how it works" section with two inline SVG geometry diagrams, and external links (incl. the AARO Satellite Flaring information paper, Sitrec on GitHub, Metabunk, CelesTrak, Wikipedia). The animated visuals are refactored onto a shared `twinkleFlare()` SMIL generator extracted from `flareDots()`, with new `upOnly` (drift never heads downward) and `shrinkFade` (fade by radius rather than opacity) options for the naked-eye sky preview. The About copy follows the AARO paper: the reflector is the satellite bus's flat, mirror-like, ground-facing underside (nadir, tangential to the surface); flares appear in a "flare window" 0–10° above the horizon toward the set Sun while the Sun sits roughly 38°–46° below the horizon; they are NOT a twilight-only effect, NOT a moving "train" (each flash is a different satellite), and are often brighter than Venus.
- **Starlink Horizon Flare tool — Install App button** (`tools/starlink/index.html`, `app.js`): An *Install App* button appears at the bottom of every screen (hidden via `isStandalone()` when already running as an installed app). An early-capture inline script in `index.html` stashes the `beforeinstallprompt` event (`window.__bipEvent`) and re-fires `bip-ready`/`app-installed` for the async `app.js` module. On Chrome/Edge/Android the button confirms ("Install the Starlink Horizon Flares app on this device?") then triggers the native prompt; on iOS/iPadOS (`isIOS()`) and other browsers without an automated prompt it opens a modal with platform-specific manual steps (Safari Share → "Add to Home Screen", or the browser's install menu item). This builds on the 2.67.0 PWA/service-worker work — it adds the explicit in-app install affordance the tool previously lacked.

### Improvements
- **AARO Official UAP Imagery cases PR1–PR18 now resolve** (`src/WarGovUFOUtils.js`, `src/CSitchBrowser.js`): The browser tile and dropped-URL paths already resolved war.gov "DOW-UAP-PRxx" cases (PR019+) via the bundled WARGOV CSVs, but AARO's Official UAP Imagery (PR-001..PR-018) predates that release and is hosted on DVIDS, absent from those CSVs, so typing/dropping PR1–PR18 previously failed. A fixed `AARO_PR_DVIDS_IDS` table (PR-001..PR-018 → DVIDS video ID, sourced from the matching dvidshub.net videos) plus `getAaroDvidsIdForPrCode()` are added; `getWarGovUFODvidsId()` and `getWarGovUFODvidsIdForPrCode()` check the AARO table first and fall back to the war.gov CSV catalog, so both the URL pathway (`resolveWarGovUFOVideoURL`) and the prCode pathway share one resolver. `extractWarGovPRCode` was widened to 1–3 digits so single-digit codes (PR1..PR9) are recognised (all normalise to zero-padded `PRNNN`), and the tile label was genericized to "Open UAP case record" (PR1–18 AARO, PR19+ war.gov). All 18 mappings are pinned by `tests/WarGovUFOUtils.test.js`.
- **Starlink Horizon Flare tool — "next flares" search capped at 24 hours** (`tools/starlink/app.js`): The fixed-location forward search look-ahead (`LOOK_AHEAD_DAYS`) was reduced from 3 days to 1. The flare geometry recurs on a ~daily cycle (Sun position + the constellation's ground track), so if there's no flare in the first day there won't be one in the next two — searching further just wasted time.
- **Lazy MISB flight-track for the synthetic app flight** (new `src/nodes/CNodeLazyMISBFlightTrack.js`, `src/TrackManager.js`, `src/fromApp.js`, `src/CustomManagerSerialize.js`, `src/nodes/CNodeMunge.js`, `src/nodes/CNodeSmoothedPositionTrack.js`): The synthetic "Open in Sitrec" airplane flight no longer bakes a ~414k-entry per-global-frame array (and then re-smooths it). `CNodeLazyMISBFlightTrack` (extends `CNodeTrackFromMISB`, keeps full MISB/KML export and the time-offset wrapper) stores only the sparse MISB samples (≤1200) as a chordal `CatmullRomCurve3` and evaluates the camera position on demand at the fractional global frame, mirroring the existing `method:"spline"` sparse path but lazily. It is chosen in `TrackManager` strictly when `FileManager.getInfo().isAppFlight` is set (via `info.isAppFlight` in `buildAppFlightTrack`), so no other track path changes. `CNodeSmoothedPositionTrack` gains a passthrough mode: when its (switched) source resolves to a `lazyInterpolated === true` track it delegates `getValue`/`getValueFrame`/`exportArray` to the source instead of baking, sets its own `lazyInterpolated` flag so chained smoothers (e.g. the ObjectTilt orientation smoothers off `cameraTrackSwitchSmooth`) also take the passthrough path, and re-evaluates every cascade so switching camera tracks turns it on/off dynamically. `CNodeMunge` now skips its per-frame bake when `countVisibleOutputs(0, true) === 0` (default-on `checkDisplayOutputs`, opt out with `checkDisplayOutputs:false`); `getValueFrame()` falls back to a live `munge()` compute and nothing reads `.cachedValues` directly, so this is behavior-identical and only changes WHEN the work happens. `fromApp.js` / `CustomManagerSerialize.js` add `applyFlightLightweightGating()`, which hides the unused `traverseDisplayTrack`/`altitudeLabel2`/`distanceLabel`/`traverseObject`/`moveTargetAlongPath`/`orientTarget` display leaves (it hides, not deletes, so referencing node ids don't break and a real dropped track restores them) on both live launch (`finishFromApp`) and saved-sitch reload (pre-recalc in the deserialize path) so the `checkDisplayOutputs` gate skips their expensive per-frame bakes — gated on `Sit.appFlight`. The `node-smoke` skip-list was updated for the new node's nested ESM path.

### Bug Fixes
- **Fixed a WebGL context-loss crash on sitch swaps** (`src/nodes/CNodeView3D.js`): `dispose()` called `forceContextLoss()` (which fires `webglcontextlost` asynchronously) and then nulled `this.renderer`, so the never-removed listener fired on a disposed view → "Cannot read properties of null (reading 'info')". The lost/restored handlers are now stored as references and `removeEventListener`-ed at the top of `dispose()` before `super.dispose()` nulls the canvas. Genuine context-loss recovery on live views is unaffected.
- **Fixed a duplicate Three.js runtime copy** (`src/QuadTreeTile.js`, `webpack.common.js`): `QuadTreeTile.js` used `require("three")` in two spots, which resolves via the package's "require" export to `three.cjs` — a second runtime copy alongside the ESM `three.core.js` — triggering the runtime "Multiple instances of Three.js being imported" warning and disjoint prototypes (broken `instanceof`). Those inline requires were replaced with the already-imported `Vector3` and `LLAToECEFInto`. The `DetectDuplicateThreeModules` webpack plugin was upgraded to detect runtime builds by content (presence of the `window.__THREE__` init guard) rather than by path, and now pushes to `compilation.errors` (hard build failure) naming the offending source module, so a future duplicate-runtime import can't ship silently.
- **Fixed the synthetic "Open in Sitrec" flight being saved as a rehosted file** (`src/fromApp.js`, `src/CustomManagerSerialize.js`): A custom sitch built by the handoff used to persist the synthetic flight as a rehosted MISB file (and left a dead filename reference on local saves). The flight is fully regenerable from ~8 scalar parameters, so `buildAppFlightTrack(p)` was extracted from `finishFromApp` and shared by both the live launch and the reload path (identical node graphs); the generated "App Flight.kml" FileManager entry is flagged `skipSerialization` so it is never rehosted/embedded and is dropped from the `loadedFiles` save loop (and its per-file track metadata is skipped); the generator params are stashed on `Sit.appFlight`, written as `out.appFlight`, and regenerated on deserialize before the mods pass so `Track_Flight` et al. exist for their mods to attach (guarded against double-create for legacy saves that still embed the file). Verified by a save+reload round-trip: the saved sitch carries only the params and the flight regenerates as an identical `CNodeTrackFromMISB` in the Contents menu, selected in `cameraTrackSwitch`, with all node mods applied.

## Version 2.67.0 (2026-05-30)

### New Features
- **Starlink Flare Predictor is now an installable PWA** (standalone tool, `tools/starlink/`): The standalone flare tool can now be installed to a phone/desktop home screen and run offline. New `tools/starlink/manifest.webmanifest` (name "Starlink Flare Predictor", `short_name` "Flares", `display: standalone` with `display_override: ["standalone","minimal-ui"]`, `orientation: portrait`, theme/background `#070b18`, `categories: ["utilities","education"]`, a full icon set incl. maskable variants and an SVG, and two narrow-form-factor screenshots). New `tools/starlink/sw.js` service worker with runtime caching (no hand-maintained precache list): navigations are network-first (a new build shows immediately online, falls back to the cached app shell offline); same-origin assets are cache-first and safe because every asset URL is build-stamped `?v=<build>` (a new build = new URLs = cache misses that fetch fresh); cross-origin requests (Nominatim geocoding, TLE fetch) are never cached and pass straight to the network, so offline use falls back to the synthetic constellation. The cache name is `starlink-flares-<build>`, so each deploy's `activate` deletes the prior build's cache. `index.html` head gains the manifest link, favicon/apple-touch-icon links, `description`, `mobile-web-app-capable` / `apple-mobile-web-app-capable` / `apple-mobile-web-app-status-bar-style: black-translucent` / `apple-mobile-web-app-title: Flares`, and `viewport-fit=cover`; `style.css` adds `env(safe-area-inset-*)` to the body padding so the installed (standalone) app clears the iOS status bar, notch, and home indicator. `app.js` `registerServiceWorker()` registers `sw.js` on `load` with relative scope and `updateViaCache: "none"` (so each build's stamped worker is picked up fresh), and is skipped under `navigator.webdriver` to keep e2e runs deterministic. `webpackCopyPatterns.js` now stamps both `index.html` and `sw.js` with the build version (the loop over `["index.html","sw.js"]`, each with `force: true` to override the verbatim copy from the `tools` glob).

### Improvements
- **Playback speed range widened to 1/100× – 100×** (frames bar → *Playback Speed*): in `src/JetGUI.js` `updateGUIFrames`, the `playbackSpeed` slider range/step changed from `0.25, 10, 0.25` to `0.01, 100, 0.01`, allowing both far slower frame-by-frame scrubbing and much faster playback.
- **Starlink tool — realistic synthetic constellation** (`tools/starlink/dummyTLE.js`): the synthetic Starlink set (used by default and offline) was reworked to match the real constellation — a per-shell Walker-plane layout, the real altitude distribution (~360–580 km, median ~490 km), and the satellite count matched to the real set (~10,500). The synthetic "view from here" now matches real-TLE density and az/el distribution (verified via the dev `tools/compare-views.mjs` synth-vs-real all-sky comparison).
- **Starlink tool — synthetic-by-default TLE source with in-session real opt-in** (`tools/starlink/app.js`): the synthetic constellation is the default; real data is an explicit in-session opt-in (Advanced › *Fetch current TLE*, or load a `.tle` file) held in memory only — a page reload returns to synthetic rather than silently reusing a cached set across loads. Synthetic generation is now reproducible (the synthetic epoch is anchored to the requested time, so repeating an unchanged search gives the same result). The Advanced section's numeric inputs were removed; Advanced now controls only the TLE source.
- **Starlink tool — explicit per-source data note at the bottom of results** (`tools/starlink/app.js` `notesHTML` / `renderResults`): the data-source note now renders at the bottom of the results (after the legend) instead of under the header, and is explicit per source — an amber `⚠ Synthetic satellites — positions are approximate…` warning for synthetic, a `Real Starlink data (current TLE)` note for fetched/cached real TLE, and a green `Using your uploaded TLE file` confirmation for an uploaded file. The out-of-date-range guard note wording also changed to "Simulated results, out of date range — recomputed for today."
- **Starlink tool — peak time on the results header** (`tools/starlink/app.js` `renderResults`): the first results line now reports the session's busiest minute (greatest flare density, matching the rose's density arc) — "Flares visible HH:MM TZ · peak HH:MM". Peak is computed by binning each flare's `peakMs` into 60-second buckets and taking the most populous bucket; density (not single-flare brightness) is used because flare intensity saturates at 1.0.
- **Starlink tool — compact iPhone-SE results layout** (`tools/starlink/`, `e7e4a4f0`): the large "FLARES VISIBLE" banner was replaced with a compact 3-line header (when / direction / place-date-UTC) with smaller fonts and a smaller compass rose, so the results content fits a ~592 px viewport (< the 667 px iPhone-SE height). The input page was tidied (subtitle/help lines removed, Origin relabelled "Origin (blank for current location)", Advanced moved below *Find Flares*), and horizon-view satellites are drawn as small white disks with thinner 75%-opacity motion arrows (the heavy amber glows were dropped). The geolocation, simulated-out-of-range fallback, and animated compass-sprinkle behaviors of this same commit shipped in 2.66.0 and are documented there.

### Bug Fixes
- **Fixed H.264 video exports/imports that play only in Chromium** (`src/H264Utils.js`, `src/MediabunnyExporter.js`, `src/CVideoMp4Data.js`): Firefox's WebCodecs `VideoEncoder` on the Windows Media Foundation backend ("Microsoft H.264 Encoder V1.5.3", identified by an in-band SEI fingerprint) emits a malformed `AVCDecoderConfigurationRecord` — each stored SPS/PPS NAL unit has its 1-byte NAL header duplicated (e.g. `67 67 …` / `68 68 …`) and the avcC reserved bits are zeroed (byte[4]=0x03 instead of 0xFF, byte[5]=0x01 instead of 0xE1). mediabunny (export) and mp4box (import) carry this `description` verbatim into/out of the MP4 `avcC` box, so the files play in Chromium (which recovers via the correct in-band SPS/PPS before each keyframe) but fail in ffmpeg, Safari/QuickTime, and Firefox with `sps_id out of range` / too-many-reference-frames. New `sanitizeAvcDescription(description)` strips the duplicated parameter-set header bytes, recomputes the length fields, and restores the reserved bits. It is gated on the non-compliant reserved bits, so any correctly-serialized description (Chrome/Firefox/Safari, and the theoretical valid PPS whose first RBSP byte is legitimately 0x68) is left byte-for-byte untouched; unrepairable forms (Annex-B description, truncated/garbage) are warned about but not altered. `MediabunnyExporter` repairs the encoder description on export, and `CVideoMp4Data` repairs the `avcC` on import so already-broken files also decode in strict browsers. Covered by `tests/H264Utils.test.js` (10 cases, including the exact broken bytes from a reported export).
- **Starlink tool — stale-TLE phantom orbits no longer manufacture bogus flares** (`tools/starlink/flareEngine.js`): a months-old TLE propagated far forward flings satellites to absurd altitudes that otherwise read as sunlit and generate spurious flares. A LEO altitude sanity band now rejects those out-of-band orbits. Separately, the deep-night productive band was lowered from −40° to −56° (horizon flares persist through most of the night, not just twilight), and a fetch/run race was fixed so a just-loaded TLE applies to the very next search instead of one run late.

## Version 2.66.0 (2026-05-29)

### New Features
- **Fixed Altitude orbit mode** (Export → Orbit Image Set): The Orbit Image Set exporter (`src/ExportImageSet.js`) gains an **Orbit Mode** dropdown (`CNodeGUIValue` with options `{"Fixed Distance": "distance", "Fixed Altitude": "altitude"}`). *Fixed Distance* is the prior behavior — a constant slant range to the target, so the camera's altitude rises with elevation. *Fixed Altitude* (new) holds the camera at a constant geodetic altitude (HAE) above sea level and solves, per shot, how far out along each az/el direction the camera must sit to reach that altitude. The solve is `solveDistanceForHAE(target, dir, altMeters)`, a doubling-bracket + bisection root-find; it is well-posed because moving the camera away from the target along an ECEF direction monotonically increases geocentric radius, so it converges even at near-horizontal elevations. Altitude mode adds a **Use Current Camera Altitude** checkbox and an **Orbit Altitude** slider (new `imageSetOrbitAltitude` `CNodeGUIValue` node, small ft/m units, `getValueFrame(0)` returns meters HAE). `_resolveFixedAltitude(camera)` returns either the look camera's current HAE (checkbox on) or the slider value (checkbox off). `_updateOrbitModeVisibility()` toggles the distance-pair vs altitude-pair controls based on the selected mode and the relevant "Use Current" checkbox. The preview path re-solves distance live so dragging the Orbit Altitude slider updates the preview immediately (the Orbit Mode `onChange` re-enters an active preview so mode/validation changes apply at once). The export path solves distance per shot; if a time-stepped target rises above the chosen altitude on some shots it reuses the last valid distance and emits a `console.warn` with `altitudeFallbackCount`. Both paths validate that the requested altitude is above the target's own altitude, otherwise they `alert()` (showing the target's approximate HAE) and bail.

- **Starlink Flare Predictor** (standalone tool, `tools/starlink/`, linked from `tools/index.html`): A new self-contained, mobile-friendly browser tool — NOT part of the main Sitrec webpack bundle — that predicts Starlink "horizon flare" times and sky directions for a fixed location or along a flight. It reuses Sitrec's nadir-panel mirror-reflection flare physics (the `CSatellite`/`CNodeDisplayNightSky` model), runs SGP4 via a vendored `satellite.js`, and carries its own Sun/star astronomy. Forward search ("next flares from here") uses a session-stepped twilight scan; flight mode scans the great-circle route at cruise altitude. The results screen gives a FLARES VISIBLE / No Flares verdict, a one-sentence summary (local + UTC times, start/end direction), a compass rose, and a labelled horizon view. Inputs accept airport IATA/ICAO/name (bundled OpenFlights list) or any place via OpenStreetMap Nominatim; live Starlink TLEs come from `sitrecServer/proxy.php?request=CURRENT_STARLINK` with a Celestrak fallback. Build-timestamp cache-busting stamps `index.html` via `webpackCopyPatterns`. The tool as shipped in 2.66.0 also includes the geolocation, simulated-fallback, and compass-sprinkle behaviors below.

### Improvements
- **Starlink tool — blank Origin uses browser geolocation** (`tools/starlink/`): Leaving the Origin field blank now calls `navigator.geolocation.getCurrentPosition`, reverse-geocodes the fix to a place name via Nominatim (`reverseGeocode` in `location.js`, returning a `{lat, lon, altKm:0, name, source:"geolocation"}` origin in `app.js`), populates the Origin field and proceeds. New help text "Leave blank to use your current location." replaces the old "enter an origin" form-validation block.
- **Starlink tool — out-of-range dates fall back to simulated results** (`tools/starlink/`): TLEs are only accurate within roughly a week of now. If the requested moment is more than a week from `Date.now()`, the tool falls back to today's date (keeping the requested time-of-day) and shows an orange banner — "Simulated results, out of date range — using current satellite data." (`.sim-note`) — on both the FLARES VISIBLE and No Flares results screens.
- **Starlink tool — animated compass sprinkle** (`tools/starlink/skyview.js`): The compass-rose SVG gains an animated sprinkle of ~16 small white flare dots (`flareDots`) in the angular wedge between the direction arrows, just beyond the rim, twinkling (opacity + size) and drifting over a 60 s SMIL loop. The SVG viewBox is expanded upward to make room.
- **Starlink tool — cleaner results page** (`tools/starlink/app.js`): The per-flare "All N flares · scanned M satellites" `<details>` list is now gated behind a `SHOW_FLARE_LIST = false` flag (hidden) for a less cluttered results screen. New `.sim-note` CSS style added.

### Bug Fixes
- **Fixed "Save Sitch As" aborting with an InvalidStateError when capturing the thumbnail** (`src/CFileManager.js`): `captureViewportScreenshot()` composites all effectively-visible views with `drawImage`, which throws `InvalidStateError` ("The image argument is a canvas element with a width or height of 0") when a source canvas has zero width or height — this can happen for a view not yet laid out, e.g. a freshly-created overlay view. The base-view loop now requires `view.canvas.width > 0 && view.canvas.height > 0` before drawing, the overlay loop skips any 0-sized canvas, and `targetHeight` is clamped with `Math.max(1, ...)` so an extreme aspect ratio can't yield a 0-height thumbnail canvas. Save no longer fails.

## Version 2.65.0 (2026-05-28)

### New Features
- **Global video filename overlay** (Settings → *Show Filename*, default on): a new bottom-center HTML overlay (`<div id="sitrec-filename">`) shows the currently-loaded video's filename centered along the bottom of the page, as a sibling to the existing bottom-right attribution overlay in `src/AttributionOverlay.js`. A new helper `getDisplayFilename(source)` in `src/FilenameUtils.js` does the cleanup: it `String`-coerces and trims the input, tries `new URL(value, window.location.href)` and uses `url.pathname` (falling back to stripping `?` and `#` for non-URL strings), normalizes backslashes to forward slashes, takes the last non-empty path segment, and `decodeURIComponent`s it (returning the raw segment if decode throws). Returns `""` on empty input. The overlay module gains module-level `filenameDiv` / `currentFilename` state, a `getBottomOffsetPx()` helper extracted from the existing banner-aware attribution offset so both overlays sit at the same `BANNER_HEIGHT + 2` px above the bottom, a `createFilenameOverlay()` that styles the div (`position: fixed`, `bottom: getBottomOffsetPx()`, `left: 50%`, `transform: translateX(-50%)`, `max-width: 60vw`, semi-transparent black background, 10px sans-serif white text, single-line with ellipsis, `pointer-events: none`, `z-index: 10000`), a `renderFilename()` that hides the div when `Globals.settings?.showFilename` is falsy or `currentFilename` is empty, and exports `setFilenameOverlaySource(source)` (runs `getDisplayFilename` and re-renders) and `updateFilenameOverlay()` (re-render only, for settings-change wiring). `render()` now calls `renderFilename()` so attribution updates trigger a filename re-render, and `disposeAttributionOverlay()` removes the new div and clears `filenameDiv` + `currentFilename`. The overlay is also baked into exported videos: `drawAttributionOnCanvas` is restructured so the previous "early return if attribution text is empty" no longer suppresses the filename — the function now draws the filename (`textAlign: "center"` at `canvasWidth / 2`, only when `Globals.settings?.showFilename && currentFilename`) and the attribution (`textAlign: "right"` at `canvasWidth - 4`, only when text is present) as independent passes, so either, both, or neither can appear in a rendered viewport video. The Settings folder builder in `CCustomManager.setupSettingsFolder` (`src/CustomSupport.js`) gains a `Globals.settings.showFilename` checkbox (label/tooltip from `custom.settings.showFilename`); its `onChange` coerces to boolean, calls `this.saveGlobalSettings(true)`, and invokes `updateFilenameOverlay()` so the overlay reflects the toggle immediately; the folder builder also calls `updateFilenameOverlay()` once at construction so an existing filename appears when the menu is built. `sanitizeSettings` accepts a `showFilename` boolean and the default settings object in `initializeSettings()` includes `showFilename: true` (`src/SettingsManager.js`). `CNodeVideoView` (`src/nodes/CNodeVideoView.js`) imports `setFilenameOverlaySource` and pushes the current filename into the overlay at every entry point that sets `this.fileName`: `videoImportStarted` in the import path, `loadedCallback` (`this.fileName ?? videoData?.filename`), the video-switch path after `this.fileName = entry.fileName` (`?? vd?.filename`), and `makeImageVideo(filename, …)`. New i18n string `custom.settings.showFilename` (*Show Filename* / tooltip "Show the current video filename centered at the bottom of the viewport and exported videos") in `src/i18n/en.js`.
- **Per-view Video Info → Filename** (per video view, Video Info folder → *Filename*, default off): `CNodeVideoInfoUI` (`src/nodes/CNodeVideoInfoUI.js`) gains a draggable, serialized *Filename* entry that lives alongside the existing frame counter / timecode / date-time items. New instance fields `this.showFilename` (default `false`), `this.filenameX`, `this.filenameY` (both `DEFAULT_X` / `DEFAULT_Y`) are added via `addSimpleSerial` so they round-trip through save/load. A new method `getVideoFilename()` returns `getDisplayFilename(videoView?.fileName ?? videoView?.videoData?.filename)`. The new `'filename'` id is registered with `hasAnyInfoItem`, `getAllItemIds`, `getShowProp` (mapped to `showFilename`), `getElementPos` (mapped to `['filenameX', 'filenameY']`), and `addBbox` (with backing `_filenameBbox`), so the entry participates in the existing collision-avoidance auto-positioning, drag-to-move, and bbox tracking the same way the other items do. The render loop draws it via `drawTextWithBg(this.getVideoFilename(), this.filenameX, this.filenameY)` when `this.showFilename` is true and the filename is non-empty. The GUI adds `folder.add(this, "showFilename")` with `positionItemToAvoidOverlaps('filename')` on enable. This is independent of the global overlay toggle and is intended for per-sitch in-viewport labeling. New i18n string `videoInfo.filename` (*Filename* / tooltip "Show the current video filename").
- **`getDisplayFilename` filename normalization helper** (`src/FilenameUtils.js`): centralizes the URL / path / percent-encoded filename → display-name logic used by both overlays. Unit-tested in `tests/FilenameUtils.test.js` with two cases — `"https://example.com/video/My%20Clip%201.mp4?token=abc"` → `"My Clip 1.mp4"` (URL with percent-encoded spaces and query string) and `"/Users/example/Videos/PR055-5Pct.mp4"` → `"PR055-5Pct.mp4"` (plain local path).

## Version 2.64.0 (2026-05-28)

### New Features
- **Unique frames only — video export** (Video → Render Video → *Unique frames only* + *Unique threshold*): video export gains a pre-export duplicate-frame scan that excludes near-identical consecutive source frames from the encoded output while keeping the original/selected frame rate, so e.g. a 30 fps re-encode of a true 15 fps source produces a shorter video at 30 fps rather than a duplicated one. New manager state in `VideoExporter.VideoExportManager` (`uniqueFramesOnly` default off, `uniqueFrameMeanAbsDiffThreshold` default `DEFAULT_UNIQUE_FRAME_MEAN_ABS_DIFF_THRESHOLD = 1.0`, 0–5 step 0.05) drives a new `buildDuplicateFrameSetForExport(videoData, startFrame, endFrame)` that shows an `ExportProgressWidget` ("Scanning duplicate video frames...") and delegates to `scanDuplicateVideoFrames(videoData, startFrame, endFrame, progress, {meanAbsDiffThreshold})`, which in turn calls `scanDuplicateFramesForVideoExport(startFrame, endFrame, progress, expectedVideoData, options)` in `CMotionAnalysisUI.js`. That helper reuses the existing motion-analyzer duplicate detection: it sets `Globals.justVideoAnalysis = true` and pauses playback, resets motion-analysis derived state if `videoId`/`Sit.aFrame`/`Sit.bFrame` changed since the last analyzer run, ensures `motionAnalyzer.params.skipDuplicateFrames = true`, runs `motionAnalyzer.buildDuplicateFrameMap(...)` (skipped if `hasDuplicateFrameMapForRange` reports a cached map already covers the range), then walks `startFrame+1..endFrame` collecting frames where `duplicateInfo.isDuplicate` OR `Number.isFinite(meanAbsDiffThreshold) && duplicateInfo.meanAbsDiff <= meanAbsDiffThreshold`. `duplicateFrameSet.delete(startFrame)` always keeps the very first frame in the range, even if it happens to duplicate the frame immediately before A. All saved state (`par.paused`, `par.frame`, `Globals.justVideoAnalysis`) is restored in `finally` and `setRenderOne(true)` re-kicks rendering. If the analyzer's primary `videoData` differs from the export's target, the helper logs a `console.warn` and proceeds with the analyzer's primary view rather than re-binding. `createVideoExportFramePlan` gains a `duplicateFrameSet` argument: it now builds `unfilteredSourceFrames` first via `buildBaseFrameSequence`, then produces `sourceFrames = filterDuplicateFrames(unfilteredSourceFrames, duplicateFrameSet)`, and exposes `unfilteredSourceFrames`, `totalUnfilteredSourceFrames`, and `skippedDuplicateFrames` on the plan. `totalFrames` short-circuits to 0 on an empty filtered list and `frameAt(index)` returns `startFrame` defensively in that case. `getVideoExportSpeedInfo` appends `"N duplicate frames skipped"` to the speed suffix when `skippedDuplicateFrames > 0`. All three export entry points scan before plan construction and `alert("...no unique frames found in the A-B range.")` if the filtered plan is empty: `VideoExportManager.exportSourceVideo()` (Render Source Video), `VideoExportManager.exportVideo()` (Render Viewport Video, including the displayStream-based path which also calls `displayStream.getTracks().forEach(t => t.stop())` before bailing), and `CNodeView3D.exportVideo()` (per-view single-view path), which now imports `findFirstVideoData` and `scanDuplicateVideoFrames` from `VideoExporter` and runs its own progress widget. The single-view export call passes `uniqueFramesOnly` / `uniqueFrameMeanAbsDiffThreshold` through `view.exportVideo(format, audio, wait, {loops, uniqueFramesOnly, uniqueFrameMeanAbsDiffThreshold})`. Audio gating across all four call sites now also requires `plan.skippedDuplicateFrames === 0` (since a shorter video desyncs from the original audio), and the "Audio export skipped" log line is updated to mention "unique-frame export" as a reason. New i18n strings under `videoExport`: `uniqueFramesOnly` (label *Unique frames only*, tooltip describing the scan-and-skip behavior) and `uniqueFrameThreshold` (label *Unique threshold*, tooltip explaining mean-grayscale-difference semantics and tuning direction for recompressed vs. subtle-motion footage). Two lower-level helpers are exported for reuse and testing: `compareGraySamplesForDuplicate(grayA, grayB)` returns `{isDuplicate, identicalRatio, meanAbsDiff}` against module-level `DUPLICATE_IDENTICAL_RATIO = 0.93` and `DUPLICATE_MEAN_ABS_DIFF = 0.15` (length mismatch or empty input returns `isDuplicate=false`), and `findFirstVideoData(NodeMan)` walks `Object.values(NodeMan.list)` returning the first `node.videoData`. Regression coverage in `tests/VideoExporter.test.js` adds *"filters duplicate source frames without changing fps"* (verifies `duplicateFrameSet: new Set([2, 4])` against `startFrame:0, endFrame:5, sourceFps:30` yields `sourceFrames=[0,1,3,5]`, `fps=30`, `totalFrames=4`, `skippedDuplicateFrames=2`) and a new `compareGraySamplesForDuplicate` describe block with identical and visibly-different Uint8Array cases.

## Version 2.63.0 (2026-05-28)

### New Features
- **Annotate overlay on video** (Video → Annotate): new `CNodeAnnotateOverlay` provides a drawing surface composited on top of the video view, auto-created on any custom sitch with a video. *Show Annotations* is the master switch; *Edit Mode* reveals a toolbar (select, pencil, brush, line, arrow, rectangle, ellipse, text, image drop, eraser — hotkeys S/P/B/L/A/R/E/T/I/X), captures the mouse, and suppresses video pan via `_isAnnotateEditing()`. Selection supports corner handles for rect/ellipse/image, endpoint handles for line/arrow, and live color/width edits. Strokes are stored in original-video pixel coordinates so they follow zoom, pan, resize, and reload (`modSerialize`/`modDeserialize`). *Fade Frames* makes strokes vanish N frames after creation (0 = persistent). Exports respect annotations: single-frame PNG/JPG composites the overlay canvas, *Render Source Video* (in `VideoExporter`) composites strokes onto the source canvas at original-video resolution honoring zoom/pan, and *Render Viewport Video* picks them up via the normal view iteration. Created from `CustomManagerSetup.js` rather than `SitCustom.js` so older saves get the overlay on reload.
- **Lighting Preset dropdown** (Lighting menu): a *Lighting Preset* dropdown sits above the six light sliders in `CNodeLighting`. *Default* snapshots each sitch's construction-time values for those sliders, the master shadows toggle, and the lookView atmosphere flag. *Shadows* applies a fixed set (0.07, 0.8, 1.02, 0, 1, 0.22) with shadows on and atmosphere off, tuned for shadow rendering. The chosen preset label is serialized so a saved sitch remembers the user's last pick. Orbit Image Set (`ExportImageSet.js`) gained a mirror of the same dropdown, attached lazily via `folder.onOpenClose` because `Sit.setup()` (which builds the lighting node) runs after `FileManager.sitchChanged()` on initial load.
- **Atmosphere relocated to Lighting** (Lighting → Atmosphere Tweaks): atmosphere controls move out of the Effects menu into a new *Atmosphere Tweaks* subfolder under Lighting, with the master *Atmosphere* checkbox sitting at lighting-level alongside *Shadows* / *Shadow tweaks*. The preset machinery flips the per-view `lookView.atmosphereEnabled` via `ViewMan` (`CNodeView3D.js`).
- **Orbit Image Set — AZ Start and single-shot sweeps** (Export → Orbit Image Set): new *AZ Start* slider (default 0, 0–355, step 5) shifts the azimuth sweep clockwise from a chosen starting heading. Setting *AZ Step* to 0 produces a single shot per elevation at *AZ Start*; setting *EL Step* to 0 produces a single elevation at *EL Start* (and skips the 90° cap row). The shot builder normalizes *AZ Start* with a double-mod-and-add so out-of-range values wrap cleanly.
- **On-screen histogram option** (Video → Effects → *Histogram On-Screen*): new `CNodeGUIFlag` `videoHistogramOnScreen` (default off) limits histogram sampling to the pixels currently visible in the video view rather than the full source frame. `CNodeVideoHistogramView.getHistogramSourceRect()` maps the view's `dx/dy/dWidth/dHeight` back to source-pixel coordinates and `drawSample()` now takes that sub-rect as input.

### Improvements
- **Subfolder open/closed state round-trips through save/load**: `MenuBar.modSerialize` in `lil-gui-extras.js` now walks `gui.folders` recursively, capturing each subfolder's `_closed` flag keyed by `$title.innerHTML`; `modDeserialize` reapplies the map. Top-level docked menus still always close on load — only nested folder state round-trips. Folders without a matching saved entry keep their default state, and saved entries that don't match any current folder are silently dropped, so adding/renaming/removing folders never breaks loading.
- **Global menu items survive custom sitch loads**: `loginServer` (file.savingDisabled), the local-folder status row, *Add Object*, *Export Debug Log*, and the HUD Color picker now have `.perm()` applied so they persist through the lil-gui teardown that happens when a custom sitch loads (`CFileManager.js`, `index.js`, `HUDColor.js`).
- **Faster tonal adjustments**: `CNodeVideoViewFilters.applyShadowHighlight` / `applyDehaze` now use dedicated tight per-pixel loops (`applyTonalRegionLoop`, `applyShadowHighlightRegionLoop`, and float-output variants for the shadow→highlight→dehaze pipeline). The new helpers hoist slider-dependent values out of the loop, share a single luma calculation across the shadow and highlight passes, and use module-level constants (`TONAL_REGION_WIDTH`, `TONAL_REGION_INV_WIDTH`, `TONAL_LUMA_R/G/B`, `TONAL_ENDPOINT_PI`). The `edgeDetect` kernel hoists the `kernelName === 'edgeDetect'` check out of the inner pixel loop too. Behavior is unchanged (covered by a new `tests/nodes/CNodeVideoViewFilters.test.js`); just noticeably faster when scrubbing with shadows / highlights / dehaze active.

The `ImageSetExporter` instance is preserved across reloads so user-set fields (`trackToOrbit`, `azStep`, `verticalFOV`, …) persist, and the `filesParsed` listener is registered only once to avoid handler leaks. URL-driven sitch loads were unaffected (teardown hadn't run yet).

## Version 2.62.4 (2026-05-27)

### Bug Fixes
- **Terrain flicker / mass low-Z drop during rapid camera motion** (`src/QuadTreeMap.js`, `src/QuadTreeMapTexture.js`, `src/QuadTreeTile.js`). Under a fast pan/rotate (e.g. a ~45° rotational sweep) the rendered texture cut would briefly collapse: 60+ z14 leaf tiles vanished for a single frame and the eager z1/z2/z3 globe imagery showed through, producing the visible "drops to a very low Z for a frame" flicker. Root cause was in `describeDescendantCutForView`: when reconcile recursed into a forced subtree (`forcedVisibleByRendering` / `forceFullSiblingCheck`), it walked the whole forced subtree with `camera=null` and any single empty/inactive cache leaf cascaded `renderedCovered=false` / `readyCovered=false` back up to a shallow ancestor (z9/z10/z11). `reconcileRenderedTileCut`'s partial-fallback block then suppressed the entire descendant branch for one frame. The fix changes cover semantics inside a forced subtree: a child visited only because of force trusts the force signal — cover is now evaluated against `anyRendering`/`anyReady` for that subtree rather than the strict `renderedCovered`/`readyCovered`, so empty cache siblings inside a known-rendering subtree no longer veto cover. `describeDescendantCutForView` also now returns `anyRendering` alongside `anyReady`, and reconcile uses it to suppress overlapping render branches on partial-cover paths. Supporting changes in the same diff: (1) `applyParentDataFallback` in `QuadTreeMapTexture.js` (the new shared parent-data helper extracted from the old inline subdivide path) refuses to downgrade a tile that already has its own loaded high-res non-wireframe material (`!tile.usingParentData && tile.mesh.getMap()`) — surgical reactivation passes `useParentData=true` based on the *parent's* state, so an existing-tile reactivation could otherwise stomp a freshly-installed high-res child material with the parent's downsampled material (seen as a brown/khaki rectangle flickering over an otherwise-sharp area). It also refuses tiles flagged `isDeadBranch=true` (set when a `'PlaceholderTile'` error is caught in `triggerLazyLoadIfNeeded` — Esri has no imagery for that footprint), so dead leaves aren't resurrected into another load-fail cycle. (2) `QuadTreeTile.applyMaterial` now clears `this.usingParentData = false` synchronously the moment the high-res material is assigned, closing a microtask race where the `.then(() => usingParentData = false)` in `triggerLazyLoadIfNeeded` ran a tick later and let a surgical reactivation land on a stale `usingParentData=true` and stomp the fresh material. (3) New `updateMergeCameraStability` in `QuadTreeMap.js` replaces the previous scalar-sum camera fingerprint (which aliased smooth pans as "stable" — a `(+dx, -dy, 0)` translation preserves the sum, and the rotation diagonal moves by only `~1 + 2cosθ` for small θ) with element-wise compare across rotation rows 0/1/2 of `matrixWorld`, translation, fov, and zoom. Visible merges (parent reclaims a ready child cut) are now gated behind `MERGE_CAMERA_STABLE_FRAMES = 12` frames of true stability, so the merge step can't fire mid-pan and flash a coarse parent tile. (4) `reconcileRenderedTileCut`'s partial-fallback branch no longer activates an inactive parent — it only unsuppresses an already-active parent — so reconcile can no longer undo PASS 2's camera-aware deactivation. (5) `subdivideTilesViewSpecific`'s surgical reactivation now calls `calculateTileVisibility` with the real view predicate (was `coverageSphereOnly`) and threads `useParentData=true` through `activateTile` so a child entering visibility shows instantly with the parent's downsampled texture rather than wireframe. (6) The `tile.z < 3` root-tile branch in subdivision no longer forces `visible=true` — that override was pinning every z2 globe tile into narrow look views and overdrawing the ready deep cut. Regression coverage: `tests/QuadTreeMapReconcile.test.js` gains nine new cases (force-visited empty wing siblings, coverage-invisible full rendered cover, view-mode-only parent reconcile, ready-covered inactive parent reveals suppressed children, view-ready cover not vetoed by coverage-only siblings, preload-margin children don't force fallback, surgical reactivation passes `useParentData`, merges wait for camera stability, `activateTile` applies parent-data fallback when reactivating, and a top-level "reconcile never activates an inactive parent" guard), and one prior test that encoded the old "suppress rendering descendants under coarse parent" behavior is rewritten as the new force-visited-empty-siblings case. All 48 jest tests pass; an MCP-driven 45° rotational sweep that previously dropped 13–14 z14 batches per sweep now drops zero.

## Version 2.62.3 (2026-05-27)

### New Features
- **Sun Reflection slider on synthetic clouds** (Objects → *Clouds: \<name\>* → Properties): a new `sunReflection` slider is added to `CNodeSynthClouds` (`src/nodes/CNodeSynthClouds.js`), range 0–10000 in steps of 1 (meters), default 0 (no-op). The control sits in the Properties subfolder alongside Density/Opacity/Brightness, uses the new `synthClouds.sunReflection.label` i18n key (`src/i18n/en.js`), and persists via `serialize()` / `static deserialize()`. Implementation adds two `ShaderMaterial` uniforms — `reflectionPoint` (vec3) and `reflectionRadius` (float) — and a per-frame `preRender(view)` update. When `sunReflection > 0`, `Globals.sunLight` exists, and `this.localUp` is set, `preRender` looks up `NodeMan.get("lookCamera", false)` and computes the specular reflection point on the locally flat cloud plane through `this.group.position` with normal `localUp`: it mirrors the lookCamera position across that plane (`camMirror = camPos − planeNormal · 2h`, where `h = (camPos − planePoint) · planeNormal`), then traces a ray from `camMirror` in the already-normalized `sunDirection` until it intersects the plane (`t = −((camMirror − planePoint) · planeNormal) / (sunDir · planeNormal)`), and writes the resulting world-space point into `reflectionPoint`. If `sunDir · planeNormal ≤ 0.001` (sun at or below the cloud horizon), the effective radius is left at 0 so the shader noops. The fragment shader now computes `planeNormal = normalize(reflectionPoint − earthCenter)`, projects `vWorldPosition − reflectionPoint` onto the plane, takes its length `pdist`, and multiplies the diffuse-lit color (`texColor * color * lighting`, BEFORE `emissive` is added) by `1 + max(0, 1 − pdist / reflectionRadius)` — so brightness is +100% at the exact reflection point and decays linearly to +0% at `reflectionRadius`. The reflection point intentionally tracks the *look* camera only (not `view.camera`), so the glint stays anchored to what the look view is pointing at even when the same cloud layer is observed from `mainView`.

### Improvements
- **URL drag/drop and paste on the sitch browser** (`src/CSitchBrowser.js`, `src/DragDropHandler.js`): the sitch browser's overlay drop zone, previously file-only, now also accepts URLs. The drop-hint label changes from *Drop files to create a new sitch* to *Drop files or URLs to create a new sitch*. The internal/external drag filter is widened from `dataTransfer.types.includes("Files")` to a new `hasExternalDropData` helper that also matches `"text/uri-list"` and `"text/plain"`, applied to `dragenter`/`dragover`/`drop`. When the drop carries no files, the handler falls back to `DragDropHandler.getDroppedText(dataTransfer)` (extracts the first non-comment line of `text/uri-list`, falling back to `text/plain`, trimmed) and pushes the URL onto a new `DragDropHandler.pendingDropTexts` queue, parallel to the existing `pendingDropFiles` queue. The custom-sitch load is now shared via `_loadCustomSitchForQueuedDrops(queuedCount)`, called whenever at least one file *or* one URL was queued. `DragDropHandler.handleDrop` (the post-load processor) drains `pendingDropTexts` after `pendingDropFiles`, dispatching each via a new `handleDroppedText(text)` method. `handleDroppedText` consolidates the `http://`/`https://` discriminator that the old `else` branch of `onDrop` did inline: URLs go to `uploadURL(text, {persistDrop: true})`, anything else goes to `uploadText(text)`. The search box (`si` in `addSearchInput`) also gains a `paste` listener: pasted text starting with `http://` or `https://` is intercepted (preventDefault + stopPropagation), pushed onto `pendingDropTexts`, and triggers the same `_loadCustomSitchForQueuedDrops(1)` flow so a pasted URL behaves identically to a dragged one.
- **War.gov PR-coded Metabunk URLs resolve without fetching the thread** (`src/MetabunkThreadUtils.js`): `resolveMetabunkThreadVideoURL` now extracts a `PR-NNN` War.gov release code from the *thread URL itself* via `extractWarGovPRCode(threadURL)` before any HTTP traffic. If a code is found, it calls `getWarGovUFODvidsIdForPrCode(prCode, fetchImpl)` against the bundled `data/WARGOV/uap-data.csv` / `uap-release001.csv` index; on a hit it routes straight to `resolveDvidsVideoURL("https://www.dvidshub.net/video/<id>", fetchImpl)`, skipping the Metabunk thread fetch entirely. Failures in that fast path are swallowed and the function falls through to the existing thread-HTML scrape, so this is a pure optimization. Covered by a new `MetabunkThreadUtils.test.js` case ("resolves PR code from the thread URL before fetching Metabunk HTML") that asserts the thread URL is never fetched when the PR code resolves, using the `dow-uap-pr072-…14909` example URL.

## Version 2.62.2 (2026-05-27)

### Bug Fixes
- Fixed a double-unescape edge case in `decodeHTMLEntities` in `src/DVIDSUtils.js` and `src/MetabunkThreadUtils.js`. The previous sequential `.replace()` chain decoded `&amp;` first, so an already-encoded payload like `&amp;lt;` collapsed to `<` instead of `&lt;` because the substituted `&` was reconsidered as the start of the next entity. Rewrote both as a single-pass `String.replace` over `/&(amp|quot|#39|lt|gt);/g` backed by a `HTML_ENTITY_MAP` lookup, so each character is visited once and double-encoded input round-trips correctly. The existing 12 tests in `DVIDSUtils.test.js` and `MetabunkThreadUtils.test.js` still pass. Closes CodeQL alerts #48 and #49 (`js/double-escaping`).

### Security
- Hardened the Metabunk host check in `isIgnoredMetabunkMP4URL` (`src/MetabunkThreadUtils.js`). The previous `parsed.hostname.endsWith("metabunk.org")` test would also match attacker-controlled lookalike hostnames such as `evilmetabunk.org`; the check now requires either an exact host match or a true `.metabunk.org` subdomain before the `/styles/` path filter is applied. Defensive hardening — no known exploit path through real upstream thread content. Closes CodeQL alert #50 (`js/incomplete-url-substring-sanitization`). Alert #47 (`js/clear-text-storage-of-sensitive-data` for an API key stored in `localStorage` by `tools/airport-arrivals/index.html`) was dismissed as won't-fix: the standalone client-side tool stores the user's own ADS-B Exchange key with no backend, which is the canonical pattern.
- Upgraded `qs` to 6.15.2 in `package-lock.json` and `tools/SitrecBridge/package-lock.json` (transitive via `express` / `body-parser` and `webpack-dev-server → express@4`), closing Dependabot alerts #132 and #133 (DoS via `TypeError` in `qs.stringify` on `null`/`undefined` entries in comma-format arrays when `encodeValuesOnly` is set; medium severity). Pulled via `npm audit fix`.
- Upgraded `uuid` to 11.1.1 via a new `overrides: { "uuid": "^11.1.1" }` block in `package.json` (transitive via `sockjs → webpack-dev-server`), closing Dependabot alert #131 (missing buffer bounds check in v3/v5/v6 when a `buf` argument is supplied; medium severity). Our only caller is `sockjs` invoking `uuid.v4()` with no arguments, so the CVE is not reachable in practice, but the patched version ships anyway. The `npm audit fix` suggestion of downgrading `webpack-dev-server` 5.x to 1.16.5 was rejected. `npm audit` now reports 0 vulnerabilities in both lockfiles.
- Upgraded `tmp` to ≥ 0.2.6 in `apps/video-viewer/package-lock.json` (transitive via `electron-builder → app-builder-lib → @malept/flatpak-bundler → tmp-promise`), closing Dependabot alert #134 (path traversal via unsanitized `prefix`/`postfix`; high severity). Pulled via `npm audit fix`; `npm audit` now reports 0 vulnerabilities in the video-viewer lockfile.

## Version 2.62.1 (2026-05-27)

### Improvements
- **Render Source Video shortcut in Video Adjustments** (Video → Video Adjustments): a second `Render Source Video` button is added at the bottom of `addFiltersToVideoNode` in `src/nodes/CNodeVideoViewFilters.js`, bound to the same instance method as the existing button in Video → Video Render & Export — `CustomManager?.videoExportManager?.exportSourceVideo()`. Both buttons share the `videoExport.renderSource.label` / `videoExport.renderSource.tooltip` i18n keys, so future changes to the source-render flow or its translations apply to both. The button is styled light-green via the project's canonical `Controller.prototype.setLabelColor("#90EE90")` extension (`src/lil-gui-extras.js`), which injects a per-controller `<style>` block with `!important` rules — the only reliable way to override lil-gui's per-element `color: var(--text-color)` on a `<button>` (earlier inline `domElement.style.backgroundColor` / `style.color` writes silently lost to lil-gui's own CSS). A companion fix in the same change makes the green styling survive controller mirroring: `setLabelColor` now records `this._labelColor = color` after injecting its style block, and `mirrorController` in `src/CustomManagerMirror.js` replays `setLabelColor(controller._labelColor)` on the mirrored controller right after copying the tooltip. The standalone right-click Video Adjustments popup (and any other mirrored panel) now shows the same label colors as the source folder, which also restores colors that were silently dropping out of mirrored copies elsewhere in the codebase — the file-manager "Saving Disabled" warning, the PTZ angle indicators, the current-sub-sitch indicator, and any other `setLabelColor`-styled control.

### Bug Fixes
- **Blurry, overlapping, and z-fighting terrain tiles**: `QuadTreeMap.reconcileTextureCut` in `src/QuadTreeMap.js` is rewritten to maintain a single per-view rendered cut for texture tiles. The previous reconcile pass could reveal a deep ready branch and then have a shallower fallback parent suppress it again in the same pass, and partial descendants could render against a fallback parent — producing z-fighting and blurry fallback imagery, especially after zoom-in followed by zoom-out and after camera `goToPoint`. The new reconcile walks texture cuts top-down, marks fallback-owned branches for the pass, and tracks ready-vs-rendering tiles with `renderSuppressedLayers` on `QuadTreeMapTexture` so descendants can finish loading without drawing over fallback parents. Stale suppression is cleared when an active parent becomes a fallback again, merges only collapse immediate active children (not the deep subtree, which was over-flattening), and coverage-visible texture leaves are kept alive when strict OBB subdivision culling would otherwise reject them (`QuadTreeCullingBounds.js`). `CNodeCamera` now refreshes subdivision after `goToPoint` and fingerprints camera matrices after `matrixWorld` updates so the reconciler sees the post-move pose on the same tick. A new 276-line regression test `tests/QuadTreeMapReconcile.test.js` covers the reveal/suppress race, the merge-immediate-children rule, and the post-`goToPoint` refresh; the OBB helper import path is normalized for Jest/Webpack and Three is deduped via a `package.json` resolution so the test runs against the same Three instance as the app.

## Version 2.62.0 (2026-05-27)

### New Features
- **Orbit Image Set: Vertical FOV control** (File → Export → Orbit Image Set): added a `Use Current Camera FOV` checkbox (default on) and a `Vertical FOV (deg)` slider (range 0.1–120, default 30) in `src/ExportImageSet.js`. When the checkbox is off, the export locks the look camera's vertical FOV to the slider value once before the orbit loop (look-camera controllers are already disabled during export) and re-pins it inside `_applyPreviewCameraPose` so other nodes (match-video-aspect, fovOverride, etc.) can't nudge it mid-shot. Both `exportImageSet` and `exportImageSetFullscreen` honor the setting; the saved/restored `savedFov` snapshot is added to the existing snapshot/restore block.
- **Orbit Image Set: JPEG output** (File → Export → Orbit Image Set): new `Use PNGs` checkbox, default off. With it off, each shot is encoded as JPEG at quality 0.9 via the renamed `canvasToImageBlob` helper (formerly `canvasToPngBlob`); with it on, PNG is preserved. Filename extension switches with format (`.jpg` / `.png`). PNG encoding was the long tail of per-shot wall time; JPEG cuts encode time ~5–20× and file size ~10–15× at imperceptible loss on terrain/sky-dominated shots.
- **Orbit Image Set: Orbit Preview mode** (File → Export → Orbit Image Set): new `Orbit Preview` checkbox repurposes the main frame slider as an index into the precomputed orbit shot list (az_steps × el_steps × time_steps). `_enterPreview` snapshots camera pose/FOV, `Sit.frames`/`aFrame`/`bFrame`, `par.frame`, `Sit.startTime`, render hooks, controls, and the look-camera controllers (disables them like the export does); `_applyPreviewFrame` runs per tick via `Globals.orbitPreviewApply` (called from `updateFrame.js` after the slider sync) and moves the camera to the current shot's az/el at the current distance, shifting `GlobalDateTimeNode.startDate` at time-step boundaries. The frame slider tints green (`#1a5d2a` track, `#2ecc71` accent) to signal the mode. `preRenderFunction` re-applies the orbit pose just before each `lookView` render, fixing a two-position flicker when `fixedTarget` moved (CNodeCamera.update runs `altAdjust` and `applyGroundTrackSwitch` directly, bypassing the disabled controllers, between the per-tick update and the GL pipeline reading `camera.matrixWorld`). Orbit Distance and Vertical FOV update the preview live; `_buildShotList` is shared by preview and export so the geometry stays in lock-step. Clicking `Export Image Set` while preview is on auto-exits preview first so the export's own snapshot/restore captures a clean pre-export state. `_exitPreview` restores everything captured at enter time, including slider styling.
- **Video tonal adjustments: Shadows, Highlights, Dehaze** (Video → Video Adjustments): three new sliders in `src/nodes/CNodeVideoViewFilters.js`, range -100 to +100, default 0, with i18n keys `videoShadows`, `videoHighlights`, `videoDehaze`. Implemented as a per-pixel pass (`applyTonalAdjustmentsToImage` → `applyTonalAdjustmentToPixel`) inserted into `CNodeVideoView.getAdjustedVideoFrameSource` between Curves and Invert. Shadows lifts/crushes darker tones using a luma-based region weight centered at 0.1; Highlights does the same for brighter tones centered at 0.9; Dehaze adds a contrast-around-airlight (220) plus saturation pass when positive, or blends toward airlight with reduced saturation when negative. Result is cached per `(image, frame, shadows:highlights:dehaze)` key on `_tonalAdjustCanvas`. Reset button in Video Adjustments resets all three. The `applyByteInvertToImage` cache now also keys on a per-effect `sourceKey` so Invert correctly re-runs when the upstream chain changes.
- **Histogram tonal-loss readout** (Video → Video Adjustments → Histogram): the live RGB histogram view (`CNodeVideoHistogramView`) now overlays a tonal-resolution stats line — `Levels NN% | N.Nb | CXX | WX:1` — showing what fraction of distinct RGB input levels survive the current adjustment chain, the effective output bit depth, total collapsed inputs across RGB, and the worst many-to-one collapse for any output level. The text tints amber when any collapse is present. A transparent hover div over the readout exposes a tooltip explaining each value. Stats are computed in `calculateTonalLossStats` using per-channel `originalSeen`, `adjustedSeen`, and reverse-map bitmaps built during the histogram pass.
- **Lines of Sight: Current LOS toggle** (Show/Hide → Current LOS): new per-LOS-display checkbox (i18n key `showHiders.currentLOS`, tooltip "Show only the current frame's line of sight"). When on, `CNodeDisplayLOS` draws a single white `Line2` for just `par.frame`'s LOS into a dedicated `currentLOSGroup`, on top of the existing per-second LOS bundle. Endpoint math (including the clip-to-sea-level path for downward-pointing LOSes on large-tile sitches) is extracted into a shared `getLineEndpoints(f)` so `recalculate()` and `updateCurrentLOS(f)` share one implementation. `showCurrentLOS` is added to `simpleSerials` so the toggle survives serialization; a new `dispose()` cleans up the group, the `Line2`, and the `LineGeometry`.

### Improvements
- **Curves editor: easier to grab handles** (Video → Video Adjustments → Curves): point and curve hit radii in `CNodeVideoCurvesView` doubled — `HIT_RADIUS` 9 → 18 and `CURVE_HIT_RADIUS` 10 → 20 — so clicking near a control point or curve segment is far more forgiving without changing the visible curve.
- **View dragging: drag-off-top to close, any view commits its new position**: in `CNodeView.onViewDragEnd`, the early-return on `!this.dockable` is moved to AFTER the new position is committed via `setFromDiv(this.div)` and AFTER a top-edge close check — so any draggable view now persists its dragged position on release (previously only dockable views did), and dragging any view above `CLOSE_OFF_TOP_PX` (-5px) hides it via `setVisible(false)`.
- **Camera controls: symmetric vertical tilt clamp**: `CameraMapControls.rotateUp` in `src/js/CameraControls.js` now clamps the camera elevation symmetrically between -89° and +89° (constants `MIN_CAMERA_ELEVATION_DEGREES` / `MAX_CAMERA_ELEVATION_DEGREES`) by computing the target elevation, clamping it, and converting back to an angle delta. Replaces the old nadir-only guard, so the camera no longer pops past the zenith and the residual angle math no longer fires a tiny rotation when fully clamped.

### Bug Fixes
- **Histogram clip indicators on inverted video**: `CNodeVideoView.calculateClippingDistribution` now feeds the "original" comparison value through `getClipComparisonValue(value, invertActive)`, which mirrors via `255 - value` when the Invert filter is on. Previously the shadow/highlight clip masks compared the inverted output against the un-inverted source and reported spurious clipping.
- **Saved GUI flags loading as off**: `CNodeGUIFlag` now coerces incoming values through `normalizeGUIFlagValue` (true / 1 / "1" / "true" → on) on construction, on user change, and during `modDeserialize`, so flags persisted as numeric or string-truthy in saved sitches restore correctly across the many filters that use it.

## Version 2.61.2 (2026-05-26)
